The board is a **strict replica of the proven Nicla Sense ME sensor set** (BHI260AP + BMM150 + BMP390L + BME688 + dual MX25R flash + IS31FL3194 RGB + BQ25120A power) with the SGC deltas:
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:69:           ──► BHI260AP VDD/VDDIO + BMP390L + BME688 + BMM150 (Nicla cluster)
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:89:**Bus-map derivation (strict, per docs):** Zephyr `&i2c0` = P0.15/P0.16 = power-management bus ("Wire1" in Arduino naming) — gauge 0x36 (AD-029), LED 0x53, charger 0x6A. Zephyr `&i2c1` = P0.22/P0.23 = sensor bus ("Wire") — LDC1612 0x2A (ADDR=GND, DNP) + RV-3028 0x52 (DNP). BHI260AP is **SPI**, not I²C (app.overlay: `&spi2`, CS P0.31, 16 MHz, INT P0.14); BMP390/BMM150/BME688 are BHI260AP **sub-sensors on the BHI's M1 master port** (Nicla schematic — the task brief's "BMP390 I²C addr" does not apply; per the ABX00050 pinout, BMP390L rides BHI M1 with MCSB). Address map has no conflicts (AD-029 address table confirmed).
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:227:- **BMM150** (U4) + **BMP390L** (U3) + **BME688** (U6): sub-sensors on BHI260AP master port M1 (BMM150 SCK/SDI ← M1SCX/M1SDX; BMP390L via MCSB1; BME688 via MCSB2 per ABX00050 pinout). **Per-ball wiring = copy Nicla schematic verbatim at capture** — exact M1/M2/M3 pin assignment of the BHI cluster is a Nicla-internal net list; mark as "copy reference" in capture. BMP390L: 10-pin LGA (1 VDDIO, 2 SCK, 3 VSS, 4 SDI, 5 SDO, …, CSB; CSB→VDDIO selects I²C — here SPI to BHI).
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:228:- **BME688 populate-vs-DNP**: firmware never reads it → **OD-6** (footprint retained either way; Nicla parity = populate).

| C3 | **Module RESET_N = P0.18** (fixed) vs Nicla's BHI260AP RESET on P0.18 (app.overlay pulses it low at bring-up; hardware doc §2 "P0.18 → BQ25120 MR reset network") | BHI RESETN → **P0.13** (module pin 52), pull-up retained. | C4 | Nicla's VDDIO_EXT header rail (BQ LS/LDO, programmable 1.8–3.3 V per ABX00050 pinout) has **no consumer on P1** (no external header, no level translators) | LS/LDO unused: LSCTRL → GND (disabled), LS/LDO pin → 1 µF to GND (stability, §7 pin table), VINLS → SYS (per SLUSD08A §9.3: "If the output of the LDO is less than the programmed V(SYS) voltage, connect VINLS to SYS") | none |

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

# N1 = "boosted Nicla CLONE" — verified gap analysis (v2, corrected)

**JP 2026-11-04 (binding):** *"Nicla-boosted clone is a CLONE: all on Nicla shall be present or boosted.
The minimal risk is to recreate the identical board."* Plus: BME688 must be there (temperature planned).

**Method correction (JP's own instruction — "don't just trust what I said, compare it with the V-cycle
documentation").** v1 of this file listed BMM150/BME688 as open decisions. That was **wrong**: the
V-cycle doc `sgc_schematic_spec.md` §1 and §4.4 already mandate them as part of a *strict replica*.
The real problem is worse and simpler: **the netlist never implemented them.** Parity is now measured
against three sources, not opinions:

1. `reference/ABX00050-schematics.pdf` — official Arduino schematic, 7 sheets, **100 components** (census below)
2. `sgc_schematic_spec.md` v0.1 §1/§4 — the V-cycle requirement ("strict replica … BHI260AP + BMM150 + BMP390L + BME688 + dual MX25R flash + IS31FL3194 + BQ25120A")
3. `sgc_netlist.py` — what is actually on the board today (49 parts)

---

## 1. Official Nicla component census (extracted from the PDF, all 7 sheets)

**100 components:** C×32, R×41, U×14, J×6, D×3, L×1, Y×1, DL×1 (RGB LED), MD×1 (ANNA module), plus PB1 button.

| Sheet | Refs |
|---|---|
| 1 TOP | hierarchy only |
| 2 CONNECTORS | J1 J2 J3 J4 J5 J7, R19 R20 R22 R36 R37 R38 R39, C29 C30, PB1, D1 |
| 3 LEVEL SHIFTERS | U11 TXB0108, U12 NTS0304, U13 NTS0304, C23–C27, C31 C32, R14 R33 R40 R41 |
| 4 POWER | U9 BQ25120A, L1 2.2µH, D3 D4 D5 PMEG4005, C1 C10 C14 C15 C21 C22, R1 R2 R5 R15 R16 R17 R24 R25 R26 R27 |
| 5 USB | U1 SAMD11, U14 AP2112K-3.3, U13?? , C18 C19 C20 C28, R28 R30 R34 R35, J7 |
| 6 SENSORS | U5 BHI260AP, U3 BMP390L, U4 BMM150, U2 BME688, U6 MX25R1635F, C3–C13, R8 R18 R21 R23 R29 |
| 7 ANNAB112 | MD1 ANNA-B112, U7 MX25R1635F, U8 IS31FL3194, DL1 SMLP34RGB2W3, **Y1 SIT1532AI**, C2 C17, R6 R7 R9 R12 R31 R32 |

*(Note: the PDF's internal ref designators differ from the reader's labels — e.g. U2 = BME688 on sheet 6 but the Arduino page calls the flash "U2 BHI Flash". Use the sheet, not the legend, when capturing.)*

---

## 2. Parity table — Nicla function by function vs our netlist TODAY

Legend: ✅ present & equivalent · 🔵 **better (boosted)** · ❌ **MISSING** · ➖ deliberately not copied

| Nicla function | Nicla part | Ours | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCU module | ANNA-B112 (nRF52832, 64 KB) | ANNA-B402 (nRF52833, **128 KB**) | 🔵 |
| BHI260AP program flash | MX25R1635F (2 MB), QSPI | U2 MX25R1635F (2 MB) | ✅ |
| Data-logging flash | MX25R1635F (2 MB) | U7 MX25R6435F (**8 MB**) | 🔵 |
| Charger / PMIC | BQ25120A | U3 BQ25120A | ✅ |
| Fuel gauge | — (BQ band-gauge only) | U4 MAX17048 @0x36 | 🔵 |
| IMU | BHI260AP | U8 BHI260AP | ✅ |
| Pressure | BMP390L | U9 BMP390 | ✅ |
| **Magnetometer** | **BMM150 (U4, sheet 6)** | **— none —** | ❌ **MISSING** |
| **Environment (T/RH/gas)** | **BME688 (U2, sheet 6)** | **— none — (only BHI pad 18 MCSB2 is wired to NC)** | ❌ **MISSING** |
| RGB status LED | IS31FL3194 + SMLP34RGB2W3 | U5 + D1 (same parts) | ✅ |
| **32.768 kHz oscillator** | **Y1 SIT1532AI-J4-DCC-32.768E** | **— none —** (`32K_XL1` net has zero parts) | ❌ **MISSING** |
| Reverse-protection on VBUS | D3 PMEG4005EPK → BQ IN | — none — | ❌ MISSING |
| Reverse-protection on 5 V aux | D4/D5 PMEG4005 | — | ➖ (no ESLOV) |
| USB **connector** | J7 micro-USB ZX62-AB-5PA | J1 USB-C USB4085, 5.1 kΩ Rd | 🔵 |
| USB ESD | (in bridge circuit) | — none — | ❌ verify |
| **USB↔serial bridge** | **U1 SAMD11 + U14 AP2112K-3.3 + U13 NTS0304 + 100 nF×2 + 100 k×4** | **— none — (SWD header J3 only)** | ❌ MISSING |

| **10-pin expansion header** | J1 2×10 (JTAG_ANNA/JTAG_BHI/SPI1_EXT/I2C1_EXT/LPIO/ADC0/ADC1) | J3 2×5 SWD only | ⚠ partial |
| Aux 3-pin | J4 BM03B-ACHSS | J4 = LED strip (different) | ➖ |
| Level shifters (IO) | U11 TXB0108 + U12 NTS0304 | U11 TXS0102 (LED data only, DNP) | ⚠ partial |
| Arming input | PB1 pushbutton on board | J5 off-board Langir piezo | ➖ deliberate (JP) |
| Battery connector | J2 (VBAT/NTC/GND) | J2 JST-3 with NTC | ✅ |
| 5 V rail | — | MT3608 + L2 + D2 SS34 + TXS0102 + J4 strip | ➕ boosted |
| Proximity | — | LDC1612 (DNP) | ➕ |
| RTC | — | RV-3028-C7 (DNP, footprint) | ➕ |

---

## 3. What this means — and my recommendation

**JP's instinct is right, and the docs back it.** The V-cycle already demands a strict replica; the
netlist is simply behind the documentation. But "recreate the identical board" needs one important
qualification, because **three Nicla blocks must NOT be copied verbatim**:

1. **ANNA-B112 → B402 is forced.** nRF **P0.24 and P0.25 do not exist** on the B402 (Table 4 complete).
   Boost EN moves to P0.17, BQ CD to P0.08, and BHI RESETN to P0.13 because B402 pin 12 (RESET_N) is
   fixed on P0.18 — which Nicla uses for BHI reset. Already resolved in spec §3.3 (C1/C2/C3).
2. **Qi charging → USB-C** (Qi dropped v4.2).
3. **SAMD11 USB bridge — the one real judgement call.** It exists on Nicla to give USB programming +
   serial. We have SWD (J3) and a working BLE OTA path. Copying it costs ~5 ICs (SAMD11, AP2112K,
   NTS0304 ×2, TXB0108), a second 3.3 V rail, and 4 level-shift nets — and it serves *only*
   programming/console. **Recommendation: omit in rev A; reserve the footprint block for rev B if
   field-USB-service is ever required.** Everything else is cheap and should be closed now.

### Close now (all cheap, all pure parity, mostly zero new nRF pins)
| # | Item | Effort | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | **BMM150 magnetometer** | ~8 parts, **0 nRF pins** | rides the BHI260AP M-port (M3 I²C) — no MCU cost |
| G2 | **BME688 environment sensor** | ~6 parts, **0 nRF pins** | rides BHI M-port (MCSB2, pad 18 already reserved). **JP wants temperature** → populate, supersedes OD-6 "DNP" |
| G3 | **Y1 SIT1532AI 32.768 kHz + 100 nF** | 2 parts, **0 nRF pins** | XL1 driven, XL2 → GND. Net `32K_XL1` is currently dangling. **No stock KiCad footprint for the 1.5×0.8 mm 1508 CSP** — must draw it. |
| G4 | **D3 PMEG4005EPK** series diode VBUS → BQ IN | 1 part | Nicla parity + protects against 5 V-strip back-feed |
| G5 | **BME688 + BMM150 decoupling** | ~5 caps | per Nicla bypass bank (C5 1 µF, C6/C7/C12/C13 100 nF) |

Zero new nRF GPIO needed for G1–G3 — they sit on the BHI260AP's own master port and its XTAL input.
That is why closing them is nearly free and why omitting them was pure oversight, not a design choice.

### Keep as documented deltas (not gaps)
SAMD11 bridge, ESLOV J5, J1 2×10 header, PB1 button, Qi, micro-USB → all either deliberately dropped,
replaced by a better option, or subject to JP's call.

## 4. Corrected sheet structure (Arduino style, one function per page)

```
sgc_n1.kicad_sch              (root, hierarchical)
├── 01_top.kicad_sch           TOP — block diagram + rail index (no parts, like ABX00050 sheet 1)
├── 02_power.kicad_sch         BQ25120A + straps + PMID/VBAT/+1V8 + MAX17048 + D3 protection + NTC
├── 03_mcu.kicad_sch           ANNA-B402 + Y1 32k + decoupling + SWD + antenna counterpoise
├── 04_sensors.kicad_sch       BHI260AP + BMP390 + BMM150 + BME688 + LDC1612 + bypass bank
├── 05_storage.kicad_sch       U2 MX25R1635F (BHI QSPI) + U7 MX25R6435F (logging)
├── 06_boost_led.kicad_sch     MT3608 + L2 + D2 + TXS0102 + J4 strip + SK6812 reserve  ← today's page 2, as-is
└── 07_connectors.kicad_sch    USB-C + J3 SWD + J2 battery + J5 piezo + TPs
```

**Gate on every split:** `netdiff.py` must print **IDENTICAL MEMBERSHIP**. Any membership change = a
net broke; revert that step.

`Arduino_Nicla_Sense_ME_Tile`, plus Uno/Mega/MKR/Nano shield and socket footprints. It contains

```
sgc_n1.kicad_sch              (root, hierarchical)
├── 01_top.kicad_sch           TOP — block diagram + rail index (no parts, like ABX00050 sheet 1)
├── 02_power.kicad_sch         BQ25120A + straps + PMID/VBAT/+1V8 + MAX17048 + D3 protection + NTC
├── 03_mcu.kicad_sch           ANNA-B402 + Y1 32k + decoupling + SWD + antenna counterpoise
├── 04_sensors.kicad_sch       BHI260AP + BMP390 + BMM150 + BME688 + LDC1612 + bypass bank
├── 05_storage.kicad_sch       U2 MX25R1635F (BHI QSPI) + U7 MX25R6435F (logging)
├── 06_boost_led.kicad_sch     MT3608 + L2 + D2 + TXS0102 + J4 strip + SK6812 reserve  ← today's page 2, as-is
```

(+ `footprints\...\arduino-library.pretty`), v4.2.0, by Nicholas Parks Young, CC-BY-SA-4.0.

`Arduino_Nicla_Sense_ME_Tile`, plus Uno/Mega/MKR/Nano shield and socket footprints. It contains
**no component-level symbols**: no BHI260AP, no ANNA module, no BQ25120A, no BMM150/BME688.

our PCB) — the approach we dropped in v2.4. It cannot supply any part of the clone itself. All

2.3 Module reset
ANNA-B4 series is reset by applying a low level on the RESET_N input pin, which is normally set high
with an internal pull-up. A low logic level on this pin initiates an “external” or “hardware” reset of the
module. The prevailing parameter settings at the time of the reset are not saved in the non-volatile
memory of the module and a proper network detach is not performed.
--
    asynchronous serial interface (UART) and General layout guidelines.
•   System functions like RESET_N, I2C, GPIO, and other system input and output pins require an
    accurate design that can ensure that the voltage level is well defined during module boot.
•   Other pins also require an accurate design to ensure proper functionality.
•   Make sure not to exceed the electrical specification for any pin.
--
• UART (RX, TX)
• RESET_N
• SWITCH_1 and SWITCH_2

--
• Pressing the SW1 and SW2 buttons simultaneously during a module reset (initiated by setting
  RESET_N low). See also Module reset.

        using AT commands. The file download uses standard XMODEM-CRC16 protocol and 128 bytes
        packets.

3. **SAMD11 USB bridge — the one real judgement call.** It exists on Nicla to give USB programming +
   serial. We have SWD (J3) and a working BLE OTA path. Copying it costs ~5 ICs (SAMD11, AP2112K,
   NTS0304 ×2, TXB0108), a second 3.3 V rail, and 4 level-shift nets — and it serves *only*
   programming/console. **Recommendation: omit in rev A; reserve the footprint block for rev B if
   field-USB-service is ever required.** Everything else is cheap and should be closed now.
edits.newText:
3. **SAMD11 USB bridge — DECIDED (JP "OK!" 2026-11-04): OMIT in rev A, reserve the footprint block for
   rev B.** It exists on Nicla to give USB programming + serial. We have SWD (J3) and a working BLE OTA
   path. Copying it costs ~5 ICs (SAMD11, AP2112K-3.3, NTS0304 ×2, TXB0108), a second 3.3 V rail, and 4
   level-shift nets — and it serves *only* programming/console. Not a parity gap; a deliberate delta.
   Everything else is cheap and should be closed now.

## 3. What this means — and my recommendation

> **Doc defects found while answering JP's questions (2026-11-04) — fix before rev A snapshot:**
> - **D1** `sgc_architecture_hardware.md:162` says "P0.18 → BQ25120 MR (reset network)". **Wrong.**
>   Verified in ABX00050: net **`RESET_BHI260`** (BHI260 pad 9 / E3 `PIU509`) goes to the B112 **P0.18**.
>   Corroborated by our own Zephyr overlay comment: "BHI260 RESET pin 9 = Arduino variant pin 13 =
>   P0.18 (see variant.cpp:91)". P0.18 on Nicla is the **BHI reset**, not BQ MR.
> - **D2** `sgc_netlist.py:492` R4 net is **`+1V8`** but its own comment and spec §4.1 E2 say **`V_PMID`**.
>   V_PMID is the correct rail (present with battery alone; +1V8/SYS does not exist in ship mode, so the
>   pull-up would not guarantee active mode at cold boot — the whole point of OD-8). **Fix net, not doc.**

content.text:
All four answered from the files, and two of them exposed defects.

**1) Why do they claim "most Arduino modules"?**

Because it's true — for *modules*. I pulled every `ki_description` in the file. There are ~65 symbols, and every single one is a **Socket**, **Tile**, or **Shield**: Uno R3/R4, Mega, Due, Zero, MKR ×9, Nano ×12, Pro Mini, Leonardo, Giga, Nicla Vision/Voice/Sense ME. That covers "most Arduino modules" as the author means it — a *socket* for the module itself (2×14 pin headers with the right pitch) plus an SMD *tile* pattern for soldering it down flat, plus shield outlines for the giant form factors.

It never claims to contain the chips *on* those modules. So the description is accurate; my reading of it was too generous. **Concretely useless for us:** it would only give us a Nicla socket to plug a stock Nicla into — the carrier concept dropped in v2.4.

*"Use whatever is simple"* — noted. What's actually simple is what we already do: draw parts straight from the datasheets. No library shopping.

**2) Qi → USB-C**

Qi = wireless charging (the pad you drop a phone on). The original concept had a Qi receiver coil + **IP6833** chip on the back of the board, so the ski device could be charged by dropping it on a pad — no connector, good for a sealed IP67 unit.

Dropped **2026-08-13** (`sgc_bom.md` v4.1, `sgc_usb_c_charging_spec.md`) for two reasons: **planarity** (a coil on the back of a 22 × 55 mm board warps/cups it during reflow) and **centring** (you must align the device on the pad, which in a ski glove at −15 °C is the exact experience we're trying to avoid). Replaced by USB-C with an **IP67 sealed cap**: GCT USB4085 mid-mount, two 5.1 kΩ Rd resistors so any USB-C source gives 5 V, into the same BQ25120A.

It's still mentioned in `sgc_architecture_hardware.md` §7.4 as a retained-but-DNP section, plus a stale `P0.10 → QI_DETECT` line in the block diagram. The decision stands — I'm not reopening it.

**3) What P0.24 / P0.25 were for**

From `sgc_architecture_hardware.md`:
- **P0.24** → **Boost EN** (v1): the enable pin of the MT3608 that makes the 5 V rail for the LED strip. In v2 it was going to double as **RFID_EN** (power gate for the UHF reader).
- **P0.25** → **Charge disable** (BQ25120A `/CD`).

Both are SGC functions, **not** Nicla signals — so losing them costs us nothing in parity. Already remapped in spec §3.3: **Boost EN → P0.17**, **BQ CD → P0.08**. The netlist already uses the new pins.

Datasheet confirmation is unambiguous: **zero occurrences** of P0.24/P0.25 in the B402 datasheet, and the P0.2x list runs `P0.20 P0.21 P0.22 P0.23 P0.26 …` — the gap is real, not a doc slip. The B402 gives 33 GPIOs, so we still have plenty.

**4) RESET_N on P0.18 — do we change it? No. We adopt it, and the firmware changes instead.**

On the B112, GPIO pin 18 was a normal I/O that Nicla used for **BHI260AP reset**. On the B402, physical pin 12 **is** RESET_N and it's hardwired to P0.18 inside the module — it resets *us*. We can't repurpose it.

So:
- **Hardware:** BHI260AP RESETN moves to **P0.13** (B402 pin 52). Already in the netlist.
- **Firmware:** one pin change — BHI reset moves 18 → 13. Our Zephyr overlay doesn't even declare it as a DT property (the `bosch,bhi260ap` binding silently drops `reset-gpios`); it's a code-level pulse, so this is a small edit, not a re-architecture.
- **Bonus:** we gain a clean module reset on the SWD header instead of relying on power-cycling.

Note the trade: Nicla's `P0.18 → BQ25120 MR` net disappears, because P0.18 is no longer ours to drive. MR is unused on P1 anyway (ship mode goes through `/CD`). But the BHI reset pulse we *do* want to keep — hence P0.13.

**Two defects I found while verifying this:**

- **D1** — `sgc_architecture_hardware.md:162` claims "P0.18 → BQ25120 MR (reset network)". **Wrong.** ABX00050 shows the net **`RESET_BHI260`** (BHI260 pad 9, E3 `PIU509`) going to B112 P0.18 — corroborated by our own overlay comment ("BHI260 RESET pin 9 = Arduino variant pin 13 = P0.18"). Nicla's P0.18 is BHI reset, not BQ MR. Spec §3.3 C3 had already reasoned to the right answer from wrong premises; the outcome (BHI RST → P0.13) is unchanged and correct.
- **D2** — `sgc_netlist.py:492`: R4, the `/CD` pull-up, sits on **`+1V8`** while its own comment and spec §4.1 say **`V_PMID`**. That's a functional bug, not cosmetics: in ship mode SYS/+1V8 doesn't exist, so a pull-up there can't hold CD high — which defeats the entire OD-8 rationale of always waking active. **The net must change to V_PMID.**

Committed as `c53fe09`.

**SAMD11 bridge: recorded as omitted in rev A, footprint block reserved for rev B.** ✅

Next I'd fix D2 (one-line net change, real bug) and D1 (doc), then start the page split with `04_sensors` so G1/G2/G3 are drawn once, in the right place. Say go and I'll run it.

arguments.content:
# Nicla (P0) → custom N1 board: firmware migration assessment

**JP question 2026-11-04:** *"In general, will we need to change the code? How likely is it that we will get
problems when migrating from the Nicla to the custom boosted version? Let's introduce the eventual
differences behind macro switches, so that a macro declaration is enough to compile for one module or
another."*

**Short answer:** Yes, code changes — but only **3 real ones**, and the "one declaration" mechanism you want
**already exists** and is better than macros. Honestly measured below.

---

## 1. What is actually hardcoded today (measured, not estimated)

The whole app is **9,122 lines** of C. A full grep for every pin, port and register constant finds:

| Location | What | Portable? |
|---|---|---|
| `app.overlay:32` | `cs-gpios = <&gpio0 26>, <&gpio0 31>` — flash CS, BHI CS | ✅ devicetree (move to board) |
| `app.overlay:63` | button `gpios = <&gpio0 2>` | ✅ devicetree (move to board) |
| `app.overlay:34-44` | `&spi2` node, `bhi260@1`, 16 MHz | ✅ devicetree (move to board) |
| `src/button.c:23` | `#define BTN_PIN 2` | ⚠ duplicates DT — should read DT instead |
| `src/ble_config.c:368-380` | BQ CD commented/written as **P0.25** | ❌ **wrong on N1** (P0.25 absent; CD = P0.08) |
| `src/bhy2/bhy2_zephyr.c:363-371` | **raw `PIN_CNF` block**, `cnf[18]=0x301` = BHI reset | ❌ **dangerous on N1** (P0.18 = module RESET_N) |
| `bq_probe()` (same file) | writes BQ reg `LDO_CTRL <- 0xA8` (`enable1V8LDO()`) | ❌ pointless on N1 (LS/LDO unused) |

**That is the entire non-portable surface of 9,122 lines** — 4 items, 2 of them in one forensic probe
function (`bhy2_bitbang_probe`) that is a *debug artifact* from the M1 bring-up saga and should not ship
to N1 at all.

Everything else in the firmware — BLE/GATT, OTA/mcumgr, RawRunStore/SGL log, recorder state machine,
bitpacking, ring buffer, LED state, power state, pull protocol — is **board-agnostic already**. That is the
payoff of the V-cycle discipline.

---

## 2. The mechanism: board target, not `#ifdef`

**Your instinct is right, but macros are the wrong tool — and you already have the better one.**

`tools/zbuild.bat` takes the board as an argument:
```
zbuild.bat <app-dir> <board> <build-dir> [overlay]
buildfw.bat:  ... C:\sgc\apps\03_pull_proto arduino_nicla_sense_me ...
```

So the "one declaration" you're asking for is **one word on the build line**:

```bat
buildfw.bat  →  BOARD = arduino_nicla_sense_me   (P0, today)
buildfw.bat  →  BOARD = sgc_n1                   (N1, new board dir)
```

`-DBOARD=sgc_n1` is literally a single switch that produces two firmwares. Pins then live in the board
devicetree (`boards/sgc_n1/*.dts` + `.dtsi`), which is exactly what Zephyr created the board abstraction
for. **No source change at all** for anything pin-related — the three DT items above vanish into the board
file.

**Where a real compile-time conditional *is* justified** — only because these are register pokes and BQ
register writes that cannot be expressed in devicetree:

```c
/* one Kconfig symbol, three uses, that's all */
CONFIG_SGC_BOARD="n1"          // prj.conf / board defconfig
```
```c
#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_BOARD_SGC_N1)
    cnf[18] = 0x0;   /* BHI reset is P0.13 on N1; P0.18 is our own RESET_N — never drive it */
    cnf[13] = 0x301;
#else
    cnf[18] = 0x301; /* Nicla: mbed core drives BHI reset released */
#endif
```

My recommendation: **delete `bhy2_bitbang_probe()` for N1** rather than conditionalise it. It exists to
excavate a bug that is already solved (BHI on Zephyr works since M1). Shipping it to a board where
`cnf[18]` drives our own reset line is asking for a mystery-brick.

---

## 3. Likelihood of problems — honest, per risk

| # | Risk | Likelihood | Why | Cost if it bites |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-a | **Pin map errors** (wrong GPIO in board file) | 🟡 Medium | 33 signals to transcribe; three already moved (C1/C2/C3) | 1 hour each, caught at bring-up LED/button test |
| R-b | **`cnf[18]=0x301` drives RESET_N** | 🔴 **High if probe kept** | P0.18 *is* RESET_N on B402. Writing output-HIGH to it → reset held/glitched | Brick-loop; `netdiff` + code review catches it. **Delete the probe** |
| R-c | **BHI260AP bring-up regression** | 🟡 Medium | This exact block consumed weeks on Nicla (PIN_CNF/bitbang saga). Same SPI, same CS pin, same cluster wiring copied verbatim → physics identical, but any 100 ns timing difference re-opens it | Days, *if* it goes wrong. Mitigated by verbatim cluster copy + keeping CS/SCK/MOSI/MISO identical |
| R-d | **32 kHz clock** | 🟢 Low | Nicla fits Y1 SIT1532AI → LFXO. **N1 adds Y1 (gap G3)** → same config | Zero, *provided* G3 lands. If Y1 is ever omitted → LFRC Kconfig change |
| R-e | **BQ LDO / VDDIO_EXT** | 🟢 Low | Nicla has software-programmable VDDIO_EXT for the headers; N1 drops it (§C4, LSCTRL→GND). `LDO_CTRL <- 0xA8` becomes a no-op | Write returns ACK, does nothing. Harmless |
| R-f | **Flash size / OTA partitions** | 🟢 Low | nRF52833 = 512 KB flash = same as 52832. MCUboot layout unchanged | Zero |
| R-g | **RAM** | 🟢 **Improvement** | 128 KB vs 64 KB — we were at 7.3 KB free. OTA reassembly (+11 KB) becomes *possible* | Positive |
| R-h | **Console/UART** | 🟢 Low | Both use TX P0.20 / RX P0.09 (Nicla LPIO1/LPIO2 parity) | Zero |
| R-i | **New sensors appear** (BME688, BMM150, MAX17048, Y1) | 🟢 Low, additive | All new code is *guarded by presence*; existing paths untouched | Additive only |
| R-j | **Rev B SAMD11 bridge** | 🟢 Low | Omitted rev A (your OK). If added later: USB CDC console + programming path changes | Scoped separately |

**Overall verdict: low-to-moderate.** The one item that could genuinely hurt (R-b) is a debug function we
should delete, not port. The one that could cost days (R-c) is mitigated by the fact that we are copying
the sensor cluster *verbatim* — deliberately, which is precisely why your "clone, don't reinterpret"
doctrine is the low-risk path.

**Biggest real risk is not in this list:** it is *believing* the board file without verifying. Mitigation is
a defined N1 bring-up gate — LED → button → console → flash JEDEC → BHI → sensors, each a pass/fail line,
exactly like the M0/M1 gates that worked.

---

## 4. Work plan (small, ordered, each step verifiable)

1. **Create `boards/sgc_n1/`** — board yaml, `.dts`/`.dtsi`, `Kconfig.defconfig`, pinmap header. Transcribe
   the 33 signals from `sgc_schematic_spec.md` §3.2. **No app source touched.**
2. **Move the 3 DT items** (2× cs-gpios, button, `&spi2`) from `app.overlay` into the board devicetree.
   Build for Nicla → must still pass the existing CORE suite (regression proof).
3. **Kill/guard the two hazards:** remove `bhy2_bitbang_probe()` for N1; make BQ CD pin DT-driven instead of
   the `P0.25` comment/literal.
4. **`#define BTN_PIN 2` → DT lookup** (removes the last duplicate pin).
5. **Build both targets in CI-ish fashion**: `zbuild.bat <app> arduino_nicla_sense_me` and
   `zbuild.bat <app> sgc_n1` must both link green before any N1 board exists. This proves the "one switch"
   promise *before* hardware is in hand.
6. When N1 rev A comes back: run the bring-up gate above.

**What I will NOT do:** litter the 9,122 lines with `#ifdef`. Two targets, one board argument, three guarded
register-level spots — everything else stays single-source.

---

## 5. Answer to "will we need to change the code?"

**Yes — 3 spots, ~15 lines total**, plus one new board directory. Not a port; a pin remap.

The reason it is this small is that we already respect the Nicla pin map exactly. The migration is cheap
**because** you chose the clone strategy — the further the board drifts from Nicla, the more firmware forks.
That is a strong argument for closing the G1–G5 parity gaps rather than "improving" them.

| `src/ble_config.c:368-380` | BQ CD commented/written as **P0.25** | ❌ **wrong on N1** (P0.25 absent; CD = P0.08) |
| `src/bhy2/bhy2_zephyr.c:363-371` | **raw `PIN_CNF` block**, `cnf[18]=0x301` = BHI reset | ❌ **dangerous on N1** (P0.18 = module RESET_N) |
| `bq_probe()` (same file) | writes BQ reg `LDO_CTRL <- 0xA8` (`enable1V8LDO()`) | ❌ pointless on N1 (LS/LDO unused) |

**That is the entire non-portable surface of 9,122 lines** — 4 items, 2 of them in one forensic probe
function (`bhy2_bitbang_probe`) that is a *debug artifact* from the M1 bring-up saga and should not ship
to N1 at all.

Everything else in the firmware — BLE/GATT, OTA/mcumgr, RawRunStore/SGL log, recorder state machine,
bitpacking, ring buffer, LED state, power state, pull protocol — is **board-agnostic already**. That is the
payoff of the V-cycle discipline.

---

## 2. The mechanism: board target, not `#ifdef`

**Your instinct is right, but macros are the wrong tool — and you already have the better one.**

`tools/zbuild.bat` takes the board as an argument:
```
zbuild.bat <app-dir> <board> <build-dir> [overlay]
buildfw.bat:  ... C:\sgc\apps\03_pull_proto arduino_nicla_sense_me ...
```

So the "one declaration" you're asking for is **one word on the build line**:

```bat
buildfw.bat  →  BOARD = arduino_nicla_sense_me   (P0, today)
buildfw.bat  →  BOARD = sgc_n1                   (N1, new board dir)
```

`-DBOARD=sgc_n1` is literally a single switch that produces two firmwares. Pins then live in the board
devicetree (`boards/sgc_n1/*.dts` + `.dtsi`), which is exactly what Zephyr created the board abstraction
for. **No source change at all** for anything pin-related — the three DT items above vanish into the board
file.

**Where a real compile-time conditional *is* justified** — only because these are register pokes and BQ
register writes that cannot be expressed in devicetree:

```c
/* one Kconfig symbol, three uses, that's all */
CONFIG_SGC_BOARD="n1"          // prj.conf / board defconfig
```
```c
#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_BOARD_SGC_N1)
    cnf[18] = 0x0;   /* BHI reset is P0.13 on N1; P0.18 is our own RESET_N — never drive it */
    cnf[13] = 0x301;
#else
    cnf[18] = 0x301; /* Nicla: mbed core drives BHI reset released */
#endif
```

My recommendation: **delete `bhy2_bitbang_probe()` for N1** rather than conditionalise it. It exists to
excavate a bug that is already solved (BHI on Zephyr works since M1). Shipping it to a board where
`cnf[18]` drives our own reset line is asking for a mystery-brick.

---

## 3. Likelihood of problems — honest, per risk

| # | Risk | Likelihood | Why | Cost if it bites |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-a | **Pin map errors** (wrong GPIO in board file) | 🟡 Medium | 33 signals to transcribe; three already moved (C1/C2/C3) | 1 hour each, caught at bring-up LED/button test |
| R-b | **`cnf[18]=0x301` drives RESET_N** | 🔴 **High if probe kept** | P0.18 *is* RESET_N on B402. Writing output-HIGH to it → reset held/glitched | Brick-loop; `netdiff` + code review catches it. **Delete the probe** |
| R-c | **BHI260AP bring-up regression** | 🟡 Medium | This exact block consumed weeks on Nicla (PIN_CNF/bitbang saga). Same SPI, same CS pin, same cluster wiring copied verbatim → physics identical, but any 100 ns timing difference re-opens it | Days, *if* it goes wrong. Mitigated by verbatim cluster copy + keeping CS/SCK/MOSI/MISO identical |
| R-d | **32 kHz clock** | 🟢 Low | Nicla fits Y1 SIT1532AI → LFXO. **N1 adds Y1 (gap G3)** → same config | Zero, *provided* G3 lands. If Y1 is ever omitted → LFRC Kconfig change |
| R-e | **BQ LDO / VDDIO_EXT** | 🟢 Low | Nicla has software-programmable VDDIO_EXT for the headers; N1 drops it (§C4, LSCTRL→GND). `LDO_CTRL <- 0xA8` becomes a no-op | Write returns ACK, does nothing. Harmless |
| R-f | **Flash size / OTA partitions** | 🟢 Low | nRF52833 = 512 KB flash = same as 52832. MCUboot layout unchanged | Zero |
| R-g | **RAM** | 🟢 **Improvement** | 128 KB vs 64 KB — we were at 7.3 KB free. OTA reassembly (+11 KB) becomes *possible* | Positive |
| R-h | **Console/UART** | 🟢 Low | Both use TX P0.20 / RX P0.09 (Nicla LPIO1/LPIO2 parity) | Zero |
| R-i | **New sensors appear** (BME688, BMM150, MAX17048, Y1) | 🟢 Low, additive | All new code is *guarded by presence*; existing paths untouched | Additive only |
| R-j | **Rev B SAMD11 bridge** | 🟢 Low | Omitted rev A (your OK). If added later: USB CDC console + programming path changes | Scoped separately |

**Overall verdict: low-to-moderate.** The one item that could genuinely hurt (R-b) is a debug function we
should delete, not port. The one that could cost days (R-c) is mitigated by the fact that we are copying
the sensor cluster *verbatim* — deliberately, which is precisely why your "clone, don't reinterpret"
doctrine is the low-risk path.

**Biggest real risk is not in this list:** it is *believing* the board file without verifying. Mitigation is
a defined N1 bring-up gate — LED → button → console → flash JEDEC → BHI → sensors, each a pass/fail line,
exactly like the M0/M1 gates that worked.

---

## 4. Work plan (small, ordered, each step verifiable)

1. **Create `boards/sgc_n1/`** — board yaml, `.dts`/`.dtsi`, `Kconfig.defconfig`, pinmap header. Transcribe
   the 33 signals from `sgc_schematic_spec.md` §3.2. **No app source touched.**
2. **Move the 3 DT items** (2× cs-gpios, button, `&spi2`) from `app.overlay` into the board devicetree.
   Build for Nicla → must still pass the existing CORE suite (regression proof).
3. **Kill/guard the two hazards:** remove `bhy2_bitbang_probe()` for N1; make BQ CD pin DT-driven instead of
   the `P0.25` comment/literal.
4. **`#define BTN_PIN 2` → DT lookup** (removes the last duplicate pin).
5. **Build both targets in CI-ish fashion**: `zbuild.bat <app> arduino_nicla_sense_me` and
   `zbuild.bat <app> sgc_n1` must both link green before any N1 board exists. This proves the "one switch"
   promise *before* hardware is in hand.
6. When N1 rev A comes back: run the bring-up gate above.

**What I will NOT do:** litter the 9,122 lines with `#ifdef`. Two targets, one board argument, three guarded
register-level spots — everything else stays single-source.

---

## 5. Answer to "will we need to change the code?"

**Yes — 3 spots, ~15 lines total**, plus one new board directory. Not a port; a pin remap.

The reason it is this small is that we already respect the Nicla pin map exactly. The migration is cheap
**because** you chose the clone strategy — the further the board drifts from Nicla, the more firmware forks.
That is a strong argument for closing the G1–G5 parity gaps rather than "improving" them.

content.text:
## 3. The working configuration (v0.11.14, apps/03_pull_proto)

- Manual GPIO CS (P0.31, plain polarity) around every op — never trust
  DT CS for unbound compatibles.
- Read framing: single scratch buffer covering address+data, discard
  byte 0 manually (no NULL skip entries in the rx set).
- 8 MHz (16 MHz is illegal on nRF52832 SPIM2; mbed's 16M request
  clamps anyway). Mode 0, MSB-first.
- P0.18 held output-HIGH from bring-up, never pulsed.
- Vendored bhy2 API (from Arduino_BHY2, our cal-hook-era copy) +
  `bhy2_init → soft_reset (ignore rc) → boot_from_flash → proof`.

## 4. Debugging arsenal (reusable)

- **Arduino probe sketches**: `workspace/bench_bhy_test/` (PlatformIO
  on the VPS; vendored Arduino_BHY2 + ArduinoBLE copied from the SGC
  libdeps). probe4 = the decisive bisection (library read vs bit-bang
  on a live hub).
- **Flashing Arduino images via OpenOCD**: app hexes are app-only
  (linked above the bootloader) — **flash
  `~/.platformio/packages/framework-arduino-mbed/bootloaders/NICLA/bootloader.hex`
  at 0x0 FIRST, then the app hex**, else double-fault lockup.
- **PIN_CNF dump** from the Arduino side reveals the mbed core's pin
  states (P0.18=0x301 etc.).
- **Bit-banging after SPIM detach**: nRF peripheral PSEL shadows GPIO
  — detach (ENABLE=0, PSEL=0xFFFFFFFF) before bit-banging; reboot to
  restore.
- **PMIC** BQ25120 at 0x6A on Zephyr `&i2c0` (TWIM0, P0.15/16 — same
  bus as the IS31 LED).

## 5. Post-mortem: what the debugging cost taught

- The "hub silent" diagnosis was built on a register that legitimately
  reads zero. Always calibrate your health-check register against the
  known-good stack BEFORE trusting it.
- The control group (flash JEDEC via bit-bang) proved the wires but
  couldn't prove the CS path — a shared-bus control doesn't test
  per-device select lines.
- Zephyr devicetree silently drops what bindings don't declare — both
  `reset-gpios` (compile error when referenced) and, far worse, the
  spi-device bus resolution (silent at compile time).

**Rationale (v2):** No mechanical button, no moving parts — preserves IP67 sealing. The athlete naturally brings forearms together before pushing off at the start gate. This motion is detected as rising LDC1612 inductance shift from the approaching copper/iron target disc on the opposite strap. Both arms arm independently on their own sensor.

### Piezo Pushbutton — Arming (v1 Pole-Mount)

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Type | Langir 16 mm piezoelectric pushbutton, momentary NO (pulse output) |
| Interface | GPIO P0.02 (internal pull-up). Falling edge = press. **Edge interrupt** (not 10 Hz poll) |
| Activation | Athlete presses button with back of glove |
| Arm | Single press (F03) |
| Factory reset | 5 presses within 3 s (F42) |
| Button | Langir 16 mm, IP68/IP69K, stainless, ≤3 N, 50 M cycles, −40…+85 °C |
| Output | NO pulse 20–1000 ms (piezo — no sustained hold) |

**Rationale:** No magnet (avoids BMM150 magnetometer de-calibration), no moving parts
(piezo element behind a solid metal face → trivial IP67 sealing), glove-friendly
(≤3 N on a Ø16 mm face). Replaces both the reed switch (rejected — magnet field
interferes with the BMM150 in the BHI260AP) and the LDC1612 (footprint too large
for pole-mount + aluminium pole shaft is itself a conductive target).

**Firmware change:** a piezo emits a *pulse*, not a held level. P0.02 must be configured
as a **GPIO edge interrupt** — a 10 Hz poll will miss the 20 ms pulse. Arming logic moves
from "1000 ms continuous hold" to "single press"; factory reset from "20 s hold" to
"5 presses in 3 s". Debounce is minimal (single clean closure).

content.text:
Three answers — and the button question uncovered a real contradiction in our own docs.

## 1) What `bhy2_bitbang_probe()` actually solved

From `docs/bhi260_zephyr_bringup.md` §3–5, it was the **decisive instrument in the BHI260 bring-up battle** — the one that ended a multi-week "hub silent" goose chase. It proved three separate things at once:

- **The wires were fine.** It bit-banged SPI by hand at 100 kHz on P0.03/04/05 and read the flash JEDEC ID (`C22815`) through the *same* bus — a control group proving the physical pins and the flash CS path worked. So the fault had to be on the BHI's own CS.
- **The hub was being held in reset.** The `PIN_CNF` photocopy showed `P0.18 = 0x301` — mbed's core drives it **output-HIGH** at init. Our floating bit-bang probe had left it low, holding the hub in reset through *every* scan. That's why every probe said "silent".
- **Peripheral PSEL shadows GPIO.** You can't bit-bang a pin that a peripheral owns — you must detach SPIM first (`ENABLE=0`, `PSEL=0xFFFFFFFF`).

Plus one permanent lesson recorded there: *"a shared-bus control doesn't test per-device select lines"* — flash working proved the bus, not the BHI CS.

So: it was a **bisection instrument**, and its output — "P0.18 must be driven HIGH, never pulsed" — is already baked into the working configuration. The probe itself is scaffolding around a solved problem. On N1 that same line would drive **our own RESET_N**. Deleting it is correct.

## 2) The button — no special MCU, but you've found a real bug

**No special microcontroller needed.** A piezo pushbutton is electrically just a momentary contact closure into a GPIO with a pull-up. Nothing exotic. What it needs is **protection**, not a special MCU.

**Planned model** (`sgc_bom.md` v4.0/v4.1): **Langir 16 mm piezoelectric pushbutton, momentary NO** — Ø16 mm 316L stainless face, IP68/IP69K, ≤3 N actuation, 50 M cycles, −40…+85 °C, ~$12/$9/$7. Chosen 2026-08-12 over the Schurter PSE NO 16 (EOL) and over a magnetic reed (rejected: the magnet de-calibrated the BMM150 — which is exactly the sensor we're now adding back, so that decision ages well). Bench stand-in today is a monostable switch on J5 (JST-SH-2).

**Two things that need your attention:**

**a) Genuine contradiction between docs and firmware.** Hardware doc says the piezo emits a **pulse of 20–1000 ms**, "no sustained hold", arming = **single press (F03)**. But `button.c` (JP 2026-10-15) implements **"HOLD ≥ 1 s of CONTINUOUS press → ARMED"**, with a 10-tick hold gate specifically so "pole knocks / packing bumps must not arm". **A piezo cannot hold for 1 s.** So on the real Langir button, the current firmware would likely never arm. That gate was added for the bench monostable switch — it's wire-compatible but behaviour-incompatible. This needs deciding before the button is soldered: either piezo → single-press + software bump-rejection (e.g. require press-release-press, or a quiet-period heuristic), or keep a device that can genuinely hold.

**b) Piezo elements generate voltage transients** — mechanically shocking a piezo disc can produce spikes far above the rail. Standard protection is a series resistor + clamp/TVS to the rails, plus the internal pull-up. **This is not in the netlist today** (`J5` goes straight to `BUTTON`). Worth adding regardless of which button you choose; it's ~2 cheap parts and it protects the B402 pin.

Also note the sealing benefit is real and matches your intent: piezo has **no moving part through the wall**, so IP69K is trivial — this is the right button for water.

## 3) G1–G5 recapped

All five are **Nicla-parity parts that the spec mandates but the netlist never implemented**:

| # | Gap | Part | Cost | nRF pins |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G1** | Magnetometer missing | **BMM150** — rides BHI260AP **M3 I²C** (`ASCX`/`ASDX`) | ~3 parts + decap | **0** |
| **G2** | Environment/T/RH/gas missing | **BME688** — rides BHI260AP **MCSB2, pad 18** (already reserved, currently NC) | ~3 parts + decap | **0** |
| **G3** | 32.768 kHz oscillator missing | **Y1 SIT1532AI-J4-DCC-32.768E** → XL1, XL2→GND. `32K_XL1` is currently dangling | 1 part + 100 nF | **0** |
| **G4** | VBUS reverse/back-feed protection | **D3 PMEG4005EPK** series into BQ IN | 1 part | 0 |
| **G5** | Decoupling for the two new sensors | per Nicla bank: 1 µF + 100 nF ×N | ~5 caps | 0 |

The critical point: **G1–G3 consume zero microcontroller pins.** They hang off the BHI260AP's own master port and its XTAL input. That's why they were pure oversight and why closing them is nearly free.

I confirmed from the schematic text that our architecture matches Nicla: **BME688 CS → BHI MCSB2 (pad 18)**, **BMP390 → MCSB1/CS_390**, **BMM150 → M3 (`ASCX`/`ASDX`)**. Ball-level wiring I'll copy from the PDF at capture rather than guess, as the spec already requires.

**Ready to execute.** All five are additive — no existing net changes except G4 inserting D3 in series on VBUS, plus the two independent fixes (D2 CD pull-up → V_PMID, and the `cnf[18]` hazard deletion).

One decision from you first, because it changes G-set scope: **the button issue (a)** — do we switch firmware to single-press arming for the piezo, or reconsider the button? And say go, and I'll land G1–G5 + the piezo protection RC/clamp + D2 in one pass, then re-run ERC to prove nothing broke.

content.text:
# SGC P1 — KiCad 8 schematic (generated capture)

**Board:** SGC P1 standalone carrier for u-blox ANNA-B402 — 22 × 55 mm, 4-layer, 0.8 mm, ENIG.
**Source of truth:** `../../sgc_schematic_spec.md` v0.1 (commit 92b352e). Every pin number, pin name
and net in this capture is traceable to that spec (or the datasheet texts it cites). Nothing invented;
everything the spec marks TBD-JP appears as a **text note**, never as a guessed value/net.

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `sgc_p1.kicad_pro` | KiCad 8 project (minimal) |
| `sgc_p1.kicad_sym` | Project symbol library — 21 symbols (12 ICs/connectors + R/C/L/LED_RGB + 5 power symbols) |
| `sgc_p1.kicad_sch` | Single A3 landscape sheet, KiCad 8 format (version 20231120) |
| `sgc_netlist.py` | **Data**: symbol pin tables + per-component net assignment (edit here first) |
| `gen_symbols.py` | Regenerates `sgc_p1.kicad_sym` from the netlist |
| `gen_schematic.py` | Regenerates `sgc_p1.kicad_sch` + `sgc_p1.kicad_pro` |
| `validate_sgc_p1.py` | Mandatory validation (see below) |

## How to open (KiCad 8.x)

1. Open KiCad 8 → *File → Open Project* → select `sgc_p1.kicad_pro`.
2. Add the symbol library once: *Preferences → Manage Symbol Libraries → Project Libraries → add*
   → `sgc_p1.kicad_sym` (nickname `sgc_p1`). The schematic already embeds every used symbol in its
   `lib_symbols` section, so the sheet displays even before you register the library.
3. Open `sgc_p1.kicad_sch` in Eeschema.

**Regenerate after edits:** `python3 gen_symbols.py && python3 gen_schematic.py && python3 validate_sgc_p1.py`
(requires `pip install kiutils`). Edit `sgc_netlist.py`, not the generated files.

## Layout of the sheet (grouped by subsystem)

- **Top-left:** USB-C (J1), CC Rd resistors, VBUS bulk, BQ25120A charger + its R/C network.
- **Bottom-left:** MAX17048 gauge, JST-3 battery connector, SWD header (J3).
- **Center:** ANNA-B402 (U1, all 56 pins incl. 4/7/8 GND from Table 4) + antenna keepout note.
- **Right:** BHI260AP (U8, all 44 pads), BMP390L (U9), flash U7/U2, IS31FL3194 (U5) + RGB LED (D1).
- **Bottom-middle:** LDC1612 (U6, DNP v2) + peripheral/v2 notes (boost, SK6812, Y1, TPs, DNP list).

Connectivity style: **global labels on short stubs** for every pin (61 named nets) + **power symbols**
(`#PWR01…`, per zone anchors) on the power nets GND / +1V8 / VBAT / V_PMID / VBUS_USB. No sprawling wires.
Note boxes carry all OD callouts, the antenna keepout (SIM App. B), I²C address map and the peripheral/v2 notes.

## Refdes scheme (per task; spec's Nicla numbering preserved where it matters)

U1 ANNA-B402 · U2 MX25R1635F (BHI FW flash, OD-5) · U3 BQ25120A · U4 MAX17048 · U5 IS31FL3194 ·
U6 LDC1612 (DNP) · U7 MX25R6435F · U8 BHI260AP · U9 BMP390L · J1 USB4085 · J2 JST-3 battery ·
J3 SWD 2×5 · D1 SMLP34RGB2W3 · C1–C16 · R1–R10 · L1. (Nicla-schematic numbering had IS31=U8 — remapped here.)

## What is decided vs TBD-JP (OD summary — all also on the sheet as notes)

**Decided & captured:** charger resistor network (1.82k/1k/4.99k/100k), all decoupling per spec §6,
I²C pull-ups 100 k→+1V8 (i2c0), BHI RESETN→P0.13 (C3/OD-7), BQ CD→P0.08 + 100k PU V_PMID (C2/OD-8),
boost EN→P0.17 (C1), gauge ALRT→P0.21 + 10k PU, XL2→GND, ANT_INT↔ANT bridge, ANT_PCB→GND pattern
(corner placement), U2 QSPI nets, LDC ADDR→GND (0x2A) + INTB→BUTTON (OD-11), SWD pinout.

**TBD-JP — represented as notes only (never guessed):**
- **OD-4** battery connector PN + cell confirm; NTC R_HI/R_LO values (need Renata R25/B).
- **OD-5** U2 added to BOM (drawn populated, Nicla parity).
- **OD-6** BME688 populate-vs-DNP (not drawn; note at U8 — rides BHI M1 with BMM150).
- **OD-9 / OD-9b** +5 V level translator part (TXB0102-class); SK6812 strip stays on P0.19 pending R2 bench.

content.text:
**Resumed and finished — G1–G5 are closed and the validator is green.**

`VALIDATION PASSED: all checks green` — 66 components, 351 pin connections, 73 nets.

**What landed** (`e004efd`):

| Gap | Part | Wiring |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | **BMM150** U12 | BHI M3 I²C — `M3SDA`=U8.1, `M3SCL`=U8.2, `M3_CS`=U8.19 (MCSB4); PS→+1V8 via R40 0R; SDO→GND (address LSB); R18/R29 10 kΩ pull-ups |
| G2 | **BME688** U13 | BHI M1 SPI, CS = `M1_CSB2` = **U8.18** (was NC) — **populated**, since you want temperature |
| G3 | **Y1 SIT1532AI** | OUT→`32K_XL1`=U1.17 — the net was **dangling**, now has 2 members |
| G4 | **D5 PMEG4005EPK** | series `VBUS_USB`→`VBUS_IN`→BQ IN; C1 bypass moved, C16 bulk stays at the connector |
| G5 | C21/C22/C23 | 100 nF decoupling |

**Piezo protection added** as you asked: `J5.1 → BUTTON_RAW → R41 100 kΩ → BUTTON`, clamped both ways by D6 (K→+1V8) and D7 (K→GND), BAT42WS. A piezo disc is a capacitive generator — a shock can spike well outside the rail, and the B402 pin is now protected in both directions.

**Also fixed a latent defect:** the R4 `/CD` pull-up was on **+1V8**, but it must be on **V_PMID**. SYS/+1V8 doesn't exist in ship mode, so a pull-up there could never hold CD high — which defeated the entire OD-8 cold-boot guarantee.

**Five pre-existing toolchain bugs surfaced and got fixed.** These are why the work stalled twice, and they'd have bitten you again:

1. `gen_symbols.py` had a **hand-kept symbol list** — it silently dropped symbols on regeneration (it wiped TXS0102, MT3608 and others). Now derived from the data.
2. `gen_schematic.py` **overwrote `sgc_p1.kicad_pro`**, destroying 265 lines of your project settings (3dviewports, ipc2581, net classes, ERC severities). It now **merges** and preserves them.
3. It also minted a **new root-sheet UUID every run**, breaking the child sheet link. Now reuses the existing one. The reason this was silent: `re` was imported only inside a function and a bare `except: pass` swallowed the `NameError` — the except now warns.
4. `split_led_sheet.py` hardcoded the root UUID and only understood kiutils formatting.
5. That same script's cluster box **overlapped the flash parts (U7/U2/C8/C9)** and dragged their wires onto the child sheet. Cluster relocated to a clean zone; margins now taken from **measured** label positions (the offset is 5.08 mm, not 2.54 — my first two guesses were wrong).

README now documents the mandatory 4-step pipeline, and that `kiutils` doesn't survive a container restart (`pip install --break-system-packages kiutils`).

**Two things I want to flag rather than bury:**

**Your piezo rule exposed a firmware bug.** "Reject any pressure when not idle or sleeping" is state-gated, and that's the right mechanism — but `button.c` currently requires **1 s of continuous press** to arm. A piezo emits a 20–1000 ms *pulse* and physically cannot hold for 1 s. **On the real Langir button the current firmware would probably never arm.** That gate was written for the bench monostable switch. It needs edge-interrupt + short debounce, with the state gate doing the anti-bump work. Documented in `sgc_architecture_hardware.md`; I did **not** touch the firmware yet since it's your call.

Plus a doc correction: the hardware doc claimed P0.18 → BQ25120 MR. Wrong — ABX00050 shows P0.18 is `RESET_BHI260`. Fixed (`6519ed5`).

**Honest note on the diff:** the schematic regenerates in the generator's format while the committed file was kiutils-formatted, so `sgc_p1.kicad_sch` shows a ~28k-line churn that is mostly whitespace. The electrical content is verified by the validator, not by eyeballing that diff. Worth one `git diff -w` if you want to review it.

**Still open:** D5 footprint (PMEG4005EPK is **SOD-1608** 1.0×0.6 mm — no verified stock KiCad footprint, left empty), the Y1 **1508 CSP** footprint has to be drawn, and the USB ESD part (OD-13).

content.thinking:
JP is answering my F42 question (what factory reset should do). His points:
1. "Why not from the phone?" — factory reset via the app/BLE is the natural path (the phone UI exists, it's connected, no accidental trigger).
2. If it must be on-device (button), it must be something a user would NEVER do accidentally, even when frustrated: e.g., 20 pushes in 10 s, or 5 pushes → red flash → 5 more pushes (a two-stage confirm with visual feedback).

My task now: answer the design question, make a recommendation, and implement the decision path. Also I'm mid-way through the SiT1532 pin-position extraction (charbox API name wrong — count_rects exists; I should finish that and create the footprints).

Priority: JP asked a direct design question — answer it first, then continue the footprint work in the same turn.

Design analysis for F42 factory reset:

Option A: Phone/BLE-triggered (JP's own suggestion) — best:
- Already have BLE GATT + config characteristics (F20/F21 params editors, device config)
- No accidental triggers ever
- Confirm dialog in app = two-step with UI feedback
- Works with gloves off... but reset is a maintenance action, typically done at home/with phone — perfect fit
- Consistency: pairing, config, run download all happen via phone already
- One wrinkle: if the device is bricked/config-corrupt and won't BLE-pair, a phone reset can't reach it. But config corruption is recoverable via safe defaults at boot (if we design CRC-checked config with fallback), and FW reflash via OTA/SWD exists. So the "recovery" argument for a hardware reset is weak.

Option B: On-device two-stage (JP's "5 pushes, red flash, 5 more"): good if we ever need hardware reset without phone. 5+5 with visual confirm is ~accident-proof. 20-in-10s is simpler but finger-fatiguing and no feedback mid-sequence; the red-flash variant gives feedback and intent confirmation.

My recommendation: A (phone, via a GATT command with app-side confirm) as THE factory reset; NO on-device reset in v1. Rationale:
- The user (athlete on mountain) should never be able to brick his chrono in the cold
- 20 pushes or 5+5 still has nonzero risk in the exact state where presses are accepted (SLEEP — gloves, retrying to arm, pressing repeatedly because it didn't arm = 10+ presses naturally happens when a cold user thinks the button didn't register!). That's the killer argument: a frustrated user whose arm press "didn't take" WILL hammer the button. 20-in-10s is actually reachable by hammering. So even "hard" sequences are risky in SLEEP state.
- Phone reset with explicit confirm = zero accidental risk + discoverable + consistent with F20/F21 config UI.
- Also: what does factory reset even DO? Wipe device config (name/side/discipline), un-pair? wipe stored runs? That's destructive enough that it deserves a UI, not a button dance.

Implementation shape (if JP agrees): 
- New GATT characteristic or a command on the config service: factory_reset (write 0x01 → device wipes config block, keeps runs unless "full" variant, reboots). App adds a "Factory reset" item with confirm dialog.
- Spec: add to requirements (F42 rewrite) — device.md/requirements v-next, plus BLE protocol doc line.
- On-device: nothing.

Then answer the footprint pin-position continuation: fix charbox call (use count_rects/get_rect API properly). pypdfium2 API: textpage.count_rects(index=0, count=-1), textpage.get_rect(i) → (l,b,r,t). content.thinking:
JP accepted the F42 proposal and now asks three security/pairing design questions:

1. **Athlete changes phone, no access to old one** — can he connect with the new phone?
2. **Theft prevention** — how to prevent another athlete from stealing and using the SGC? Cloud upload could help.
3. **Could a thief reflash via USB to take possession?**

These are design questions about the SGC device. Let me ground the answers in what the device actually is:

**Current architecture facts (from docs/memory):**
- BLE: Nordic SoftDevice/smp; pairing exists? Memory: "Pairing UI waits 2nd Nicla (Nov budget)" — so pairing UX is planned. The device runs a GATT server with pull protocol, config, OTA (MCUmgr SMP over BLE, RSA-signed images via MCUboot!).
- USB: **N1 board has NO USB data path at all!** We decided to OMIT the SAMD11 USB bridge (JP OK'd rev A). The USB-C is CHARGE-ONLY (VBUS → BQ25120A, D+/D− NC). There is no USB firmware interface to attack. This is a decisive fact for question 3.
- MCUboot: dual-slot, RSA-signed, swap-on-boot. Unsigned images are rejected — flashing via SWD is possible physically but requires opening the enclosure (4 screws) — and even a full reflash can't "take possession" of the *data* (runs stored in external flash... actually SWD could read flash too, but that's physical access, enclosure-opening territory).
- Device identity: nRF52 has no write-once user FUSES like nRF91? nRF52833: there's APPROTECT (debug port protection) on newer nRF52 (FICR APPROTECT) — yes! nRF52833 supports APPROTECT which permanently disables SWD access after provisioning (erase-all to unlock). Also SECURE APPROTECT variants. This is the standard anti-SWD measure.
- The device config (name/side/discipline @0x1FC000 external flash) + runs survive reflash.
- Cloud: "remote DB arc (REQ-DB/I07)" is the next planned arc — data upload planned.

Now the design answers:

**Q1: Phone change without old phone.**
Standard BLE approach: if we use "just works" pairing/bonding, the bond lives in the phone + device. New phone can't connect if the device only accepts bonded peers. Solutions:
- **Pairing mode / re-pairing flow:** device accepts a NEW bond when (a) physically confirmed — but our only input is the piezo button! We DO have a button. E.g., hold/press during power-up, or "3 presses within 3s while in SLEEP puts device into pairing mode for 60s". Since SLEEP is the state where presses are accepted, a dedicated sequence distinct from normal use... but JP just worried about frustrated hammering triggering factory reset. Pairing-mode entry could instead be: the device enters pairing mode automatically when it has NO active bond? No — bond exists on device side.
- Better, simplest and athlete-friendly: **the device doesn't hard-bind to one phone.** Use the session model: any phone running the SGC app can connect with a **device PIN** (printed in the battery bay / on the label, or shown via... no display). PIN on label under battery cap or in the box = classic. Then phone change = trivial (enter PIN). Also enables coach/loaner devices.
- Or: bond + "forget bond" via button long-press… we removed long-press (piezo).
- My recommendation: **numeric PIN on the housing/battery compartment** (6-digit), entered in the app on first connect. New phone → enter PIN → done. No dependency on old phone. PIN doubles as the anti-theft mechanism (Q2).

Alternatively BLE "Just Works" + no auth at all (current pull-proto is likely unencrypted): then any phone CAN connect — but that's also the theft answer problem.

**Q2: Theft prevention.**
Layers:
1. **PIN/bond gate** (from Q1): a stolen SGC can't be paired/used without the PIN → device is a brick to the thief. Physical PIN on label means a determined thief with physical access CAN read it though (label in battery bay — thief has the device, can open... battery is replaceable by design (4 screws + JST). Hmm — so label-PIN alone gives casual protection, not real.
2. **Owner binding in device:** device stores "owner account/device secret"; app authenticates with account credentials → cloud verifies. Stolen device: thief's app can't prove ownership. But offline (no account infra yet)…
3. **Cloud upload (JP's suggestion):** runs upload tagged with device ID + owner account. If a thief uses it with another account, the device ID appearing under a different account flags it → original owner sees their device "calling home" from elsewhere → proof/brick remotely (device checks in: cloud can push a "lock" state when device syncs). This is the LoJack approach: not preventing USE locally, but making resale/use traceable and eventually lockable. Requires the remote DB arc (I07) to exist — which is planned.
4. Practical product answer for a ski-gate chrono with a €? BOM (~$60 prototype / $27 at 1k): theft protection should be proportionate — PIN + cloud identity is enough; don't build TPM-grade security into a sports timer. A sticker/warning + traceability is the norm. Also the enclosure needs opening for battery → any "protection" is defeat-able by a screwdriver anyway.

Recommendation: PIN pairing (Q1) + device ownership record in cloud with device serial; cloud can flag/lock on next sync. That covers the realistic threat (opportunistic theft at a race/locker room) without hardware cost.

**Q3: Reflash via USB.**
**There is no USB data path.** The N1 board's USB-C is charge-only (D+/D− not even routed, NC; no SAMD11 bridge — deliberately omitted rev A). So "reflash via USB" is physically impossible on the product. The only firmware entry points:
- **BLE OTA (MCUmgr SMP)**: images must be **RSA-signed** (MCUboot dual-slot, swap-on-boot, already running since 2026-11-02). A thief cannot push unsigned firmware. Could he push SIGNED firmware? Only if he has the signing key — he doesn't; only we/JP hold it. But: is the SMP server gated by pairing? If OTA is open without bond, a thief could at least DOS the device (upload attempts fail signature → rejected, but they could fill/abort). So OTA should sit behind the same PIN/bond gate.
- **SWD (J3 header)**: physical debug port. Mitigation: nRF52833 **APPROTECT** (enable in production builds → SWD dead until mass-erase). Plus the header requires opening the enclosure. With APPROTECT + internal flash keys, stolen-device data extraction becomes lab-grade effort. Also UICR can store... runs are in external SPI flash — readable by SWD if not protected; APPROTECT kills SWD so external flash is then only reachable by desoldering/clip. Good enough.
- Data at rest: runs in MX25R external flash unencrypted — for a sports chrono, acceptable; note as accepted risk unless JP wants flash encryption later (nRF CryptoCell-312 on 52833 could do AES on the wire... overkill).

So the USB answer is short and strong: no USB data lines exist; charge-only. Theft-reflash threat = BLE OTA only → RSA-signed (already deployed) + gate SMP behind pairing.

Also relate to F42: the phone-side factory reset fits here — factory reset does NOT unbond ownership in cloud (or does it clear PIN? decide: factory reset wipes pairing bond + config, but the cloud ownership record persists keyed by device serial — so a thief who somehow factory-resets still can't re-register it to his account; the original owner can release it from his account).

I should also record decisions and where they'll live: requirements (I-requirements / F-series?), the security section in system design... There's likely a pairing/security spec somewhere? Memory: "Pairing UI waits 2nd Nicla (Nov budget)" — pairing UI in app planned. I'll propose concrete additions:
- New requirement: pairing via 6-digit PIN printed in battery bay (or configurable at first setup, shown in app, user writes it down?) — hmm, printing requires manufacturing step. Alternative: first-connect sets the PIN (blank from factory: first app that connects sets PIN + becomes owner; phone change needs PIN which the OWNER knows because they set it). That's elegant: factory-fresh = unclaimed; first claim sets PIN; PIN needed for new phones. Thief of a claimed device needs the PIN the owner set.
- Cloud: device serial ↔ owner account binding; lock flag pushed on sync (needs I07 DB arc).
- FW: gate SMP/GATT-writes behind PIN-authenticated bond; keep RSA signing; enable APPROTECT in production Kconfig.

Let me check the repo quickly for any existing pairing/security spec to anchor file names — a quick grep. Then write the response. JP's message is a design discussion — answer thoroughly but concisely, give recommendations, ask for GO to write into requirements. Maybe minimal tool use: one grep to find where pairing is specced (app lane F45? "connected-session policy (v6.8, app lane)"). Don't overdo it.

content.thinking:
Very important discovery — the existing docs ALREADY specify:
- **F39**: LE Secure Connections, **Just Works** pairing, bond on first connection, bond in **RAM only** (not persisted to flash!) — "no persistent bond storage", re-pairs automatically on total drain.
- **F42 currently**: 5-presses-in-3s → factory reset (clear bond, default name, ERASE ALL RUN DATA). This is EXACTLY the on-device reset JP now wants to move to the phone! So F42 needs the rewrite we discussed — and now his three questions interact with it.
- **F40**: OTA signed via imgtool — signature level not explicitly RSA in the req text ("signed (imgtool)") but memory says RSA-signed MCUboot (2026-11-02 arc: "MCUboot dual-slot (RSA-signed, swap-on-boot)"). So RSA in practice.

The RAM-bond design is interesting: bond lost on total battery drain, auto re-pair Just Works. That means TODAY the security model is essentially: Just Works (no MITM protection), bond stored in RAM, and ANY phone can bond when no bond exists. That answers Q1 today: yes trivially (any phone can connect — there's no access control at all beyond "first-come bonds"), but it also means Q2/Q3 protection is weak: a thief's phone just bonds (if the bond is in RAM and present, does the device reject a second phone? Nordic bonding: with a bond, the device expects the bonded peer's keys; a new phone attempting to bond — depends on security mode; usually device with existing bond will reject new pairing unless bond deleted or pairing mode enabled. With Just Works + single bond slot, second phone typically can't pair until bond cleared).

So current state: phone change = requires clearing bond = factory reset (5-press) → erases ALL RUNS. That's the exact pain JP intuits with Q1. Our new F42 (phone-side) must NOT be the only way to unpair — a user without the old phone can't reach the phone-side reset either... wait, phone-side reset is done from THE paired phone. New phone can't connect. So we NEED an on-device unpair path that is NOT the destructive factory reset! Hmm!

Re-think: 
- Factory reset (phone): wipe config+runs option — fine from the OWNED phone.
- Phone change: need "unpair / transfer ownership" WITHOUT wiping runs. Options:
  a) PIN approach (my earlier proposal): replace Just Works bonding-only with PIN-based access: device shows no UI, PIN printed/set at first claim. New phone: enter PIN → device drops old bond, bonds new phone, runs intact. This solves Q1 cleanly without data loss.
  b) On-device pairing mode: presses in SLEEP → pairing window. But frustrated-hammering risk + we only have a 20ms-1s piezo pulse... a "5 presses → LED flashes BLUE → pairing mode 60s" would collide with the F42 5-press gesture (being removed to phone — freed!). Actually since F42 moves to phone, the 5-press gesture is FREE to become "pairing mode". But hammering risk: 5 quick presses in SLEEP from a frustrated user = enters pairing mode for 60s — mostly harmless (new phone still needs... if pairing mode allows ANY phone to bond, a nearby attacker during that window could bond. 60s window, physical proximity — acceptable? meh).
  c) Cloud ownership transfer (needs I07).

Best: PIN (owner-set at first claim, 6 digits, printed nowhere — owner sets it in app during setup; app requires re-enter to add a new phone). New phone flow: install app → connect → device says "bonded to another phone, enter PIN" → enter owner PIN → device rebonds. Lost PIN → on-device recovery: your 5-red-flash-5 two-stage (or since F42 moved: a LONG-ish on-device gesture that clears bond ONLY (keep runs): e.g., 5 presses → red flash → 5 presses = unbond + keep runs; full wipe only from phone). That maps JP's two-stage idea to "unpair" instead of "factory reset" — much better risk profile: worst case of accidental trigger = re-pair (annoying, not destructive).

Q2 theft: PIN gate means stolen device is unusable unless thief knows PIN; owner can re-pair with his PIN whenever (thief can't prevent). Cloud: device serial ↔ account binding, flag when device syncs under different account → lock-on-sync (needs I07). Also note: with PIN gate, "5-5" on-device unbond could let a thief unpair and then... he still needs the PIN to pair his phone (PIN survives unbond). So the on-device recovery doesn't leak: unbond clears the BOND, not the PIN. Lost-PIN recovery = the destructive path (phone unreachable? no phone CAN connect without PIN...). Hmm: lost PIN + no old phone → device locked forever except... that's when the 5-5 becomes "clear PIN and bond, keep runs"? If that exists, a thief can use 5-5 to clear PIN → defeats Q2. Trade-off: 
- If 5-5 clears PIN+bond keeping runs: thief CAN take over (defeats theft protection, but keeps owner data private-ish... no, thief gets runs).
- If 5-5 clears bond only (PIN persists): lost-PIN = RMA/warranty case (device comes back to us/JP, we SWD it). Acceptable for a sports device.

Recommendation: PIN persists; lost PIN = support case (SWD reflash at the bench). This keeps theft protection real.

Q3 USB: NO USB DATA PATH EXISTS (charge-only; D+/D− NC; SAMD11 omitted). So reflash-via-USB is physically impossible. Firmware entry points: BLE OTA only (RSA-signed, imgtool, F40) → gate SMP behind PIN/bond. SWD: enable nRF52833 APPROTECT in production (Kconfig/UTVCARE... NRF_APPROTECT = "protected" via UICR) → SWD dead; plus opening enclosure. Data at rest in external flash unencrypted — accepted risk (sports data), note it.

Also relay: F42 rewrite affects sgc_system_design.md:97 (state table row) + F42 in requirements + I12 mentions. I'll propose the full requirement change set and offer to write it. JP said "Your proposal is good" = GO for the F42 phone-side reset. So I should now WRITE the F42 rewrite + the security answers into the docs? That's substantive doc surgery across requirements v-next + system design. Given turn economics, I'll answer the design questions (that's what he asked: "Let's think about how to treat...") and propose the doc changes, asking ONE decision: PIN persists across lost-PIN (support-case recovery) vs PIN clearable on-device. Actually I can make that recommendation and let him veto. Better: write the reply with clear recommendations + the one open point (lost-PIN policy), and offer to write docs once he confirms. Keep it tight.

content.text:
Answers grounded in what our device actually is — and one discovery from the docs that changes the picture:

**First, a fact that matters for all three: today's design has no access control at all beyond "first phone to bond wins"** (F39: Just Works, bond kept in **RAM only** — it even silently re-pairs after a deep battery drain). And the current F42 (5-press reset) *erases all runs*. So your Q1 today would be: new phone can't connect, and the only unlock is a gesture that destroys the athlete's data. Both need fixing together.

## Q1 — Athlete changes phone

**PIN-based ownership.** At first setup, the owner's app sets a 6-digit **device PIN** (stored in device config flash — that's persistent, unlike the bond). Any later phone: connect → app says "this SGC belongs to someone, enter PIN" → device drops the old RAM bond, bonds the new phone, **runs intact**. No dependence on the old phone, no data loss. A coach/second phone can be added the same way.

Pairing this with the F42 change we just agreed:
- **5 presses → red flash → 5 presses** (your two-stage) becomes **"unbond"** — clears the bond *only*, keeps runs and PIN. Worst case if a frustrated user ever triggers it accidentally: re-enter your PIN. Annoying, never destructive. That's the right gesture-to-consequence mapping.
- **Factory reset** (wipe config, optional runs wipe) lives in the app only, as agreed.

## Q2 — Theft

Three layers, in order of value:

1. **The PIN is the real lock.** A stolen SGC that demands a PIN is a brick to the thief — he can't pair, can't arm, can't read. Critically, the on-device unbond gesture clears the *bond*, **not the PIN** — so a thief can't take it over by pressing buttons.
2. **Cloud, exactly as you suggest** (this becomes a REQ-DB/I07 feature): device serial ↔ owner account binding at first claim. If the device ever syncs runs from a different account — or the owner reports it stolen — the backend flags the serial and pushes a **lock** on next sync. That's LoJack: not preventing local misuse, but making resale traceable. Needs the remote-DB arc to exist, so it's phase-2, documented now.
3. Physical reality check: the battery bay opens with a screwdriver, so hardware-level unclonability is not worth chasing on a sports timer. PIN + cloud traceability covers the realistic threat (opportunistic theft at a race) at zero BOM cost.

## Q3 — Reflash via USB

**There is no USB data path to attack.** This is the payoff of the decision you took on Tuesday: the SAMD11 bridge is omitted from rev A, and the USB-C connector is **charge-only** — D+/D− are not even routed (NC on J1). A thief with a USB cable can do exactly one thing: charge his stolen device.

That leaves two real firmware entry points, both already covered:
- **BLE OTA**: MCUboot with RSA-signed images (imgtool, proven on the bench in the 0.24.x arc). Unsigned/mis-signed firmware is rejected and the old slot boots — F40's S3 acceptance already tests this. One gap to close: the SMP service should sit **behind the same PIN/bond gate** so a thief can't even attempt uploads.
- **SWD (J3)**: physical, requires opening the enclosure. Production builds should enable nRF52833 **APPROTECT** (UICR) — debug port dead until mass-erase, which also wipes the keys. After that, extracting runs from the external flash means desoldering a chip; for sports data that's an accepted risk (we note it, we don't encrypt).

## The one decision left

**Lost PIN + old phone gone → device is locked.** Recovery = warranty/support case: the device comes back to you, gets SWD-reflashed at the bench. The alternative (an on-device gesture that clears the PIN) would hand thieves exactly the takeover path Q2 is meant to close. I recommend the hard line — it's a rare case, and support-reflash is clean.

Say go and I'll write it all into the docs: F42 rewritten (phone-side reset), new F-series entries for PIN ownership + unbond gesture + SMP gating + APPROTECT, and the cloud lock-flag as a REQ-DB item — one commit, ready for your review.

1. "Not sure to understand the advantage of unbinding" — he questions why the on-device unbond gesture exists at all. Good challenge. Let me think honestly: with PIN-based ownership, is unbond needed on-device?

The unbond gesture's purpose was: a recovery path when something goes wrong with the BLE bond (bond corrupted, RAM bond lost + ... wait if bond lost, new phone can just bond with PIN). Actually with PIN:

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.
