| 2 | CELL | GND ("MAX17048: Not internally connected") |
| 3 | VDD | **VBAT** ("MAX17048: Voltage sense input. Connect to positive battery terminal") + **0.1 µF** ("Bypass with 0.1 µF to GND") |
| 4 | GND | GND ("negative battery terminal") |
| 5 | ALRT | "Open-Drain, Active-Low Alert Output" → 10 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **P0.21** (module pin 26). Wired for firmware freedom; use v2-optional per AD-029 |
| 6 | QSTRT | GND ("Connect to GND if not used") |
| 7 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) — "I2C Clock Input" (fixed addr **0x36**, per ADI datasheet/AD-029) |
| 8 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| EP | — | GND |

**Note (OD-12):** verify MAX17048 VIH accepts 1.8 V pull-ups with VDD=VBAT (datasheet fetch was bot-blocked; pin table above is from the ADI datasheet text). BQ25120A VIH = 0.825 V and IS31FL3194 VIH ≤ 1.4 V are already 1.8 V-safe.

### 4.3 RGB LED (Nicla stock) + SK6812 strip (SGC)

**IS31FL3194-CLS2-TR (WLCSP-8)** + ROHM **SMLP34RGB2W3** LED (exact Nicla BOM, ABX00050 schematic U8/DL1):

| IS31 pin (datasheet Pin Description) | Connection |
|---|---|
| A1 SDB | "Shutdown the chip when pulled to low" → **V_PMID** (always-enabled; control via I²C) — Nicla SDB net **TBD-JP** (confirm on ABX00050 schematic at capture; do not guess) |
| A2 VCC | **V_PMID** (Nicla parity: U8 powered from PMID; IS31 VCC range 2.7–5.5 V covers 3.0–5.0 V battery/input) + 0.1 µF (value **TBD-JP** — typical-app figure is graphical; confirm vs Lumissil EVB/Nicla) |
| B1 SDA / C1 SCL | &i2c0 (P0.15/P0.16) — fixed 7-bit address **"101 0011" = 0x53**, no strap pins |
| B2/C2/D2 OUT1–OUT3 | SMLP34RGB2W3 R/G/B anodes (current-sink outputs; no resistors) |
| D1 GND | GND |

**SK6812-mini ×5** (SGC strip, P0.19): DIN ← P0.19 **through a 5 V-logic level translator** (boost rail is 5 V; SK6812 VIH ≈ 0.7·VDD — 1.8 V drive is insufficient). Dual-supply translator, VCCA=+1V8/VCCB=+5V, TXB0102/TXS0102-class — **part TBD-JP** (OD-9). Per-LED 0.1 µF; strip supply = +5V boost (hardware doc §7: full brightness for P1+).

### 4.4 Sensor cluster (Nicla replica — copy ABX00050 nets at capture)

- **BHI260AP** (44-pad LGA, 3.6×4.1×0.83 mm): HSCX pad 33 → P0.03 (SCK); HSDX pad 11 → P0.04 (MOSI); HSDO pad 32 → P0.05 (MISO); HCSB pad 34 → P0.31 (CS — "SPI mode"); HIRQ pad 10 → P0.14; **RESETN pad 9 → P0.13** (moved, C3; pad is "Input, Pull-Up, Reset input, active low"). VDD 1.71–3.6 V, **VDDIO 1.71–1.89 V** → both to +1V8 rail (this hard-pins the 1.8 V architecture — no 3.3 V sensor bus possible). Decoupling per Nicla bank: 1 µF + 100 nF ×3–4 (C5/C6/C7/C12/C13).
- **BMM150** (U4) + **BMP390L** (U3) + **BME688** (U6): sub-sensors on BHI260AP master port M1 (BMM150 SCK/SDI ← M1SCX/M1SDX; BMP390L via MCSB1; BME688 via MCSB2 per ABX00050 pinout). **Per-ball wiring = copy Nicla schematic verbatim at capture** — exact M1/M2/M3 pin assignment of the BHI cluster is a Nicla-internal net list; mark as "copy reference" in capture. BMP390L: 10-pin LGA (1 VDDIO, 2 SCK, 3 VSS, 4 SDI, 5 SDO, …, CSB; CSB→VDDIO selects I²C — here SPI to BHI).
- **BME688 populate-vs-DNP**: firmware never reads it → **OD-6** (footprint retained either way; Nicla parity = populate).
- **U2 "BHI Flash" MX25R1635FZUIH0** (Nicla U2, +1V8): BHI260AP QSPI (CLK/CS/D0–D3) — **⚠ missing from BOM v4.3** — BHY2 sensor firmware lives here (Arduino_BHY2 upload path). Must be added (OD-5).

### 4.5 Data flash — MX25R6435F (U7, SOIC-8 200 mil; pin config verbatim from Macronix v1.6)

| Pin | Name | Net |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CS# | P0.26 (&spi2 hardware CS reg 0) |
| 2 | SO/SIO1 | P0.05 (MISO/CIPO) |
| 3 | WP#/SIO2 | NC (datasheet Note 1: "will remain internal pull up function while this pin is not physically connected") |
| 4 | GND | GND |
| 5 | SI/SIO0 | P0.04 (MOSI/COPI) |
| 6 | SCLK | P0.03 |
| 7 | RESET#/SIO3 or HOLD#/SIO3 | NC (same internal-pull-up note) |
| 8 | VCC | +1V8 + 100 nF |

RawRunStore 8 MB layout per hardware doc (pre-roll 0x0000–0x13FFF etc.) unchanged. U7 supply at +1V8 = Nicla parity (schematic shows U7 on +1V8).

### 4.6 DNP footprints (v2)

- **LDC1612** (WSON-12): SCL 1 / SDA 2 / CLKIN 3 / ADDR 4 → GND (**0x2A**, "when ADDR=L, I2C address = 0x2A") / INTB 5 → BUTTON net P0.02 ("Push-pull output; does not require pull-up") / SD 6 → GND / VDD 7 (+100 nF) / GND 8 / IN0A 9, IN0B 10 (coil ch.0; 14 mm spiral, footprint retained) / IN1A 11, IN1B 12 → GND or 2nd coil pads. Sensor-bus (&i2c1) placement per docs.
- **RV-3028-C7 RTC @ 0x52** on &i2c1: 7-pin C7 footprint, /INT → TP (unconnected test point, no GPIO steal — per hardware doc §2 I²C map + TOOLS notes). Exact pad map per Micro Crystal datasheet at capture (DNP — not fetched this pass).
- Beeper BZ1 (DNP): P0.09 via 100 Ω/NPN footprint retained.

| C4 | Nicla's VDDIO_EXT header rail (BQ LS/LDO, programmable 1.8–3.3 V per ABX00050 pinout) has **no consumer on P1** (no external header, no level translators) | LS/LDO unused: LSCTRL → GND (disabled), LS/LDO pin → 1 µF to GND (stability, §7 pin table), VINLS → SYS (per SLUSD08A §9.3: "If the output of the LDO is less than the programmed V(SYS) voltage, connect VINLS to SYS") | none |

---

## 4. Per-subsystem net lists

### 4.1 Charger subsystem — BQ25120A (YFP 25-ball DSBGA; ball map verbatim from SLUSD08A §7)

| Ball | Name | Net / connection |
|---|---|---|
| A2 | IN | VBUS_USB (USB-C VBUS) + **C_IN 1 µF** ("Bypass IN to GND with at least 1 µF") |
| A3, B3 | PMID | V_PMID + **C_PMID ≥3 µF** ("at least 3 µF… as close as possible"; Nicla uses 4.7 µF C10) → IS31FL3194 VCC, CD pull-up rail |
| A1, D5 | GND | GND |
| A5 | PGND | GND (buck hot loop; output cap to this ground per §7) |
| A4 | SW | L1 **2.2 µH** (Nicla: MLZ1608A2R2WT000) → PGND side; SYS sense |
| B5 | SYS | **+1V8 rail** + **C_SYS ≥4.7 µF** (Nicla: C15 10 µF) — buck default **1.8 V** (SYS_VOUT "1.8 V through 3.3 V selection", default per §7 table "BQ25120A Enabled 1.8 V Load Switch") |
| B1, B2 | BAT | VBAT (cell +) + **C_BAT ≥1 µF** |
| C3 | TS | NTC net: **R_HI from VBUS/driver to TS**, **R_LO TS→GND**, pack NTC (TS→GND) per Fig. 18 + Eq. 1–2. R_HI/R_LO values **TBD-JP** (need Renata NTC R25/B constants; JEITA thresholds V(COLD/COOL/WARM/HOT) per datasheet) |
| C1 | ISET | **R_ISET = 1.82 kΩ 1%** → ICHG = K(ISET)/R(ISET) = 200/1820 ≈ **110 mA** (Table 5, KISET typ 200 AΩ; task-given 110 mA) |
| C2 | ILIM | **R_ILIM = 1.0 kΩ 1%** → 200 mA (Table 4 row "0.19/0.2/0.21 A — 1000 Ω") |
| D1 | IPRETERM | **4.99 kΩ** → termination/pre-charge = 10 % of ISET ≈ 11 mA (Table 3 row 10 % → 4990 Ω) |
| D2 | INT | open-drain status → 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **NC on MCU** (charging bit read from FAULTS reg over I²C, per AD-029 firmware note); TP |
| D3 | RESET | NC (BQ's MR-reset output unused on P1 — Nicla's "P0.18→MR" net dropped, see C3) |
| D4 | /PG | TP only (optional 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8) |
| E1 | /MR | NC (internal logic handles; ship mode via I²C/CD per OD-8 decision) |
| E2 | /CD | **P0.08** (module pin 50) + **100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID** — pull-up guarantees active mode at cold boot (CD has internal 900 kΩ pull-down; CD low + battery-only = Hi-Z). OD-8 |
| E3 | LSCTRL | GND (LS/LDO disabled — no consumer, C4) |
| E4 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| E5 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) |
| C4, B4 | VINLS | → SYS (rule §9.3 quoted in C4) + 1 µF |
| C5 | LS/LDO | 1 µF to GND, otherwise NC |

VBATREG note: default register = **4.2 V** (§7 table "4.2 V" battery-regulation default; VBREG equation "VBATREG = 3.6 V + VBREGCODE × 10 mV", charge range 3.6–4.65 V) — correct for the cell; no divider/resistor needed.

### 4.2 Fuel gauge — MAX17048G+T10 (TDFN-8; pin functions verbatim from ADI datasheet Pin Description table)

| Pin | Name | Connection |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CTG | GND ("Connect to Ground") |
| 2 | CELL | GND ("MAX17048: Not internally connected") |
| 3 | VDD | **VBAT** ("MAX17048: Voltage sense input. Connect to positive battery terminal") + **0.1 µF** ("Bypass with 0.1 µF to GND") |
| 4 | GND | GND ("negative battery terminal") |
| 5 | ALRT | "Open-Drain, Active-Low Alert Output" → 10 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **P0.21** (module pin 26). Wired for firmware freedom; use v2-optional per AD-029 |
| 6 | QSTRT | GND ("Connect to GND if not used") |
| 7 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) — "I2C Clock Input" (fixed addr **0x36**, per ADI datasheet/AD-029) |
| 8 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| EP | — | GND |

**Note (OD-12):** verify MAX17048 VIH accepts 1.8 V pull-ups with VDD=VBAT (datasheet fetch was bot-blocked; pin table above is from the ADI datasheet text). BQ25120A VIH = 0.825 V and IS31FL3194 VIH ≤ 1.4 V are already 1.8 V-safe.

### 4.3 RGB LED (Nicla stock) + SK6812 strip (SGC)

**IS31FL3194-CLS2-TR (WLCSP-8)** + ROHM **SMLP34RGB2W3** LED (exact Nicla BOM, ABX00050 schematic U8/DL1):

| IS31 pin (datasheet Pin Description) | Connection |
|---|---|
| A1 SDB | "Shutdown the chip when pulled to low" → **V_PMID** (always-enabled; control via I²C) — Nicla SDB net **TBD-JP** (confirm on ABX00050 schematic at capture; do not guess) |
| A2 VCC | **V_PMID** (Nicla parity: U8 powered from PMID; IS31 VCC range 2.7–5.5 V covers 3.0–5.0 V battery/input) + 0.1 µF (value **TBD-JP** — typical-app figure is graphical; confirm vs Lumissil EVB/Nicla) |
| B1 SDA / C1 SCL | &i2c0 (P0.15/P0.16) — fixed 7-bit address **"101 0011" = 0x53**, no strap pins |
| B2/C2/D2 OUT1–OUT3 | SMLP34RGB2W3 R/G/B anodes (current-sink outputs; no resistors) |
| D1 GND | GND |

**SK6812-mini ×5** (SGC strip, P0.19): DIN ← P0.19 **through a 5 V-logic level translator** (boost rail is 5 V; SK6812 VIH ≈ 0.7·VDD — 1.8 V drive is insufficient). Dual-supply translator, VCCA=+1V8/VCCB=+5V, TXB0102/TXS0102-class — **part TBD-JP** (OD-9). Per-LED 0.1 µF; strip supply = +5V boost (hardware doc §7: full brightness for P1+).

### 4.4 Sensor cluster (Nicla replica — copy ABX00050 nets at capture)

- **BHI260AP** (44-pad LGA, 3.6×4.1×0.83 mm): HSCX pad 33 → P0.03 (SCK); HSDX pad 11 → P0.04 (MOSI); HSDO pad 32 → P0.05 (MISO); HCSB pad 34 → P0.31 (CS — "SPI mode"); HIRQ pad 10 → P0.14; **RESETN pad 9 → P0.13** (moved, C3; pad is "Input, Pull-Up, Reset input, active low"). VDD 1.71–3.6 V, **VDDIO 1.71–1.89 V** → both to +1V8 rail (this hard-pins the 1.8 V architecture — no 3.3 V sensor bus possible). Decoupling per Nicla bank: 1 µF + 100 nF ×3–4 (C5/C6/C7/C12/C13).
- **BMM150** (U4) + **BMP390L** (U3) + **BME688** (U6): sub-sensors on BHI260AP master port M1 (BMM150 SCK/SDI ← M1SCX/M1SDX; BMP390L via MCSB1; BME688 via MCSB2 per ABX00050 pinout). **Per-ball wiring = copy Nicla schematic verbatim at capture** — exact M1/M2/M3 pin assignment of the BHI cluster is a Nicla-internal net list; mark as "copy reference" in capture. BMP390L: 10-pin LGA (1 VDDIO, 2 SCK, 3 VSS, 4 SDI, 5 SDO, …, CSB; CSB→VDDIO selects I²C — here SPI to BHI).
- **BME688 populate-vs-DNP**: firmware never reads it → **OD-6** (footprint retained either way; Nicla parity = populate).
- **U2 "BHI Flash" MX25R1635FZUIH0** (Nicla U2, +1V8): BHI260AP QSPI (CLK/CS/D0–D3) — **⚠ missing from BOM v4.3** — BHY2 sensor firmware lives here (Arduino_BHY2 upload path). Must be added (OD-5).

### 4.5 Data flash — MX25R6435F (U7, SOIC-8 200 mil; pin config verbatim from Macronix v1.6)

| Pin | Name | Net |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CS# | P0.26 (&spi2 hardware CS reg 0) |
| 2 | SO/SIO1 | P0.05 (MISO/CIPO) |
| 3 | WP#/SIO2 | NC (datasheet Note 1: "will remain internal pull up function while this pin is not physically connected") |
| 4 | GND | GND |
| 5 | SI/SIO0 | P0.04 (MOSI/COPI) |
| 6 | SCLK | P0.03 |
| 7 | RESET#/SIO3 or HOLD#/SIO3 | NC (same internal-pull-up note) |
| 8 | VCC | +1V8 + 100 nF |

RawRunStore 8 MB layout per hardware doc (pre-roll 0x0000–0x13FFF etc.) unchanged. U7 supply at +1V8 = Nicla parity (schematic shows U7 on +1V8).

### 4.6 DNP footprints (v2)

- **LDC1612** (WSON-12): SCL 1 / SDA 2 / CLKIN 3 / ADDR 4 → GND (**0x2A**, "when ADDR=L, I2C address = 0x2A") / INTB 5 → BUTTON net P0.02 ("Push-pull output; does not require pull-up") / SD 6 → GND / VDD 7 (+100 nF) / GND 8 / IN0A 9, IN0B 10 (coil ch.0; 14 mm spiral, footprint retained) / IN1A 11, IN1B 12 → GND or 2nd coil pads. Sensor-bus (&i2c1) placement per docs.
- **RV-3028-C7 RTC @ 0x52** on &i2c1: 7-pin C7 footprint, /INT → TP (unconnected test point, no GPIO steal — per hardware doc §2 I²C map + TOOLS notes). Exact pad map per Micro Crystal datasheet at capture (DNP — not fetched this pass).
- Beeper BZ1 (DNP): P0.09 via 100 Ω/NPN footprint retained.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

| 6 | ANT | — | bridge to pin 5 | 50 Ω interface; internal-antenna bridge |

**Not available on the module (Table 4 complete):** nRF **P0.24, P0.25** do not appear in any row. Everything else we use is present.

### 3.3 Conflicts, risks, firmware impact

| ID | Finding | Resolution in this spec | FW impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | **P0.24 absent** — hardware doc §10 assigns Boost EN = P0.24 (v1) / RFID_EN = P0.24 (v2) | Boost EN → **P0.17** (module pin 49). v2 RFID_EN → P0.17 likewise (or P0.06/P0.12) | `boost_en` pin change in config/overlay |
| C2 | **P0.25 absent** — hardware doc §2 assigns BQ CD = P0.25 | CD → **P0.08** (module pin 50) + 100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID so the board always boots active (CD low + battery-only = BQ Hi-Z ship mode = dead board). See OD-8 | `bq_cd` pin change |
| C3 | **Module RESET_N = P0.18** (fixed) vs Nicla's BHI260AP RESET on P0.18 (app.overlay pulses it low at bring-up; hardware doc §2 "P0.18 → BQ25120 MR reset network") | BHI RESETN → **P0.13** (module pin 52), pull-up retained. Do **not** wire anything external to pin 12 except SWD/TP. (The Nicla's "P0.18 → BQ MR" net is dropped — MR unused on P1, see §4.1) | overlay: BHI reset-gpios 18 → 13 |
| R1 | P0.03 (SPI SCK) carries Table 4 remark "standard drive, low-frequency I/O only… avoid using these pins for high-speed digital interfaces… Digital noise on these pins can reduce radio sensitivity" — vs app.overlay's 16 MHz BHI SPI | Keep Nicla-parity routing (function locked to the proven design); mitigation documented: if RF sensitivity regressions appear in bench S03/S04, drop SPI clock (BHI works at 8/4 MHz) and re-test. Decision point at EMC/range bench — JP informed | optional `spi-max-frequency` reduction |
| R2 | P0.19 (SK6812 data, 800 kHz NZR) carries the same "low frequency I/O only" remark | Same treatment as R1; the strip is 3 mm from the antenna zone — also see §4.9 keepout. Fallback alternative: move strip to a full-drive GPIO (P0.06/P0.12) with zero Nicla-parity loss (SK6812 is an SGC peripheral, not a Nicla part) — JP call (OD-9b) | overlay pin change if moved |
| C4 | Nicla's VDDIO_EXT header rail (BQ LS/LDO, programmable 1.8–3.3 V per ABX00050 pinout) has **no consumer on P1** (no external header, no level translators) | LS/LDO unused: LSCTRL → GND (disabled), LS/LDO pin → 1 µF to GND (stability, §7 pin table), VINLS → SYS (per SLUSD08A §9.3: "If the output of the LDO is less than the programmed V(SYS) voltage, connect VINLS to SYS") | none |

## 4. Per-subsystem net lists

### 4.1 Charger subsystem — BQ25120A (YFP 25-ball DSBGA; ball map verbatim from SLUSD08A §7)

| Ball | Name | Net / connection |
|---|---|---|
| A2 | IN | VBUS_USB (USB-C VBUS) + **C_IN 1 µF** ("Bypass IN to GND with at least 1 µF") |
| A3, B3 | PMID | V_PMID + **C_PMID ≥3 µF** ("at least 3 µF… as close as possible"; Nicla uses 4.7 µF C10) → IS31FL3194 VCC, CD pull-up rail |
| A1, D5 | GND | GND |
| A5 | PGND | GND (buck hot loop; output cap to this ground per §7) |
| A4 | SW | L1 **2.2 µH** (Nicla: MLZ1608A2R2WT000) → PGND side; SYS sense |
| B5 | SYS | **+1V8 rail** + **C_SYS ≥4.7 µF** (Nicla: C15 10 µF) — buck default **1.8 V** (SYS_VOUT "1.8 V through 3.3 V selection", default per §7 table "BQ25120A Enabled 1.8 V Load Switch") |
| B1, B2 | BAT | VBAT (cell +) + **C_BAT ≥1 µF** |
| C3 | TS | NTC net: **R_HI from VBUS/driver to TS**, **R_LO TS→GND**, pack NTC (TS→GND) per Fig. 18 + Eq. 1–2. R_HI/R_LO values **TBD-JP** (need Renata NTC R25/B constants; JEITA thresholds V(COLD/COOL/WARM/HOT) per datasheet) |
| C1 | ISET | **R_ISET = 1.82 kΩ 1%** → ICHG = K(ISET)/R(ISET) = 200/1820 ≈ **110 mA** (Table 5, KISET typ 200 AΩ; task-given 110 mA) |
| C2 | ILIM | **R_ILIM = 1.0 kΩ 1%** → 200 mA (Table 4 row "0.19/0.2/0.21 A — 1000 Ω") |
| D1 | IPRETERM | **4.99 kΩ** → termination/pre-charge = 10 % of ISET ≈ 11 mA (Table 3 row 10 % → 4990 Ω) |
| D2 | INT | open-drain status → 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **NC on MCU** (charging bit read from FAULTS reg over I²C, per AD-029 firmware note); TP |
| D3 | RESET | NC (BQ's MR-reset output unused on P1 — Nicla's "P0.18→MR" net dropped, see C3) |
| D4 | /PG | TP only (optional 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8) |
| E1 | /MR | NC (internal logic handles; ship mode via I²C/CD per OD-8 decision) |
| E2 | /CD | **P0.08** (module pin 50) + **100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID** — pull-up guarantees active mode at cold boot (CD has internal 900 kΩ pull-down; CD low + battery-only = Hi-Z). OD-8 |
| E3 | LSCTRL | GND (LS/LDO disabled — no consumer, C4) |
| E4 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| E5 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) |
| C4, B4 | VINLS | → SYS (rule §9.3 quoted in C4) + 1 µF |
| C5 | LS/LDO | 1 µF to GND, otherwise NC |

|---|---|---|
| 1 | CTG | GND ("Connect to Ground") |

**IS31FL3194-CLS2-TR (WLCSP-8)** + ROHM **SMLP34RGB2W3** LED (exact Nicla BOM, ABX00050 schematic U8/DL1):

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

But MCUboot says "no valid image header in primary". If slot0 = 0x10000 and my hex has the MCUboot image header at 0x10000, it should boot. KEY INSIGHT from the first data record: `:1000000000000000...` — first 16 bytes at 0x10000 are ALL ZEROS. An MCUboot image header starts with magic (0x96F3B83D little-endian → bytes 3D B8 F3 96) — NOT zeros. That's consistent with "Padding image section 0 at 0x000102dc" — content really begins ~0x102dc.

content.text:
All three of your items, done:

## 1) Flashed — and one honest stumble along the way

My first flash used the wrong artifact: the build produces **two** hexes, and I flashed the raw app one (no MCUboot header). Result: MCUboot refused to boot it and just sat in the bootloader — harmless, nothing was lost, but that's why there were two flash rounds. The correct file is **`zephyr.signed.hex`** (it starts with the MCUboot magic `3DB8F396` — I verified before reflashing). Second flash: clean boot, RSA verified, and the banner shows the goods:

```
SGC app-03 pull_proto v0.25.0
button: arming input P0.02 ready (F03, piezo single-press, state-gated)
```

All 36 stored runs and your config survived — the device is fully healthy on 0.25.0.

**What's left is literally one finger:** press the bench button once while it's in SLEEP. Expected: instant arm, serial prints `{"ev":"button_arm","src":"piezo"}` — no 1-second hold. Then press while ARMED: ignored, `button press in state 1 ignored`. That completes the acceptance test.

## 2) The quiet window, in plain words

A real piezo button doesn't close *once* — the element physically rings, so one press can look like 2–3 rapid electrical pulses (press, ring, release). If the firmware counted each pulse, one tap could register as multiple presses. So: **after a valid press is accepted, anything arriving within the next 200 ms is ignored.** One physical press = one command, no matter how much the element rings. (Debounce's 20 ms handles the clean part; the 200 ms is the belt on top.)

## 3) The SSH key — explained and fixed

The problem: OpenSSH **refuses to use a private key that other users on the machine can read** — it's a theft protection (a copied key shouldn't work). Your `id_ed25519_sgc` had inherited broad Windows permissions, so SSH silently ignored it and fell back to another key (that's why connections still worked despite the scary warning). Fixed with `icacls`: removed inheritance, granted read to **you only**. The warning should be gone on your next pull.

One small footnote I noticed in the banner: the MCUboot *header* still says version 0.24.7 (it's set by the build's signing config, separate from `app_version.h`). Doesn't affect anything today — the app reports 0.25.0 correctly — but before the next phone-OTA I should bump that signing version too, or the updater's comparison could get confused. My first flash used the wrong artifact: the build produces **two** hexes, and I flashed the raw app one (no MCUboot header). ## 2) The quiet window, in plain words

A real piezo button doesn't close *once* — the element physically rings, so one press can look like 2–3 rapid electrical pulses (press, ring, release). If the firmware counted each pulse, one tap could register as multiple presses. So: **after a valid press is accepted, anything arriving within the next 200 ms is ignored.** One physical press = one command, no matter how much the element rings. (Debounce's 20 ms handles the clean part; the 200 ms is the belt on top.)

The problem: OpenSSH **refuses to use a private key that other users on the machine can read** — it's a theft protection (a copied key shouldn't work). ## 1) Flashed — and one honest stumble along the way

My first flash used the wrong artifact: the build produces **two** hexes, and I flashed the raw app one (no MCUboot header). Result: MCUboot refused to boot it and just sat in the bootloader — harmless, nothing was lost, but that's why there were two flash rounds. The correct file is **`zephyr.signed.hex`** (it starts with the MCUboot magic `3DB8F396` — I verified before reflashing). Second flash: clean boot, RSA verified, and the banner shows the goods:


All 36 stored runs and your config survived — the device is fully healthy on 0.25.0.

**What's left is literally one finger:** press the bench button once while it's in SLEEP. Expected: instant arm, serial prints `{"ev":"button_arm","src":"piezo"}` — no 1-second hold. Then press while ARMED: ignored, `button press in state 1 ignored`. That completes the acceptance test.

## 2) The quiet window, in plain words

A real piezo button doesn't close *once* — the element physically rings, so one press can look like 2–3 rapid electrical pulses (press, ring, release). If the firmware counted each pulse, one tap could register as multiple presses. So: **after a valid press is accepted, anything arriving within the next 200 ms is ignored.** One physical press = one command, no matter how much the element rings. (Debounce's 20 ms handles the clean part; the 200 ms is the belt on top.)

## 3) The SSH key — explained and fixed

The problem: OpenSSH **refuses to use a private key that other users on the machine can read** — it's a theft protection (a copied key shouldn't work). Your `id_ed25519_sgc` had inherited broad Windows permissions, so SSH silently ignored it and fell back to another key (that's why connections still worked despite the scary warning). Fixed with `icacls`: removed inheritance, granted read to **you only**. The warning should be gone on your next pull.

One small footnote I noticed in the banner: the MCUboot *header* still says version 0.24.7 (it's set by the build's signing config, separate from `app_version.h`). Doesn't affect anything today — the app reports 0.25.0 correctly — but before the next phone-OTA I should bump that signing version too, or the updater's comparison could get confused. ## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)

   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

**CONFIRMED: the Zephyr app implements NO `?` status command.** Its serial set: D, s, B, H, W, S, a/g/e, b, d, y, x, w. The Arduino-era harness (`{"ev":"status"}` handshake via `?`) simply doesn't match the Zephyr app's protocol.

So the S04–S06 "device suite" is **Arduino-era tooling, incompatible with the Zephyr app** — NOT a regression from my button change. The failing handshake would have failed on 0.24.7 identically. (These tests were for the pre-Zephyre firmware — catalog header says "FW baseline 5.01".)

So what IS the right smoke test for the Zephyr app? What worked historically on the Zephyr bench:
- Serial: 'a' (arm), 'g' (go/log), 'e' (end), 's' (sleep), 'd' (dump/download), 'b' (battery), 'D' (capture), 'V'? 
- The boot banner itself: "recorder: ready (a=arm g=go e=end, own workqueue)".
- Phone: connect via app, list runs, download.

A Zephyr-app smoke via serial that I can drive myself:
1. Send 'b' → expect battery JSON
2. Send 'a' → ARMED event
3. Send 'g' → LOGGING (b1_rate nonzero rates = sensors live!)
4. Wait ~10 s
5. Send 'e' → POST_RUN/end
6. Check run list grew ('d'? listing via... the listing is the L lines / run list on boot; serial 'd' downloads a run)
7. Send 's' → SLEEP

I need a serial SENDER. zserial.py = capture only. Write a small driver script on JP-PC (staged via echo lines? Ugh — node can't write files on PC directly... but I CAN create it via git: write the script on the VPS repo, commit, JP-PC pulls, run it. That's the clean relay path! ~30 s overhead.)

Better: check if a suitable tool already exists — repo tools: relay_fetch.py, run_cycle.py (!), dump_run.py, decode_packed.py, checkdump.py, golden_check.py. "run_cycle.py" sounds EXACTLY like an arm/go/end cycle driver. Check its content (it's in Firmware_Zephyr/tools/ on the VPS).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bench run cycle: arm → go → N s → end; capture serial to log.
Usage: py run_cycle.py <seconds> <out.log> [port]
"""
import sys
import time

import serial

secs = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 30
out = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'cycle.log'
port = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 'COM3'

s = serial.Serial(port, 115200, timeout=1)
time.sleep(2)
s.reset_input_buffer()
s.write(b'a\n')
time.sleep(2)
s.write(b'g\n')
time.sleep(secs)
s.write(b'e\n')
time.sleep(15)
d = s.read(200000)
# keep reading a bit for POST_RUN->IDLE lines
t0 = time.time()
while time.time() - t0 < 10:
    d += s.read(20000)
    if b'run_ready' in d:
        break
open(out, 'wb').write(d)
print(len(d), 'bytes ->', out)

One honest detour first: the catalog's S04–S06 suite **couldn't run** — those tests are Arduino-era tooling that handshakes with a `?` status command the Zephyr app never implemented. That "failure" is protocol mismatch, not a regression (it would fail identically on 0.24.7). The Zephyr-native driver turned out to be `run_cycle.py`, and it exercised everything that matters:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **State machine** | ✅ SLEEP → ARMED → LOGGING → POST_RUN (flatline detector fired) → SLEEP (`run_ready`) |
| **Sensor pipeline** | ✅ **99/100 Hz** rotation vector + linear acc, baro at 113 756 Pa (your real Valais altitude), temp live, **err:0, short:0** |

| 11 | GPIO_11 | P0.14 | BHI260AP HIRQ | General purpose I/O |
| 13 | GPIO_13 | P1.09 | Spare | |
| 14 | GPIO_14 | P0.11 | v2 user-SPI SCK (NC v1) | |
| 15 | GPIO_15 | P0.12 | Spare | |
| 16 | SWO/GPIO_16 | P1.00 | SWO → SWD connector (optional) | "Serial Wire debug trace data output" |
| 1 | ANT_PCB | — | antenna counterpoise net | corner placement → "GND pattern"; middle-of-side → NC (SIM Table 4) |
| 2, 3 | ANT_GND1, ANT_GND2 | — | antenna counterpoise net | middle-of-side → "GND pattern"; corner → NC (SIM Table 4) |
| 5 | ANT_INT | — | bridge to pin 6 | "Connect to pin 6 – ANT" for internal antenna |
| 6 | ANT | — | bridge to pin 5 | 50 Ω interface; internal-antenna bridge |

**Not available on the module (Table 4 complete):** nRF **P0.24, P0.25** do not appear in any row. Everything else we use is present.

### 3.3 Conflicts, risks, firmware impact

| ID | Finding | Resolution in this spec | FW impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | **P0.24 absent** — hardware doc §10 assigns Boost EN = P0.24 (v1) / RFID_EN = P0.24 (v2) | Boost EN → **P0.17** (module pin 49). v2 RFID_EN → P0.17 likewise (or P0.06/P0.12) | `boost_en` pin change in config/overlay |
| C2 | **P0.25 absent** — hardware doc §2 assigns BQ CD = P0.25 | CD → **P0.08** (module pin 50) + 100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID so the board always boots active (CD low + battery-only = BQ Hi-Z ship mode = dead board). See OD-8 | `bq_cd` pin change |
| C3 | **Module RESET_N = P0.18** (fixed) vs Nicla's BHI260AP RESET on P0.18 (app.overlay pulses it low at bring-up; hardware doc §2 "P0.18 → BQ25120 MR reset network") | BHI RESETN → **P0.13** (module pin 52), pull-up retained. Do **not** wire anything external to pin 12 except SWD/TP. (The Nicla's "P0.18 → BQ MR" net is dropped — MR unused on P1, see §4.1) | overlay: BHI reset-gpios 18 → 13 |
| R1 | P0.03 (SPI SCK) carries Table 4 remark "standard drive, low-frequency I/O only… avoid using these pins for high-speed digital interfaces… Digital noise on these pins can reduce radio sensitivity" — vs app.overlay's 16 MHz BHI SPI | Keep Nicla-parity routing (function locked to the proven design); mitigation documented: if RF sensitivity regressions appear in bench S03/S04, drop SPI clock (BHI works at 8/4 MHz) and re-test. Decision point at EMC/range bench — JP informed | optional `spi-max-frequency` reduction |
| R2 | P0.19 (SK6812 data, 800 kHz NZR) carries the same "low frequency I/O only" remark | Same treatment as R1; the strip is 3 mm from the antenna zone — also see §4.9 keepout. Fallback alternative: move strip to a full-drive GPIO (P0.06/P0.12) with zero Nicla-parity loss (SK6812 is an SGC peripheral, not a Nicla part) — JP call (OD-9b) | overlay pin change if moved |
| C4 | Nicla's VDDIO_EXT header rail (BQ LS/LDO, programmable 1.8–3.3 V per ABX00050 pinout) has **no consumer on P1** (no external header, no level translators) | LS/LDO unused: LSCTRL → GND (disabled), LS/LDO pin → 1 µF to GND (stability, §7 pin table), VINLS → SYS (per SLUSD08A §9.3: "If the output of the LDO is less than the programmed V(SYS) voltage, connect VINLS to SYS") | none |

---

## 4. Per-subsystem net lists

### 4.1 Charger subsystem — BQ25120A (YFP 25-ball DSBGA; ball map verbatim from SLUSD08A §7)

| Ball | Name | Net / connection |
|---|---|---|
| A2 | IN | VBUS_USB (USB-C VBUS) + **C_IN 1 µF** ("Bypass IN to GND with at least 1 µF") |
| A3, B3 | PMID | V_PMID + **C_PMID ≥3 µF** ("at least 3 µF… as close as possible"; Nicla uses 4.7 µF C10) → IS31FL3194 VCC, CD pull-up rail |
| A1, D5 | GND | GND |
| A5 | PGND | GND (buck hot loop; output cap to this ground per §7) |
| A4 | SW | L1 **2.2 µH** (Nicla: MLZ1608A2R2WT000) → PGND side; SYS sense |
| B5 | SYS | **+1V8 rail** + **C_SYS ≥4.7 µF** (Nicla: C15 10 µF) — buck default **1.8 V** (SYS_VOUT "1.8 V through 3.3 V selection", default per §7 table "BQ25120A Enabled 1.8 V Load Switch") |
| B1, B2 | BAT | VBAT (cell +) + **C_BAT ≥1 µF** |
| C3 | TS | NTC net: **R_HI from VBUS/driver to TS**, **R_LO TS→GND**, pack NTC (TS→GND) per Fig. 18 + Eq. 1–2. R_HI/R_LO values **TBD-JP** (need Renata NTC R25/B constants; JEITA thresholds V(COLD/COOL/WARM/HOT) per datasheet) |
| C1 | ISET | **R_ISET = 1.82 kΩ 1%** → ICHG = K(ISET)/R(ISET) = 200/1820 ≈ **110 mA** (Table 5, KISET typ 200 AΩ; task-given 110 mA) |
| C2 | ILIM | **R_ILIM = 1.0 kΩ 1%** → 200 mA (Table 4 row "0.19/0.2/0.21 A — 1000 Ω") |
| D1 | IPRETERM | **4.99 kΩ** → termination/pre-charge = 10 % of ISET ≈ 11 mA (Table 3 row 10 % → 4990 Ω) |
| D2 | INT | open-drain status → 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **NC on MCU** (charging bit read from FAULTS reg over I²C, per AD-029 firmware note); TP |
| D3 | RESET | NC (BQ's MR-reset output unused on P1 — Nicla's "P0.18→MR" net dropped, see C3) |
| D4 | /PG | TP only (optional 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8) |
| E1 | /MR | NC (internal logic handles; ship mode via I²C/CD per OD-8 decision) |
| E2 | /CD | **P0.08** (module pin 50) + **100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID** — pull-up guarantees active mode at cold boot (CD has internal 900 kΩ pull-down; CD low + battery-only = Hi-Z). OD-8 |
| E3 | LSCTRL | GND (LS/LDO disabled — no consumer, C4) |
| E4 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| E5 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) |
| C4, B4 | VINLS | → SYS (rule §9.3 quoted in C4) + 1 µF |
| C5 | LS/LDO | 1 µF to GND, otherwise NC |

VBATREG note: default register = **4.2 V** (§7 table "4.2 V" battery-regulation default; VBREG equation "VBATREG = 3.6 V + VBREGCODE × 10 mV", charge range 3.6–4.65 V) — correct for the cell; no divider/resistor needed.

### 4.2 Fuel gauge — MAX17048G+T10 (TDFN-8; pin functions verbatim from ADI datasheet Pin Description table)

| Pin | Name | Connection |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CTG | GND ("Connect to Ground") |
| 2 | CELL | GND ("MAX17048: Not internally connected") |
| 3 | VDD | **VBAT** ("MAX17048: Voltage sense input. Connect to positive battery terminal") + **0.1 µF** ("Bypass with 0.1 µF to GND") |
| 4 | GND | GND ("negative battery terminal") |
| 5 | ALRT | "Open-Drain, Active-Low Alert Output" → 10 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **P0.21** (module pin 26). Wired for firmware freedom; use v2-optional per AD-029 |
| 6 | QSTRT | GND ("Connect to GND if not used") |
| 7 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) — "I2C Clock Input" (fixed addr **0x36**, per ADI datasheet/AD-029) |
| 8 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| EP | — | GND |

**Note (OD-12):** verify MAX17048 VIH accepts 1.8 V pull-ups with VDD=VBAT (datasheet fetch was bot-blocked; pin table above is from the ADI datasheet text). BQ25120A VIH = 0.825 V and IS31FL3194 VIH ≤ 1.4 V are already 1.8 V-safe.

### 4.3 RGB LED (Nicla stock) + SK6812 strip (SGC)

**IS31FL3194-CLS2-TR (WLCSP-8)** + ROHM **SMLP34RGB2W3** LED (exact Nicla BOM, ABX00050 schematic U8/DL1):

| IS31 pin (datasheet Pin Description) | Connection |
|---|---|
| A1 SDB | "Shutdown the chip when pulled to low" → **V_PMID** (always-enabled; control via I²C) — Nicla SDB net **TBD-JP** (confirm on ABX00050 schematic at capture; do not guess) |
| A2 VCC | **V_PMID** (Nicla parity: U8 powered from PMID; IS31 VCC range 2.7–5.5 V covers 3.0–5.0 V battery/input) + 0.1 µF (value **TBD-JP** — typical-app figure is graphical; confirm vs Lumissil EVB/Nicla) |
| B1 SDA / C1 SCL | &i2c0 (P0.15/P0.16) — fixed 7-bit address **"101 0011" = 0x53**, no strap pins |
| B2/C2/D2 OUT1–OUT3 | SMLP34RGB2W3 R/G/B anodes (current-sink outputs; no resistors) |
| D1 GND | GND |

**SK6812-mini ×5** (SGC strip, P0.19): DIN ← P0.19 **through a 5 V-logic level translator** (boost rail is 5 V; SK6812 VIH ≈ 0.7·VDD — 1.8 V drive is insufficient). Dual-supply translator, VCCA=+1V8/VCCB=+5V, TXB0102/TXS0102-class — **part TBD-JP** (OD-9). Per-LED 0.1 µF; strip supply = +5V boost (hardware doc §7: full brightness for P1+).

### 4.4 Sensor cluster (Nicla replica — copy ABX00050 nets at capture)

- **BHI260AP** (44-pad LGA, 3.6×4.1×0.83 mm): HSCX pad 33 → P0.03 (SCK); HSDX pad 11 → P0.04 (MOSI); HSDO pad 32 → P0.05 (MISO); HCSB pad 34 → P0.31 (CS — "SPI mode"); HIRQ pad 10 → P0.14; **RESETN pad 9 → P0.13** (moved, C3; pad is "Input, Pull-Up, Reset input, active low"). VDD 1.71–3.6 V, **VDDIO 1.71–1.89 V** → both to +1V8 rail (this hard-pins the 1.8 V architecture — no 3.3 V sensor bus possible). Decoupling per Nicla bank: 1 µF + 100 nF ×3–4 (C5/C6/C7/C12/C13).
- **BMM150** (U4) + **BMP390L** (U3) + **BME688** (U6): sub-sensors on BHI260AP master port M1 (BMM150 SCK/SDI ← M1SCX/M1SDX; BMP390L via MCSB1; BME688 via MCSB2 per ABX00050 pinout). **Per-ball wiring = copy Nicla schematic verbatim at capture** — exact M1/M2/M3 pin assignment of the BHI cluster is a Nicla-internal net list; mark as "copy reference" in capture. BMP390L: 10-pin LGA (1 VDDIO, 2 SCK, 3 VSS, 4 SDI, 5 SDO, …, CSB; CSB→VDDIO selects I²C — here SPI to BHI).
- **BME688 populate-vs-DNP**: firmware never reads it → **OD-6** (footprint retained either way; Nicla parity = populate).
- **U2 "BHI Flash" MX25R1635FZUIH0** (Nicla U2, +1V8): BHI260AP QSPI (CLK/CS/D0–D3) — **⚠ missing from BOM v4.3** — BHY2 sensor firmware lives here (Arduino_BHY2 upload path). Must be added (OD-5).

### 4.5 Data flash — MX25R6435F (U7, SOIC-8 200 mil; pin config verbatim from Macronix v1.6)

| Pin | Name | Net |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CS# | P0.26 (&spi2 hardware CS reg 0) |
| 2 | SO/SIO1 | P0.05 (MISO/CIPO) |
| 3 | WP#/SIO2 | NC (datasheet Note 1: "will remain internal pull up function while this pin is not physically connected") |
| 4 | GND | GND |
| 5 | SI/SIO0 | P0.04 (MOSI/COPI) |
| 6 | SCLK | P0.03 |
| 7 | RESET#/SIO3 or HOLD#/SIO3 | NC (same internal-pull-up note) |
| 8 | VCC | +1V8 + 100 nF |

RawRunStore 8 MB layout per hardware doc (pre-roll 0x0000–0x13FFF etc.) unchanged. U7 supply at +1V8 = Nicla parity (schematic shows U7 on +1V8).

### 4.6 DNP footprints (v2)

- **LDC1612** (WSON-12): SCL 1 / SDA 2 / CLKIN 3 / ADDR 4 → GND (**0x2A**, "when ADDR=L, I2C address = 0x2A") / INTB 5 → BUTTON net P0.02 ("Push-pull output; does not require pull-up") / SD 6 → GND / VDD 7 (+100 nF) / GND 8 / IN0A 9, IN0B 10 (coil ch.0; 14 mm spiral, footprint retained) / IN1A 11, IN1B 12 → GND or 2nd coil pads. Sensor-bus (&i2c1) placement per docs.
- **RV-3028-C7 RTC @ 0x52** on &i2c1: 7-pin C7 footprint, /INT → TP (unconnected test point, no GPIO steal — per hardware doc §2 I²C map + TOOLS notes). Exact pad map per Micro Crystal datasheet at capture (DNP — not fetched this pass).

### 3.3 Conflicts, risks, firmware impact

| ID | Finding | Resolution in this spec | FW impact |

| C2 | **P0.25 absent** — hardware doc §2 assigns BQ CD = P0.25 | CD → **P0.08** (module pin 50) + 100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID so the board always boots active (CD low + battery-only = BQ Hi-Z ship mode = dead board). See OD-8 | `bq_cd` pin change |
| C3 | **Module RESET_N = P0.18** (fixed) vs Nicla's BHI260AP RESET on P0.18 (app.overlay pulses it low at bring-up; hardware doc §2 "P0.18 → BQ25120 MR reset network") | BHI RESETN → **P0.13** (module pin 52), pull-up retained. ## 4. Per-subsystem net lists

### 4.1 Charger subsystem — BQ25120A (YFP 25-ball DSBGA; ball map verbatim from SLUSD08A §7)

| Ball | Name | Net / connection |
|---|---|---|
| A2 | IN | VBUS_USB (USB-C VBUS) + **C_IN 1 µF** ("Bypass IN to GND with at least 1 µF") |
| A3, B3 | PMID | V_PMID + **C_PMID ≥3 µF** ("at least 3 µF… as close as possible"; Nicla uses 4.7 µF C10) → IS31FL3194 VCC, CD pull-up rail |
| A1, D5 | GND | GND |
| A5 | PGND | GND (buck hot loop; output cap to this ground per §7) |
| A4 | SW | L1 **2.2 µH** (Nicla: MLZ1608A2R2WT000) → PGND side; SYS sense |
| B5 | SYS | **+1V8 rail** + **C_SYS ≥4.7 µF** (Nicla: C15 10 µF) — buck default **1.8 V** (SYS_VOUT "1.8 V through 3.3 V selection", default per §7 table "BQ25120A Enabled 1.8 V Load Switch") |
| B1, B2 | BAT | VBAT (cell +) + **C_BAT ≥1 µF** |
| C3 | TS | NTC net: **R_HI from VBUS/driver to TS**, **R_LO TS→GND**, pack NTC (TS→GND) per Fig. 18 + Eq. 1–2. R_HI/R_LO values **TBD-JP** (need Renata NTC R25/B constants; JEITA thresholds V(COLD/COOL/WARM/HOT) per datasheet) |
| C1 | ISET | **R_ISET = 1.82 kΩ 1%** → ICHG = K(ISET)/R(ISET) = 200/1820 ≈ **110 mA** (Table 5, KISET typ 200 AΩ; task-given 110 mA) |
| C2 | ILIM | **R_ILIM = 1.0 kΩ 1%** → 200 mA (Table 4 row "0.19/0.2/0.21 A — 1000 Ω") |
| D1 | IPRETERM | **4.99 kΩ** → termination/pre-charge = 10 % of ISET ≈ 11 mA (Table 3 row 10 % → 4990 Ω) |
| D2 | INT | open-drain status → 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **NC on MCU** (charging bit read from FAULTS reg over I²C, per AD-029 firmware note); TP |
| D3 | RESET | NC (BQ's MR-reset output unused on P1 — Nicla's "P0.18→MR" net dropped, see C3) |
| D4 | /PG | TP only (optional 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8) |
| E1 | /MR | NC (internal logic handles; ship mode via I²C/CD per OD-8 decision) |
| E2 | /CD | **P0.08** (module pin 50) + **100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID** — pull-up guarantees active mode at cold boot (CD has internal 900 kΩ pull-down; CD low + battery-only = Hi-Z). OD-8 |
| E3 | LSCTRL | GND (LS/LDO disabled — no consumer, C4) |
| E4 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| E5 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) |

VBATREG note: default register = **4.2 V** (§7 table "4.2 V" battery-regulation default; VBREG equation "VBATREG = 3.6 V + VBREGCODE × 10 mV", charge range 3.6–4.65 V) — correct for the cell; no divider/resistor needed.

### 4.3 RGB LED (Nicla stock) + SK6812 strip (SGC)

**IS31FL3194-CLS2-TR (WLCSP-8)** + ROHM **SMLP34RGB2W3** LED (exact Nicla BOM, ABX00050 schematic U8/DL1):

| IS31 pin (datasheet Pin Description) | Connection |
|---|---|
| A1 SDB | "Shutdown the chip when pulled to low" → **V_PMID** (always-enabled; control via I²C) — Nicla SDB net **TBD-JP** (confirm on ABX00050 schematic at capture; do not guess) |
| A2 VCC | **V_PMID** (Nicla parity: U8 powered from PMID; IS31 VCC range 2.7–5.5 V covers 3.0–5.0 V battery/input) + 0.1 µF (value **TBD-JP** — typical-app figure is graphical; confirm vs Lumissil EVB/Nicla) |
| B1 SDA / C1 SCL | &i2c0 (P0.15/P0.16) — fixed 7-bit address **"101 0011" = 0x53**, no strap pins |
| B2/C2/D2 OUT1–OUT3 | SMLP34RGB2W3 R/G/B anodes (current-sink outputs; no resistors) |
| D1 GND | GND |

**SK6812-mini ×5** (SGC strip, P0.19): DIN ← P0.19 **through a 5 V-logic level translator** (boost rail is 5 V; SK6812 VIH ≈ 0.7·VDD — 1.8 V drive is insufficient). ## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

| A4, A9, B4, B9 | VBUS → VBUS_USB: **10 µF bulk at connector** (sgc_usb_c_charging_spec §1) + ESD (OD-13: PESD5V0U2UT vs TPD4E05U06) → BQ IN (+1 µF at ball) |
| A1, A12, B1, B12 + SHELL | GND (shell stitched to GND; TH shell stakes soldered for pull-out strength) |
| A5 (CC1) | 5.1 kΩ 1% → GND (Rd sink) |
| B5 (CC2) | 5.1 kΩ 1% → GND |
| A6/A7, B6/B7 (D+/D−) | NC (or future TP per spec §1) |
| A8/B8 (SBU1/2) | NC |

USB-IF note (BQ §9.3.13): inrush compliance assumes device input capacitance < 10 µF — our 10 µF bulk + 1 µF IN exceeds it → fine for our USB-A→C/legacy sourcing, note in quote package (OD-14).

### 4.8 Connectors & test points

- **Battery JST-3** (VBAT / GND / NTC): part **TBD-JP** — BOM v4.1 flags the connector provisional, varies with final cell pack. Pinout per ABX00050 pinout PDF (battery connector = VBAT/NTC/GND).
- **SWD**: SWDCLK (pin 41), SWDIO (pin 42), SWO (pin 16, optional), RESET_N (pin 12), VCC(+1V8) sense, GND. Style OD-2: Tag-Connect TC2050 footprint vs 2×5 1.27 mm Cortex Debug (EVK uses a 6-pin J-link needle adapter — either is defensible).
- **UART console TP**: TX P0.20 (module pin 10), RX P0.09 (module pin 22) — Nicla LPIO1/LPIO2 parity (ABX00050 pinout: "2/LPIO1/TX P0_20, 1/LPIO2/RX P0_09").
- **TP set** (OD-3): +1V8, +5V, VBAT, V_PMID, GND, BQ INT, SWD row, UART row, ALRT, LED-data.

### 4.9 Mechanical / antenna keepout (internal chip antenna; SIM UBX-21000517-R08 quotes)

- SIM Table 4 (p.13), internal antenna: pin 5 ANT_INT "Connect to pin 6 – ANT"; corner placement → pin 1 ANT_PCB = "GND pattern", ANT_GND1/2 NC; middle-of-side → pins 2+3 ANT_GND1/2 = "GND pattern", ANT_PCB NC. **Recommendation: module in a PCB corner** ("a corner location offers slightly better antenna performance", SIM §2.2.1).
- Keepout rule (SIM Appendix B, p.70, verbatim): "It is important not to route any traces in any layer in the antenna strip clearance area." — antenna strip = module edge + counterpoise region per SIM Figures 33–36; **no traces/vias in any layer** under/around the strip; counterpoise trace per the reference design.
- Certification caution (SIM App. B): "PCB layout must be identical to that provided by u-blox… The designer must use the stack-up provided by u-blox. RF traces on the carrier PCB are part of the certified design." → our 0.8 mm 4-layer stackup must be checked against the SIM reference stackup; if it differs, follow SIM App. B exactly or contact u-blox (flag in §8).
- Board outline: 22 × 55 mm, 4-layer, 0.8 mm, ENIG (hardware doc §9). BHI260AP antenna-adjacent and BMM150 keepouts (>10 mm from coil/RFID footprints) per hardware doc §9 table. SK6812 strip along top edge; button/LED face outward (§8).
- datasheet note: "The IC should be placed far away from the mobile antenna in order to prevent the EMI" (IS31FL3194 datasheet) — keep U8 clear of the module antenna strip.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

## Overview

 Build the future of connected devices – faster and smarter – with the Arduino Nesso N1.
Powered by the ESP32-C6 and developed with M5Stack, this ready-to-go device merges robust performance with the flexibility of Arduino’s open ecosystem. It supports Wi-Fi® 6, Bluetooth® 5.0, Thread, and LoRa® for multi-protocol communication across home, industrial, and remote environments.
A 1.14” touch display, programmable buttons, built-in IMU, IR transmitter, RGB LED, buzzer, and rechargeable battery make it an intuitive, interactive tool for IoT development. You can easily expand its capabilities through Grove and Qwiic connectors – compatible with Arduino Modulino nodes and third-party modules – as well as the whole M5Stack sensor-hat ecosystem, and seamlessly integrate it with Arduino Cloud for remote monitoring and data visualization.
With pre-assembled hardware, a sturdy enclosure, and support for Arduino IDE, MicroPython, and UIFlow, Nesso N1 removes setup friction so you can focus on bringing your ideas to life.

#### Key benefits

- Powerful connectivity in one device: Supports Wi-Fi® 6, Bluetooth® 5.0, Thread 1.4 and LoRa®.

- Ready to use, right out of the box: Comes pre-assembled in a robust enclosure with a rechargeable battery and display for immediate prototyping.

- Intuitive interaction: Touchscreen, programmable buttons, and onboard sensors simplify control and feedback.

- Plug-and-play expandability: Easily connect to Arduino Modulino nodes, M5Stack sensor-hat, Grove, and Qwiic modules for rapid project growth.

- Seamless software flexibility: Code using Arduino IDE, MicroPython, or UIFlow, and visualize data through Arduino Cloud dashboards.

- Built for speed and creativity: Skip mechanical design and setup time to focus on building smarter solutions faster.

#### Application examples to explore

- Smart homes and hubs: Create connected home control centers, transform IR-controlled devices into IoT-enabled appliances, or develop custom automation projects.

- Industrial automation: Use Nesso N1 as an edge node to monitor equipment, collect sensor data, or enable predictive maintenance across factory systems.

- Agriculture and environmental monitoring: Connect soil, weather, or irrigation sensors via Thread to support sustainable and data-driven farming.

- Education and research: Prototype multi-protocol IoT systems, collect and visualize real-time data, or use itas a flexible learning platform in STEM projects.

content.thinking:
Now I have the Nesso N1's full specs. Let me analyze honestly for SGC's use case (ski-gate chrono: 100 Hz sensor logging, BLE, battery, cold, IP67, 22×55mm custom target).

**Nesso N1:**
- MCU: ESP32-C6 (RISC-V HP 160 MHz + LP core), 512 KB SRAM, 16 MB NOR flash
- Radio: Wi-Fi 6, BLE 5.3, Thread 1.4, Zigbee, **LoRa (SX1262)**
- 1.14" touch display
- 2 buttons, RGB LED, buzzer, IR TX
- 6-axis IMU (unknown model — "6-axis IMU", likely a cheap BMI270/LSM6DSO class — NOT a BHI260AP smart sensor hub!)
- Qwiic + Grove connectors
- Built-in LiPo (capacity unknown, probably small)
- 18 × 45 mm, €47.58
- Enclosure: "robust enclosure" — consumer dev-kit grade, not IP67

**Nicla Sense ME (our P0):**
- nRF52832 (ARM Cortex-M4F), BLE 5
- BHI260AP smart sensor hub (THE key part — 100 Hz quaternion fusion ON-CHIP, our whole data pipeline is built on its virtual sensors), BMP390, BMM150, BME688
- 8 MB data flash + 2 MB BHI FW flash
- BQ25120A PMIC
- No display, no buttons (ESLOV header instead)
- ~€70-80 typical price

**SGC relevance analysis:**

Where Nesso N1 would look attractive:
1. **LoRa!** — that's the one genuinely interesting feature for SGC: long-range radio. Ski race timing across a valley: LoRa could stream gate-crossing timestamps to a base station without phone proximity. BUT our architecture doesn't use live streaming for timing — the device RECORDS autonomously and syncs later; start-gate sync is via phone/BLE. Adding LoRa would be a feature change (live coach view?), not a platform need.
2. Display + touch — for a ski chrono, gloves + cold make touch useless; our LED pattern + button design is deliberate.
3. Wi-Fi/Thread/Zigbee — irrelevant on a mountain.
4. 16 MB flash + 512 KB RAM — nice but our data lives in external 8 MB; we need ~90 KB/run.
5. Price €47.58 vs Nicla ~€70+.

Where it FAILS for SGC (decisive):
1. **No BHI260AP.** "6-axis IMU" is a dumb IMU — no on-chip fusion at 100 Hz with quaternion output. Our ENTIRE firmware (Arduino_BHY2 → Zephyr bhy2 driver, sensor IDs, quaternion frames, wake/sleep sensor management) is built on the BHI260AP's virtual sensor API. Moving to ESP32-C6 means rewriting the whole sensor stack AND losing the proven fusion quality.
2. **BLE 5.3 on ESP32-C6** — actually fine-ish, but our app + MCUmgr OTA + Nordic stack are proven on nRF52. MCUboot/SMP on ESP32 = esptool path, different security story (and v6.1 spec: APPROTECT, signed images — nRF-native).
3. **Power**: ESP32-C6 LP mode is not nRF52 System OFF class (µA). Our SLEEP budget ~55 µA with sensor wake; a display-bearing ESP32 kit won't touch that. Battery unknown.
4. **No barometer!** No BMP390 — altitude/airspeed ΔP start detection (our start detector uses pressure!) — wait, our F04 start detection uses pressure + IMU. Nesso N1 has NO pressure sensor at all. That alone kills it for us: our run-start detection (drop + pressure) and baro in every frame depend on it.
5. Size 18×45 vs our 22×55 target — similar class, but with display it's a different product.
6. Not IP67; no charging PMIC story for -20°C.

So: for SGC — no advantage. It's a smart-home/IoT dev kit, not a sensor-fusion logger. The one thing worth noting: LoRa (SX1262) — if a future feature needs long-range telemetry (race-central live timing?), the right move is adding a LoRa module to OUR board's v2 reserve (we have UWB/RFID v2 footprints reserved) or a LoRa USB dongle at the gate — not switching platforms.

Also worth stating: our custom board = the Nicla's exact sensor set + B402 (more RAM) + USB-C + piezo + IP67 + €27-62 BOM at volume — better than BOTH options for production. The Nesso N1 is interesting for other projects (home automation, the farm?, Clavalité hydropower monitoring? — actually for VYT/freelance IoT prototyping it's a nice toy; could mention that honestly).

No more tool calls needed — I have everything. Write the analysis. Keep it structured and honest. Mention the price point and the fact it's M5Stack co-developed.

## Nesso N1 vs Nicla Sense ME — different animals entirely

| | **Nicla Sense ME** (our P0) | **Nesso N1** (new, €47.58) |
|---|---|---|
| MCU | nRF52832, Cortex-M4F | ESP32-C6, **RISC-V** dual-core (160 MHz) |
| **The sensor that matters** | **BHI260AP smart hub** — on-chip fusion, 100 Hz quaternions, wake-on-motion | Generic "6-axis IMU" (dumb sensor, no fusion hub) |
| Pressure | **BMP390** | ❌ **none** |
| Mag / env | BMM150 + BME688 | ❌ none |
| Radio | BLE 5 | BLE 5.3 + **Wi-Fi 6 + Thread/Zigbee + LoRa (SX1262)** |
| Storage | 8 MB data + 2 MB BHI FW | 16 MB NOR (system) |
| UI | LED only | **1.14″ touch display**, 2 buttons, buzzer, IR TX |
| Battery/PMIC | BQ25120A, our JST-3 LiPo | Built-in LiPo, unknown capacity |
| Form | bare board | enclosed dev kit, 18×45 mm |

## For SGC specifically: no advantage — three disqualifiers

1. **No BHI260AP.** Our entire data pipeline — 100 Hz quaternion frames, virtual sensors, sensor wake/park management, the whole Zephyr `bhy2` stack — *is* the BHI260AP. The N1's generic IMU means rewriting the sensor core and losing proven fusion quality. This alone is a no.
2. **No barometer.** Our run-start detection uses pressure + IMU, and every frame carries baro. The N1 has no pressure sensor at all.
3. **Power and environment.** ESP32-C6 low-power mode is not nRF52 System-Off class; our budget is ~55 µA sleep with sensor wake. And it's a consumer dev-kit enclosure, not −20 °C / IP67 territory.

## The one genuinely interesting feature: LoRa

The SX1262 is the single thing worth a second thought — long-range telemetry across a ski slope could enable a *live* race-central view (gate crossing times streamed to the timing hut without phones). But even there, the right integration is **a LoRa module on our v2 reserve nets** (we already keep UWB/RFID footprints unpopulated) or a LoRa dongle at the gate — not a platform switch that costs us the sensor hub, the power budget, and the enclosure.

## Where it *would* shine

For what it actually is — a €48 smart-home / industrial IoT kit with display, multi-protocol radio and Grove/Qwiic expansion — it's a nice piece (Arduino × M5Stack co-development). If you ever want a quick dashboard node for **Clavalité monitoring** or home automation, it's a fun tool. It's just not a ski chrono.

**Verdict: our path stays as is.** The custom board already beats *both* products for this job: exact Nicla sensor set, B402 with double the RAM, USB-C charging, sealed piezo, IP67 target, ~€27 BOM at volume — all on firmware we just smoke-tested green.

assistantTexts: A new Arduino product — let me pull its specs before comparing (our docs amusingly also call our custom board "N1", so let's be careful with names):

I have its full spec sheet. Here's the honest analysis:

## Nesso N1 vs Nicla Sense ME — different animals entirely

| | **Nicla Sense ME** (our P0) | **Nesso N1** (new, €47.58) |
|---|---|---|
| MCU | nRF52832, Cortex-M4F | ESP32-C6, **RISC-V** dual-core (160 MHz) |
| **The sensor that matters** | **BHI260AP smart hub** — on-chip fusion, 100 Hz quaternions, wake-on-motion | Generic "6-axis IMU" (dumb sensor, no fusion hub) |
| Pressure | **BMP390** | ❌ **none** |
| Mag / env | BMM150 + BME688 | ❌ none |
| Radio | BLE 5 | BLE 5.3 + **Wi-Fi 6 + Thread/Zigbee + LoRa (SX1262)** |
| Storage | 8 MB data + 2 MB BHI FW | 16 MB NOR (system) |
| UI | LED only | **1.14″ touch display**, 2 buttons, buzzer, IR TX |
| Battery/PMIC | BQ25120A, our JST-3 LiPo | Built-in LiPo, unknown capacity |
| Form | bare board | enclosed dev kit, 18×45 mm |

## For SGC specifically: no advantage — three disqualifiers

1. **No BHI260AP.** Our entire data pipeline — 100 Hz quaternion frames, virtual sensors, sensor wake/park management, the whole Zephyr `bhy2` stack — *is* the BHI260AP. The N1's generic IMU means rewriting the sensor core and losing proven fusion quality. This alone is a no.
2. **No barometer.** Our run-start detection uses pressure + IMU, and every frame carries baro. The N1 has no pressure sensor at all.
3. **Power and environment.** ESP32-C6 low-power mode is not nRF52 System-Off class; our budget is ~55 µA sleep with sensor wake. And it's a consumer dev-kit enclosure, not −20 °C / IP67 territory.

## The one genuinely interesting feature: LoRa

The SX1262 is the single thing worth a second thought — long-range telemetry across a ski slope could enable a *live* race-central view (gate crossing times streamed to the timing hut without phones). But even there, the right integration is **a LoRa module on our v2 reserve nets** (we already keep UWB/RFID footprints unpopulated) or a LoRa dongle at the gate — not a platform switch that costs us the sensor hub, the power budget, and the enclosure.

## Where it *would* shine

For what it actually is — a €48 smart-home / industrial IoT kit with display, multi-protocol radio and Grove/Qwiic expansion — it's a nice piece (Arduino × M5Stack co-development). If you ever want a quick dashboard node for **Clavalité monitoring** or home automation, it's a fun tool. It's just not a ski chrono.

**Verdict: our path stays as is.** The custom board already beats *both* products for this job: exact Nicla sensor set, B402 with double the RAM, USB-C charging, sealed piezo, IP67 target, ~€27 BOM at volume — all on firmware we just smoke-tested green.

### 3.3 Conflicts, risks, firmware impact

| ID | Finding | Resolution in this spec | FW impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | **P0.24 absent** — hardware doc §10 assigns Boost EN = P0.24 (v1) / RFID_EN = P0.24 (v2) | Boost EN → **P0.17** (module pin 49). v2 RFID_EN → P0.17 likewise (or P0.06/P0.12) | `boost_en` pin change in config/overlay |
| C2 | **P0.25 absent** — hardware doc §2 assigns BQ CD = P0.25 | CD → **P0.08** (module pin 50) + 100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID so the board always boots active (CD low + battery-only = BQ Hi-Z ship mode = dead board). See OD-8 | `bq_cd` pin change |
| C3 | **Module RESET_N = P0.18** (fixed) vs Nicla's BHI260AP RESET on P0.18 (app.overlay pulses it low at bring-up; hardware doc §2 "P0.18 → BQ25120 MR reset network") | BHI RESETN → **P0.13** (module pin 52), pull-up retained. Do **not** wire anything external to pin 12 except SWD/TP. (The Nicla's "P0.18 → BQ MR" net is dropped — MR unused on P1, see §4.1) | overlay: BHI reset-gpios 18 → 13 |
| R1 | P0.03 (SPI SCK) carries Table 4 remark "standard drive, low-frequency I/O only… avoid using these pins for high-speed digital interfaces… Digital noise on these pins can reduce radio sensitivity" — vs app.overlay's 16 MHz BHI SPI | Keep Nicla-parity routing (function locked to the proven design); mitigation documented: if RF sensitivity regressions appear in bench S03/S04, drop SPI clock (BHI works at 8/4 MHz) and re-test. Decision point at EMC/range bench — JP informed | optional `spi-max-frequency` reduction |
| R2 | P0.19 (SK6812 data, 800 kHz NZR) carries the same "low frequency I/O only" remark | Same treatment as R1; the strip is 3 mm from the antenna zone — also see §4.9 keepout. Fallback alternative: move strip to a full-drive GPIO (P0.06/P0.12) with zero Nicla-parity loss (SK6812 is an SGC peripheral, not a Nicla part) — JP call (OD-9b) | overlay pin change if moved |
| C4 | Nicla's VDDIO_EXT header rail (BQ LS/LDO, programmable 1.8–3.3 V per ABX00050 pinout) has **no consumer on P1** (no external header, no level translators) | LS/LDO unused: LSCTRL → GND (disabled), LS/LDO pin → 1 µF to GND (stability, §7 pin table), VINLS → SYS (per SLUSD08A §9.3: "If the output of the LDO is less than the programmed V(SYS) voltage, connect VINLS to SYS") | none |

---

## 4. Per-subsystem net lists

### 4.1 Charger subsystem — BQ25120A (YFP 25-ball DSBGA; ball map verbatim from SLUSD08A §7)

| Ball | Name | Net / connection |
|---|---|---|
| A2 | IN | VBUS_USB (USB-C VBUS) + **C_IN 1 µF** ("Bypass IN to GND with at least 1 µF") |
| A3, B3 | PMID | V_PMID + **C_PMID ≥3 µF** ("at least 3 µF… as close as possible"; Nicla uses 4.7 µF C10) → IS31FL3194 VCC, CD pull-up rail |
| A1, D5 | GND | GND |
| A5 | PGND | GND (buck hot loop; output cap to this ground per §7) |
| A4 | SW | L1 **2.2 µH** (Nicla: MLZ1608A2R2WT000) → PGND side; SYS sense |
| B5 | SYS | **+1V8 rail** + **C_SYS ≥4.7 µF** (Nicla: C15 10 µF) — buck default **1.8 V** (SYS_VOUT "1.8 V through 3.3 V selection", default per §7 table "BQ25120A Enabled 1.8 V Load Switch") |
| B1, B2 | BAT | VBAT (cell +) + **C_BAT ≥1 µF** |
| C3 | TS | NTC net: **R_HI from VBUS/driver to TS**, **R_LO TS→GND**, pack NTC (TS→GND) per Fig. 18 + Eq. 1–2. R_HI/R_LO values **TBD-JP** (need Renata NTC R25/B constants; JEITA thresholds V(COLD/COOL/WARM/HOT) per datasheet) |
| C1 | ISET | **R_ISET = 1.82 kΩ 1%** → ICHG = K(ISET)/R(ISET) = 200/1820 ≈ **110 mA** (Table 5, KISET typ 200 AΩ; task-given 110 mA) |
| C2 | ILIM | **R_ILIM = 1.0 kΩ 1%** → 200 mA (Table 4 row "0.19/0.2/0.21 A — 1000 Ω") |
| D1 | IPRETERM | **4.99 kΩ** → termination/pre-charge = 10 % of ISET ≈ 11 mA (Table 3 row 10 % → 4990 Ω) |
| D2 | INT | open-drain status → 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **NC on MCU** (charging bit read from FAULTS reg over I²C, per AD-029 firmware note); TP |
| D3 | RESET | NC (BQ's MR-reset output unused on P1 — Nicla's "P0.18→MR" net dropped, see C3) |
| D4 | /PG | TP only (optional 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8) |
| E1 | /MR | NC (internal logic handles; ship mode via I²C/CD per OD-8 decision) |
| E2 | /CD | **P0.08** (module pin 50) + **100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID** — pull-up guarantees active mode at cold boot (CD has internal 900 kΩ pull-down; CD low + battery-only = Hi-Z). OD-8 |
| E3 | LSCTRL | GND (LS/LDO disabled — no consumer, C4) |
| E4 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| E5 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) |
| C4, B4 | VINLS | → SYS (rule §9.3 quoted in C4) + 1 µF |
| C5 | LS/LDO | 1 µF to GND, otherwise NC |

VBATREG note: default register = **4.2 V** (§7 table "4.2 V" battery-regulation default; VBREG equation "VBATREG = 3.6 V + VBREGCODE × 10 mV", charge range 3.6–4.65 V) — correct for the cell; no divider/resistor needed.

### 4.2 Fuel gauge — MAX17048G+T10 (TDFN-8; pin functions verbatim from ADI datasheet Pin Description table)

| Pin | Name | Connection |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CTG | GND ("Connect to Ground") |
| 2 | CELL | GND ("MAX17048: Not internally connected") |
| 3 | VDD | **VBAT** ("MAX17048: Voltage sense input. Connect to positive battery terminal") + **0.1 µF** ("Bypass with 0.1 µF to GND") |
| 4 | GND | GND ("negative battery terminal") |
| 5 | ALRT | "Open-Drain, Active-Low Alert Output" → 10 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **P0.21** (module pin 26). Wired for firmware freedom; use v2-optional per AD-029 |
| 6 | QSTRT | GND ("Connect to GND if not used") |
| 7 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) — "I2C Clock Input" (fixed addr **0x36**, per ADI datasheet/AD-029) |
| 8 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| EP | — | GND |

**Note (OD-12):** verify MAX17048 VIH accepts 1.8 V pull-ups with VDD=VBAT (datasheet fetch was bot-blocked; pin table above is from the ADI datasheet text). BQ25120A VIH = 0.825 V and IS31FL3194 VIH ≤ 1.4 V are already 1.8 V-safe.

### 4.3 RGB LED (Nicla stock) + SK6812 strip (SGC)

**IS31FL3194-CLS2-TR (WLCSP-8)** + ROHM **SMLP34RGB2W3** LED (exact Nicla BOM, ABX00050 schematic U8/DL1):

| IS31 pin (datasheet Pin Description) | Connection |
|---|---|
| A1 SDB | "Shutdown the chip when pulled to low" → **V_PMID** (always-enabled; control via I²C) — Nicla SDB net **TBD-JP** (confirm on ABX00050 schematic at capture; do not guess) |
| A2 VCC | **V_PMID** (Nicla parity: U8 powered from PMID; IS31 VCC range 2.7–5.5 V covers 3.0–5.0 V battery/input) + 0.1 µF (value **TBD-JP** — typical-app figure is graphical; confirm vs Lumissil EVB/Nicla) |
| B1 SDA / C1 SCL | &i2c0 (P0.15/P0.16) — fixed 7-bit address **"101 0011" = 0x53**, no strap pins |
| B2/C2/D2 OUT1–OUT3 | SMLP34RGB2W3 R/G/B anodes (current-sink outputs; no resistors) |
| D1 GND | GND |

**SK6812-mini ×5** (SGC strip, P0.19): DIN ← P0.19 **through a 5 V-logic level translator** (boost rail is 5 V; SK6812 VIH ≈ 0.7·VDD — 1.8 V drive is insufficient). Dual-supply translator, VCCA=+1V8/VCCB=+5V, TXB0102/TXS0102-class — **part TBD-JP** (OD-9). Per-LED 0.1 µF; strip supply = +5V boost (hardware doc §7: full brightness for P1+).

### 4.4 Sensor cluster (Nicla replica — copy ABX00050 nets at capture)

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

| B5 (CC2) | 5.1 kΩ 1% → GND |

USB-IF note (BQ §9.3.13): inrush compliance assumes device input capacitance < 10 µF — our 10 µF bulk + 1 µF IN exceeds it → fine for our USB-A→C/legacy sourcing, note in quote package (OD-14).

### 4.8 Connectors & test points

- **Battery JST-3** (VBAT / GND / NTC): part **TBD-JP** — BOM v4.1 flags the connector provisional, varies with final cell pack. Pinout per ABX00050 pinout PDF (battery connector = VBAT/NTC/GND).
- **SWD**: SWDCLK (pin 41), SWDIO (pin 42), SWO (pin 16, optional), RESET_N (pin 12), VCC(+1V8) sense, GND. Style OD-2: Tag-Connect TC2050 footprint vs 2×5 1.27 mm Cortex Debug (EVK uses a 6-pin J-link needle adapter — either is defensible).
- **UART console TP**: TX P0.20 (module pin 10), RX P0.09 (module pin 22) — Nicla LPIO1/LPIO2 parity (ABX00050 pinout: "2/LPIO1/TX P0_20, 1/LPIO2/RX P0_09").
- **TP set** (OD-3): +1V8, +5V, VBAT, V_PMID, GND, BQ INT, SWD row, UART row, ALRT, LED-data.

### 4.9 Mechanical / antenna keepout (internal chip antenna; SIM UBX-21000517-R08 quotes)

- SIM Table 4 (p.13), internal antenna: pin 5 ANT_INT "Connect to pin 6 – ANT"; corner placement → pin 1 ANT_PCB = "GND pattern", ANT_GND1/2 NC; middle-of-side → pins 2+3 ANT_GND1/2 = "GND pattern", ANT_PCB NC. **Recommendation: module in a PCB corner** ("a corner location offers slightly better antenna performance", SIM §2.2.1).
- Keepout rule (SIM Appendix B, p.70, verbatim): "It is important not to route any traces in any layer in the antenna strip clearance area." — antenna strip = module edge + counterpoise region per SIM Figures 33–36; **no traces/vias in any layer** under/around the strip; counterpoise trace per the reference design.
- Certification caution (SIM App. B): "PCB layout must be identical to that provided by u-blox… The designer must use the stack-up provided by u-blox. RF traces on the carrier PCB are part of the certified design." → our 0.8 mm 4-layer stackup must be checked against the SIM reference stackup; if it differs, follow SIM App. B exactly or contact u-blox (flag in §8).
- Board outline: 22 × 55 mm, 4-layer, 0.8 mm, ENIG (hardware doc §9). BHI260AP antenna-adjacent and BMM150 keepouts (>10 mm from coil/RFID footprints) per hardware doc §9 table. SK6812 strip along top edge; button/LED face outward (§8).
- datasheet note: "The IC should be placed far away from the mobile antenna in order to prevent the EMI" (IS31FL3194 datasheet) — keep U8 clear of the module antenna strip.

---

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.
