## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

## 4. Per-subsystem net lists

### 4.1 Charger subsystem — BQ25120A (YFP 25-ball DSBGA; ball map verbatim from SLUSD08A §7)

| Ball | Name | Net / connection |
|---|---|---|
| A2 | IN | VBUS_USB (USB-C VBUS) + **C_IN 1 µF** ("Bypass IN to GND with at least 1 µF") |
| A3, B3 | PMID | V_PMID + **C_PMID ≥3 µF** ("at least 3 µF… as close as possible"; Nicla uses 4.7 µF C10) → IS31FL3194 VCC, CD pull-up rail |
| A1, D5 | GND | GND |
| A5 | PGND | GND (buck hot loop; output cap to this ground per §7) |
| A4 | SW | L1 **2.2 µH** (Nicla: MLZ1608A2R2WT000) → PGND side; SYS sense |
| B5 | SYS | **+1V8 rail** + **C_SYS ≥4.7 µF** (Nicla: C15 10 µF) — buck default **1.8 V** (SYS_VOUT "1.8 V through 3.3 V selection", default per §7 table "BQ25120A Enabled 1.8 V Load Switch") |
| B1, B2 | BAT | VBAT (cell +) + **C_BAT ≥1 µF** |
| C3 | TS | NTC net: **R_HI from VBUS/driver to TS**, **R_LO TS→GND**, pack NTC (TS→GND) per Fig. 18 + Eq. 1–2. R_HI/R_LO values **TBD-JP** (need Renata NTC R25/B constants; JEITA thresholds V(COLD/COOL/WARM/HOT) per datasheet) |
| C1 | ISET | **R_ISET = 1.82 kΩ 1%** → ICHG = K(ISET)/R(ISET) = 200/1820 ≈ **110 mA** (Table 5, KISET typ 200 AΩ; task-given 110 mA) |
| C2 | ILIM | **R_ILIM = 1.0 kΩ 1%** → 200 mA (Table 4 row "0.19/0.2/0.21 A — 1000 Ω") |
| D1 | IPRETERM | **4.99 kΩ** → termination/pre-charge = 10 % of ISET ≈ 11 mA (Table 3 row 10 % → 4990 Ω) |
| D2 | INT | open-drain status → 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **NC on MCU** (charging bit read from FAULTS reg over I²C, per AD-029 firmware note); TP |
| D3 | RESET | NC (BQ's MR-reset output unused on P1 — Nicla's "P0.18→MR" net dropped, see C3) |
| D4 | /PG | TP only (optional 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8) |
| E1 | /MR | NC (internal logic handles; ship mode via I²C/CD per OD-8 decision) |
| E2 | /CD | **P0.08** (module pin 50) + **100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID** — pull-up guarantees active mode at cold boot (CD has internal 900 kΩ pull-down; CD low + battery-only = Hi-Z). OD-8 |
| E3 | LSCTRL | GND (LS/LDO disabled — no consumer, C4) |
| E4 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| E5 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) |
| C4, B4 | VINLS | → SYS (rule §9.3 quoted in C4) + 1 µF |
| C5 | LS/LDO | 1 µF to GND, otherwise NC |

| Pin | Name | Connection |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CTG | GND ("Connect to Ground") |
| 2 | CELL | GND ("MAX17048: Not internally connected") |
| 3 | VDD | **VBAT** ("MAX17048: Voltage sense input. Connect to positive battery terminal") + **0.1 µF** ("Bypass with 0.1 µF to GND") |
| 4 | GND | GND ("negative battery terminal") |
| 5 | ALRT | "Open-Drain, Active-Low Alert Output" → 10 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **P0.21** (module pin 26). Wired for firmware freedom; use v2-optional per AD-029 |
| 6 | QSTRT | GND ("Connect to GND if not used") |
| 7 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) — "I2C Clock Input" (fixed addr **0x36**, per ADI datasheet/AD-029) |
| 8 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| EP | — | GND |

**Note (OD-12):** verify MAX17048 VIH accepts 1.8 V pull-ups with VDD=VBAT (datasheet fetch was bot-blocked; pin table above is from the ADI datasheet text). BQ25120A VIH = 0.825 V and IS31FL3194 VIH ≤ 1.4 V are already 1.8 V-safe.

### 4.3 RGB LED (Nicla stock) + SK6812 strip (SGC)

**IS31FL3194-CLS2-TR (WLCSP-8)** + ROHM **SMLP34RGB2W3** LED (exact Nicla BOM, ABX00050 schematic U8/DL1):

| IS31 pin (datasheet Pin Description) | Connection |
|---|---|
| A1 SDB | "Shutdown the chip when pulled to low" → **V_PMID** (always-enabled; control via I²C) — Nicla SDB net **TBD-JP** (confirm on ABX00050 schematic at capture; do not guess) |
| A2 VCC | **V_PMID** (Nicla parity: U8 powered from PMID; IS31 VCC range 2.7–5.5 V covers 3.0–5.0 V battery/input) + 0.1 µF (value **TBD-JP** — typical-app figure is graphical; confirm vs Lumissil EVB/Nicla) |
| B1 SDA / C1 SCL | &i2c0 (P0.15/P0.16) — fixed 7-bit address **"101 0011" = 0x53**, no strap pins |
| B2/C2/D2 OUT1–OUT3 | SMLP34RGB2W3 R/G/B anodes (current-sink outputs; no resistors) |
| D1 GND | GND |

**SK6812-mini ×5** (SGC strip, P0.19): DIN ← P0.19 **through a 5 V-logic level translator** (boost rail is 5 V; SK6812 VIH ≈ 0.7·VDD — 1.8 V drive is insufficient). Dual-supply translator, VCCA=+1V8/VCCB=+5V, TXB0102/TXS0102-class — **part TBD-JP** (OD-9). Per-LED 0.1 µF; strip supply = +5V boost (hardware doc §7: full brightness for P1+).

### 4.4 Sensor cluster (Nicla replica — copy ABX00050 nets at capture)

- **BHI260AP** (44-pad LGA, 3.6×4.1×0.83 mm): HSCX pad 33 → P0.03 (SCK); HSDX pad 11 → P0.04 (MOSI); HSDO pad 32 → P0.05 (MISO); HCSB pad 34 → P0.31 (CS — "SPI mode"); HIRQ pad 10 → P0.14; **RESETN pad 9 → P0.13** (moved, C3; pad is "Input, Pull-Up, Reset input, active low"). VDD 1.71–3.6 V, **VDDIO 1.71–1.89 V** → both to +1V8 rail (this hard-pins the 1.8 V architecture — no 3.3 V sensor bus possible). Decoupling per Nicla bank: 1 µF + 100 nF ×3–4 (C5/C6/C7/C12/C13).

BMP390L: 10-pin LGA (1 VDDIO, 2 SCK, 3 VSS, 4 SDI, 5 SDO, …, CSB; CSB→VDDIO selects I²C — here SPI to BHI).

- **U2 "BHI Flash" MX25R1635FZUIH0** (Nicla U2, +1V8): BHI260AP QSPI (CLK/CS/D0–D3) — **⚠ missing from BOM v4.3** — BHY2 sensor firmware lives here (Arduino_BHY2 upload path). Must be added (OD-5).

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

| D3 | RESET | NC (BQ's MR-reset output unused on P1 — Nicla's "P0.18→MR" net dropped, see C3) |

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

**Leading hypothesis: the busy flag from the phone download is stuck.** Remember the sequence — your phone auto-connected during the smoke test and was **mid-download of run id=5** when you killed the app at 13:18. 1. **First, let the clock run to ~14:45** — if Android held the BLE link a while after the app kill, the "fresh 1 h window from disconnect" could legitimately end around then. If the blue stops by ~14:45, F12 works and it was just a late disconnect.

assistantTexts: On battery since ~13:25 and still blinking at 14:29 — that's overdue by any single-clock reading. Before calling it a bug, let me read every path that re-arms that timer and how VIN detection actually works:

The state machine says the OFF should have fired at ~14:18. The last suspect standing is `bq_on_vin` — if its poll doesn't refresh while disconnected, it stays at its last value (USB present) forever. Checking where it's written:
`bq_on_vin` only updates inside the battery read. The question that decides everything: does that read still happen when the phone is *gone*? Finding the poll driver:

The poll self-reschedules unconditionally (5 s connected / 30 s not) — so `bq_on_vin` *is* being refreshed on battery, and that theory is out. Working through the guards in `off_work_handler` with your blue-blink evidence (blue = advertising = genuinely disconnected, genuinely SLEEP):

| Guard at 14:18 | Verdict |
|---|---|
| connected? | ✗ — blue blink proves disconnected |
| state == SLEEP? | ✗ — yes, resting |
| **`pull_proto_busy()`?** | ⚠️ **the suspect** |
| on_vin? | ✗ — refreshed false every 30 s on battery |

**Leading hypothesis: the busy flag from the phone download is stuck.** Remember the sequence — your phone auto-connected during the smoke test and was **mid-download of run id=5** when you killed the app at 13:18. A force-stop mid-stream is the ugly way to end a session. The disconnect handler should clean the stream state ("both abort on disconnect anyway" says the comment), but if that path missed this case, the busy flag stays set → the 1 h timer fires, sees "busy", re-arms a fresh full window — **every hour, forever**. The device would look exactly like this: healthy blue blink that never goes dark.

## How we discriminate — two steps, no reflash

1. **First, let the clock run to ~14:45** — if Android held the BLE link a while after the app kill, the "fresh 1 h window from disconnect" could legitimately end around then. If the blue stops by ~14:45, F12 works and it was just a late disconnect.
2. **If still blinking at 14:45:** open the app, let it connect cleanly, then close/disconnect it normally. That clean session should reset the stream state. Wait the hour again — if it goes dark this time, we've **proven the bug**: an app killed mid-download permanently blocks System Off. That's a real cold-weather battery drain risk (skier's phone dies mid-sync → device never sleeps deep) and the fix is mine to make — force-clear the busy state on disconnect, or time out an aborted stream.

Either way you've found something worth knowing with this test. I can't probe the device from here (USB is out — by design of your test), but the source reading is exhausted and the hypothesis is testable with exactly those two steps. Tell me what the LED does.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │

assistantTexts: Noted — clean cycle done, verdict due ~19:15. While the clock runs, let me make the wait productive: reading exactly what `pull_proto_busy()` guards and whether the disconnect path clears it:

Disconnect cleanup is airtight (and blue-advertising proves `disconnected_cb` ran) — so the busy hypothesis is dead. Reading the `off_work_handler` body itself and the timer constant — no more guessing:
The handler is clean — but the disconnect cleanup snippet was cut right at the interesting line. `job_active = false` was followed by something for `dir_active`… reading the complete function:

The cleanup is airtight — both flags and the pending slot clear on every disconnect, and your blue-advertising proves the disconnect callback ran. So the `busy` theory is dead too. What remains, honestly ranked:

**1. `ble_config_on_vin()` is lying.** Its refresh only happens when the BQ25120A read *succeeds* — on the I²C-error path (`-4`), `bq_on_vin` keeps its last value, and the boot default is **true**. If I²C reads fail in deep SLEEP (or the faults-bit semantics are off), the device believes "on USB" forever and the guard re-arms every hour, forever. Symptom match: perfect.

**2. The timer itself isn't firing** (tickless/LFCLK issue) — less likely, RC drift can't stretch 1 h into 5.

**One regression-hunting fact I owe you:** F12 System-Off was last *proven* on the bench at **v0.23.5 (2026-10-28)**. The whole 0.24.x OTA era + 0.25.0 have shipped since without, I believe, a re-test of the 1 h path. So this may not be new — it may have been silently broken for two weeks. I'll bisect if needed.

**The 5-second diagnostic in your pocket:** when you reconnect the app after 19:15 (if the LED is still blinking), look at the **battery/charging indicator**. If it shows *charging / on-USB* while the device is on battery — `bq_on_vin` is stuck, case closed, and the fix is small (fail-safe default to false on read errors + observability). If it correctly shows *battery n%*, the mystery moves to the timer chain and I'll add printk markers on every re-arm branch so the next test prints exactly *why* it stayed awake.

Also worth saying: this test of yours just earned its keep — a device that never deep-sleeps after an interrupted sync is exactly the battery-drain failure we couldn't afford to discover on a ski day.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

content.text:
**Case closed on the blocker chain.** "Battery: unknown" is the smoking gun — walk it backwards:

`batt_cache = BATT_UNKNOWN` only happens on the failure paths of the battery read, and look at the `-4` (I²C error) branch of the poll:

```c
case -4:
    batt_cache = BATT_UNKNOWN;
    break;          /* ← bq_on_vin is NEVER updated here */
```

So: **the BQ25120A read is failing** → the app shows unknown → `bq_on_vin` is frozen at its **boot default of `true`** → the device believes it's on USB → the 1 h timer fires, sees "VIN", re-arms a full window → *every hour, forever*. That's your never-dark device. The design comment even acknowledges the danger ("the boot-time default is true") — it assumed the failure mode couldn't persist. It can.

Two things follow:

**1. One question only you can answer:** did the app show a real battery percentage *earlier today* (during the smoke test, or in past sessions)? 
- If **yes** → the I²C failure started between 13:15 and 18:10 — suspiciously correlated with the USB→battery transition.
- If it's been "unknown" all along → older regression, and the hunt widens.

**2. The diagnosis takes 10 seconds of USB:** plug back in, I capture serial — the poll prints `batt: BQ25120A I2C error` (I²C dead) versus `batt: BQ alive, faults=…` (battery-detect bit, i.e. the pack/UVLO story). That distinguishes the two failure modes.

**The fix is mine regardless, and it's small:** on read failure, stop trusting the frozen default — after N consecutive failed reads, treat the device as battery (fail-*safe*: the cost of wrongly going dark on a bench is trivial; the cost of never sleeping on a mountain is a dead device). Plus printk markers on every re-arm branch of `off_work_handler`, so the next time something defers System Off, the serial log says *why* instead of leaving us reading source for an hour.

Say the word when USB is back in and I'll grab the evidence.

assistantTexts:
**Case closed on the blocker chain.** "Battery: unknown" is the smoking gun — walk it backwards:

`batt_cache = BATT_UNKNOWN` only happens on the failure paths of the battery read, and look at the `-4` (I²C error) branch of the poll:

```c
case -4:
    batt_cache = BATT_UNKNOWN;
    break;          /* ← bq_on_vin is NEVER updated here */
```

So: **the BQ25120A read is failing** → the app shows unknown → `bq_on_vin` is frozen at its **boot default of `true`** → the device believes it's on USB → the 1 h timer fires, sees "VIN", re-arms a full window → *every hour, forever*. That's your never-dark device. The design comment even acknowledges the danger ("the boot-time default is true") — it assumed the failure mode couldn't persist. It can.

Two things follow:

**1. One question only you can answer:** did the app show a real battery percentage *earlier today* (during the smoke test, or in past sessions)? 
- If **yes** → the I²C failure started between 13:15 and 18:10 — suspiciously correlated with the USB→battery transition.
- If it's been "unknown" all along → older regression, and the hunt widens.

**2. The diagnosis takes 10 seconds of USB:** plug back in, I capture serial — the poll prints `batt: BQ25120A I2C error` (I²C dead) versus `batt: BQ alive, faults=…` (battery-detect bit, i.e. the pack/UVLO story). That distinguishes the two failure modes.

**The fix is mine regardless, and it's small:** on read failure, stop trusting the frozen default — after N consecutive failed reads, treat the device as battery (fail-*safe*: the cost of wrongly going dark on a bench is trivial; the cost of never sleeping on a mountain is a dead device). Plus printk markers on every re-arm branch of `off_work_handler`, so the next time something defers System Off, the serial log says *why* instead of leaving us reading source for an hour.

Say the word when USB is back in and I'll grab the evidence.

USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │

# bq25120A Low I Q Highly Integrated Battery Charge Management Solution for Wearables and IoT 

> 1

## 1 Features 

> 1

• Increases System Operation Time Between Charges – Configurable 300-mA Buck Regulator (1.8-V Default) – 700 nA (typical) Iq with Buck Converter Enabled (No Load) – Configurable Load Switch or 100mA LDO Output (Load Switch by Default) – Up to 300-mA Charge Current for Fast Charging – 0.5% Accurate Battery Voltage Regulation (Configurable from 3.6 V to 4.65 V in 10-mV Steps) – Configurable Termination Current Down to 500 μA – Simple Voltage Based Battery Monitor • Highly Integrated Solution with Small Footprint – 2.5 mm x 2.5 mm WCSP Package and 6 External Components for Minimal Solution – Push-Button Wake-Up and Reset with Adjustable Timers – Power Path Management for Powering the System and Charging the Battery – Power Path Management enables <50 nA Ship Mode Battery Quiescent Current for Longest Shelf Life – Battery Charger Operates from 3.4 V – 5.5 V IN 

(5.5-V OVP / 20-V Tolerant) – Dedicated Pins for Input Current Limit, Charge Current, Termination Current, and Status Output • I2C Communication Control – Charge Voltage and Current – Termination Threshold – Input Current Limit – VINDPM Threshold – Timer Options – Load Switch Control – Controls for Interrupts for Faults and Status – System Output Voltage Adjustment – LDO Output Voltage Adjustment 

## 2 Applications 

• Smart Watches and other Wearable Devices • Fitness Accessories • Health Monitoring Medical Accessories • Rechargeable Toys 

## 3 Description 

The bq25120A is a highly integrated battery charge management IC that integrates the most common functions for wearable devices: Linear charger, regulated output, load switch, manual reset with timer, and battery voltage monitor. The integrated buck converter is a high efficiency, low I Q switcher using DCS control that extends light load efficiency down to 10-μA load currents. The low quiescent current during operation and shutdown enables maximum battery life. The device supports charge currents from 5 mA to 300 mA. The input current limit, charge current, buck converter output voltage, LDO output voltage, and other parameters are programmable through the I 2C interface.

## 5 Description (continued) 

The battery is charged using a standard Li-Ion charge profile with three phases: precharge, constant current and constant voltage. A voltage-based JEITA compatible battery pack thermistor monitoring input (TS) is included that monitors battery temperature and automatically changes charge parameters to prevent the battery from charging outside of its safe temperature range. The charger is optimized for 5-V USB input, with 20-V tolerance to withstand line transients. The buck converter is run from the input or battery. When in battery only mode, the device can run from a battery up to 4.65 V. A configurable load switch allows system optimization by disconnecting infrequently used devices. The manual reset with timer allows mutliple different configuration options for wake are reset optimization.

## 7 Pin Configuration and Functions 

YFP Package 25-Pin DSBGA Top View 

Pin Functions 

PIN I/O DESCRIPTION NAME NO. 

IN A2 I DC Input Power Supply. IN is connected to the external DC supply. Bypass IN to GND with at least 1 μF of capacitance using a ceramic capacitor. PMID A3, B3 I/O High Side Bypass Connection. Connect at least 3μF of ceramic capacitance with DC bias derating from PMID to GND as close to the PMID and GND pins as possible. When entering Ship Mode, PMID is discharged by a 20-k Ω internal discharge resistor. GND A1, D5 Ground connection. Connect to the ground plane of the circuit. PGND A5 Power ground connection. Connect to the ground plane of the circuit. Connect the output filter cap from the buck converter to this ground as shown in the layout example. CD E2 IChip Disable. Drive CD low to place the part in High-Z mode with battery only present, or enable charging when V IN is valid. Drive CD high for Active Battery mode when battery only is present, and disable charge when V IN is present. CD is pulled low internally with 900 k Ω.SDA E4 I/O I2C Interface Data. Connect SDA to the logic rail through a 10-k Ω resistor. SCL E5 I I2C Interface Clock. Connect SCL to the logic rail through a 10-k Ω resistor. ILIM C2 IAdjustable Input Current Limit Programming. Connect a resistor from ILIM to GND to program the input current limit. The input current includes the system load and the battery charge current. Connect ILIM to GND to set the input current limit to the internal default threshold. ILIM can also be updated through I 2C. LSCTRL E3 I Load Switch and LDO Control Input. Pull high to enable the LS/LDO output, pull low to disable the LS/LDO output. ISET C1 IFast-Charge Current Programming Input. Connect a resistor from ISET to GND to program the fast-charge current level. Connect a resistor from ISET to GND to set the charge current to the internal default. ISET can also be updated through I 2C. While charging, the voltage at ISET reflects the actual charging current and can be used to monitor charge current if an ISET resistor is present and the device is not in host mode. 5

Pin Functions (continued) 

PIN I/O DESCRIPTION NAME NO. 

IPRETERM D1 ITermination current programming input. Connect a 0-Ω to 10-k Ω resistor from IPRETERM to GND to program the termination current between 5% and 20% of the charge current. The pre-charge current is the same as the termination current setting. Connect IPRETERM to GND to set the termination current to the internal default threshold. IPRETERM can also be updated through I 2C. INT D2 OStatus Output. INT is an open-drain output that signals charging status and fault interrupts. INT pulls low during charging. INT is high impedance when charging is complete, disabled, or the charger is in high impedance mode. When a fault occurs, a 128μs pulse is sent out as an interrupt for the host. INT charge indicator function is enabled/disabled using the EN_INT bit in the control register. Connect INT to a logic rail using an LED for visual indication of charge status or through a 100k Ω resistor to communicate with the host processor. PG D4 OOpen-drain Power Good status indication output. PG pulls to GND when V IN is above V (BAT) 

+ V SLP and less that V OVP . PG is high-impedance when the input power is not within specified limits. Connect PG to the desired logic voltage rail using a 1k Ω to 100k Ω resistor, or use with an LED for visual indication. PG can also be configured as a push-button voltage shifted output (MRS) in the registers, where the output of the PG pin reflects the status of the MR input, but pulled up to the desired logic voltage rail using a 1k Ω to 100k Ω resistor. RESET D3 OReset Output. RESET is an open drain active low output that goes low when MR is held low for longer than t RESET , which is configurable by the MRRESET registers. RESET is deasserted after the t RESET_D, typically 400ms. MR E1 IManual Reset Input. MR is a push-button input that must be held low for greater than t RESET 

to assert the reset output. If MR is pressed for a shorter period, there are two programmable timer events, t WAKE1 and t WAKE2 , that trigger an interrupt to the host. The MR input can also be used to bring the device out of Ship mode. SW A4 O Inductor Connection. Connect to the switched side of the external inductor. SYS B5 I System Voltage Sense Connection. Connect SYS to the system output at the output bulk capacitors. Bypass SYS locally with at least 4.7 μF of effective ceramic capacitance. LS/LDO C5 OLoad Switch or LDO output. Connect 1 μF of effective ceramic capacitance to this pin to assure stability. Be sure to account for capacitance bias voltage derating when selecting the capacitor. VINLS B4, C4 I Input to the Load Switch / LDO output. Connect 1 μF of effective ceramic capacitance from this pin to GND. BAT B1, B2 I/O Battery Connection. Connect to the positive terminal of the battery. Bypass BAT to GND with at least 1 μF of ceramic capacitance. TS C3 IBattery Pack NTC Monitor. Connect TS to the center tap of a resistor divider from VIN to GND. The NTC is connected from TS to GND. The TS function provides four thresholds for JEITA compatibility. TS faults are reported by the I 2C interface during charge mode. 6

## 7 Pin Configuration and Functions 

YFP Package 25-Pin DSBGA Top View 

Pin Functions 

PIN I/O DESCRIPTION NAME NO. 

IN A2 I DC Input Power Supply. IN is connected to the external DC supply. Bypass IN to GND with at least 1 μF of capacitance using a ceramic capacitor. PMID A3, B3 I/O High Side Bypass Connection. Connect at least 3μF of ceramic capacitance with DC bias derating from PMID to GND as close to the PMID and GND pins as possible. When entering Ship Mode, PMID is discharged by a 20-k Ω internal discharge resistor. GND A1, D5 Ground connection. Connect to the ground plane of the circuit. PGND A5 Power ground connection. Connect to the ground plane of the circuit. Connect the output filter cap from the buck converter to this ground as shown in the layout example. CD E2 IChip Disable. Drive CD low to place the part in High-Z mode with battery only present, or enable charging when V IN is valid. Drive CD high for Active Battery mode when battery only is present, and disable charge when V IN is present. CD is pulled low internally with 900 k Ω.SDA E4 I/O I2C Interface Data. Connect SDA to the logic rail through a 10-k Ω resistor. SCL E5 I I2C Interface Clock. Connect SCL to the logic rail through a 10-k Ω resistor. ILIM C2 IAdjustable Input Current Limit Programming. Connect a resistor from ILIM to GND to program the input current limit. The input current includes the system load and the battery charge current. Connect ILIM to GND to set the input current limit to the internal default threshold. ILIM can also be updated through I 2C. LSCTRL E3 I Load Switch and LDO Control Input. Pull high to enable the LS/LDO output, pull low to disable the LS/LDO output. ISET C1 IFast-Charge Current Programming Input. Connect a resistor from ISET to GND to program the fast-charge current level. Connect a resistor from ISET to GND to set the charge current to the internal default. ISET can also be updated through I 2C. While charging, the voltage at ISET reflects the actual charging current and can be used to monitor charge current if an ISET resistor is present and the device is not in host mode. 5

Pin Functions (continued) 

PIN I/O DESCRIPTION NAME NO. 

IPRETERM D1 ITermination current programming input. Connect a 0-Ω to 10-k Ω resistor from IPRETERM to GND to program the termination current between 5% and 20% of the charge current. The pre-charge current is the same as the termination current setting. Connect IPRETERM to GND to set the termination current to the internal default threshold. IPRETERM can also be updated through I 2C. INT D2 OStatus Output. INT is an open-drain output that signals charging status and fault interrupts. INT pulls low during charging. INT is high impedance when charging is complete, disabled, or the charger is in high impedance mode. When a fault occurs, a 128μs pulse is sent out as an interrupt for the host. INT charge indicator function is enabled/disabled using the EN_INT bit in the control register. Connect INT to a logic rail using an LED for visual indication of charge status or through a 100k Ω resistor to communicate with the host processor. PG D4 OOpen-drain Power Good status indication output. PG pulls to GND when V IN is above V (BAT) 

+ V SLP and less that V OVP . PG is high-impedance when the input power is not within specified limits. Connect PG to the desired logic voltage rail using a 1k Ω to 100k Ω resistor, or use with an LED for visual indication. PG can also be configured as a push-button voltage shifted output (MRS) in the registers, where the output of the PG pin reflects the status of the MR input, but pulled up to the desired logic voltage rail using a 1k Ω to 100k Ω resistor. RESET D3 OReset Output. RESET is an open drain active low output that goes low when MR is held low for longer than t RESET , which is configurable by the MRRESET registers. RESET is deasserted after the t RESET_D, typically 400ms. MR E1 IManual Reset Input. MR is a push-button input that must be held low for greater than t RESET 

to assert the reset output. If MR is pressed for a shorter period, there are two programmable timer events, t WAKE1 and t WAKE2 , that trigger an interrupt to the host. The MR input can also be used to bring the device out of Ship mode. SW A4 O Inductor Connection. Connect to the switched side of the external inductor. SYS B5 I System Voltage Sense Connection. Connect SYS to the system output at the output bulk capacitors. Bypass SYS locally with at least 4.7 μF of effective ceramic capacitance. LS/LDO C5 OLoad Switch or LDO output. Connect 1 μF of effective ceramic capacitance to this pin to assure stability. Be sure to account for capacitance bias voltage derating when selecting the capacitor. VINLS B4, C4 I Input to the Load Switch / LDO output. Connect 1 μF of effective ceramic capacitance from this pin to GND. BAT B1, B2 I/O Battery Connection. Connect to the positive terminal of the battery. Bypass BAT to GND with at least 1 μF of ceramic capacitance. TS C3 IBattery Pack NTC Monitor. Connect TS to the center tap of a resistor divider from VIN to GND. The NTC is connected from TS to GND. The TS function provides four thresholds for JEITA compatibility. TS faults are reported by the I 2C interface during charge mode. 6

9.3.5 Sleep Mode
The device enters the low-power sleep mode if the voltage IN falls below the sleep-mode entry threshold and VIN
is higher than the undervoltage lockout threshold. In sleep mode, the input is isolated from the connected battery.
This feature prevents draining the battery during the absence of VIN. When VIN < V(BAT) + VSLP, the device turns
the battery discharge FET on, sends a 128-µs pulse on the INT output, and the FAULT bits of the register are
update over I
2C. Once VIN > V(BAT) + VSLP, the device initiates a new charge cycle. The FAULT bits are not
cleared until they are read over I
2C and the sleep condition no longer exists. It is not recommended to do a
battery connection or plug in when VUVLO< VIN < VBAT + VSLP as it may cause higher quiescent current to be
drained form the battery.
9.3.6 Input Voltage Based Dynamic Power Management (VIN(DPM))
During the normal charging process, if the input power source is not able to support the programmed or default
charging current and System load, the supply voltage decreases. Once the supply approaches VIN(DPM), the input
DPM current and voltage loops will reduce the input current through the blocking FETs, to prevent the further
drop of the supply. The VIN(DPM) threshold is programmable through the I
2C register from 4.2 V to 4.9 V in 100-
mV steps. It can be disabled completely as well. When the device enters this mode, the charge current may be
lower than the set value and the VINDPM_STAT bit is set. If the 2X timer is set, the safety timer is extended
while VIN(DPM) is active. Additionally, termination is disabled. Note that in a condition where the battery is
connected while VUVLO<VIN < VIN(DPM), the VINDPM loop will prevent the battery from being charged and PMID
will be powered from BAT.

content.text: §9.3.5 + §9.3.7 give the mechanism: with USB out, **VIN is below UVLO → the BQ sets a UVLO fault bit** — our code treats that bit as "no battery" (`return -1`) *before* the line that updates the VIN oracle. On battery the function can never update `bq_on_vin`. One last grep for the exact bit names, then I write the fix:

args.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
txt = open('/tmp/bq.txt').read()
for kw in ('TIMER_FAULT', 'TS_FAULT', 'SYS_SHORT', 'BAT_UVLO ', 'VIN Poor', 'VINPOOR', '0x06'):
    for m in list(re.finditer(re.escape(kw), txt))[:2]:
        seg = re.sub(r'[ \t]+', ' ', txt[max(0,m.start()-150):m.start()+500])
        print('=====', kw, '=====')
        print(seg[:600]); break
EOF

High_Level_Requirements/system_design/sgc_system_design.md:209:Barometric temperature is NOT stored per-frame. High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_bom.md:85:- nRF52832 (ANNA-B112 module), BHI260AP, BMP390, BMM150, BME688 — already on Nicla. **Custom-board radio module: ANNA-B402** (nRF52833, decided 2026-09-10 — supersedes B112/B412 evaluations); add to the module line-item at the next BOM revision
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:34:P1 **standalone custom PCB** (first non-Nicla hardware spin), based on the **u-blox ANNA-B402** open-CPU module (nRF52833) per **AD-019** — no companion-carrier phase. The board is a **strict replica of the proven Nicla Sense ME sensor set** (BHI260AP + BMM150 + BMP390L + BME688 + dual MX25R flash + IS31FL3194 RGB + BQ25120A power) with the SGC deltas:
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:69:           ──► BHI260AP VDD/VDDIO + BMP390L + BME688 + BMM150 (Nicla cluster)
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:89:**Bus-map derivation (strict, per docs):** Zephyr `&i2c0` = P0.15/P0.16 = power-management bus ("Wire1" in Arduino naming) — gauge 0x36 (AD-029), LED 0x53, charger 0x6A. Zephyr `&i2c1` = P0.22/P0.23 = sensor bus ("Wire") — LDC1612 0x2A (ADDR=GND, DNP) + RV-3028 0x52 (DNP). BHI260AP is **SPI**, not I²C (app.overlay: `&spi2`, CS P0.31, 16 MHz, INT P0.14); BMP390/BMM150/BME688 are BHI260AP **sub-sensors on the BHI's M1 master port** (Nicla schematic — the task brief's "BMP390 I²C addr" does not apply; per the ABX00050 pinout, BMP390L rides BHI M1 with MCSB). Address map has no conflicts (AD-029 address table confirmed).
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:227:- **BMM150** (U4) + **BMP390L** (U3) + **BME688** (U6): sub-sensors on BHI260AP master port M1 (BMM150 SCK/SDI ← M1SCX/M1SDX; BMP390L via MCSB1; BME688 via MCSB2 per ABX00050 pinout). **Per-ball wiring = copy Nicla schematic verbatim at capture** — exact M1/M2/M3 pin assignment of the BHI cluster is a Nicla-internal net list; mark as "copy reference" in capture. BMP390L: 10-pin LGA (1 VDDIO, 2 SCK, 3 VSS, 4 SDI, 5 SDO, …, CSB; CSB→VDDIO selects I²C — here SPI to BHI).
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:228:- **BME688 populate-vs-DNP**: firmware never reads it → **OD-6** (footprint retained either way; Nicla parity = populate).

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

| 2 | CELL | GND ("MAX17048: Not internally connected") |
| 3 | VDD | **VBAT** ("MAX17048: Voltage sense input. Connect to positive battery terminal") + **0.1 µF** ("Bypass with 0.1 µF to GND") |
| 4 | GND | GND ("negative battery terminal") |
| 5 | ALRT | "Open-Drain, Active-Low Alert Output" → 10 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **P0.21** (module pin 26). Wired for firmware freedom; use v2-optional per AD-029 |
| 6 | QSTRT | GND ("Connect to GND if not used") |
| 7 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) — "I2C Clock Input" (fixed addr **0x36**, per ADI datasheet/AD-029) |
| 8 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |

**Note (OD-12):** verify MAX17048 VIH accepts 1.8 V pull-ups with VDD=VBAT (datasheet fetch was bot-blocked; pin table above is from the ADI datasheet text). BQ25120A VIH = 0.825 V and IS31FL3194 VIH ≤ 1.4 V are already 1.8 V-safe.

### 4.3 RGB LED (Nicla stock) + SK6812 strip (SGC)

**IS31FL3194-CLS2-TR (WLCSP-8)** + ROHM **SMLP34RGB2W3** LED (exact Nicla BOM, ABX00050 schematic U8/DL1):

| IS31 pin (datasheet Pin Description) | Connection |
|---|---|
| A1 SDB | "Shutdown the chip when pulled to low" → **V_PMID** (always-enabled; control via I²C) — Nicla SDB net **TBD-JP** (confirm on ABX00050 schematic at capture; do not guess) |
| A2 VCC | **V_PMID** (Nicla parity: U8 powered from PMID; IS31 VCC range 2.7–5.5 V covers 3.0–5.0 V battery/input) + 0.1 µF (value **TBD-JP** — typical-app figure is graphical; confirm vs Lumissil EVB/Nicla) |
| B1 SDA / C1 SCL | &i2c0 (P0.15/P0.16) — fixed 7-bit address **"101 0011" = 0x53**, no strap pins |
| B2/C2/D2 OUT1–OUT3 | SMLP34RGB2W3 R/G/B anodes (current-sink outputs; no resistors) |
| D1 GND | GND |

**SK6812-mini ×5** (SGC strip, P0.19): DIN ← P0.19 **through a 5 V-logic level translator** (boost rail is 5 V; SK6812 VIH ≈ 0.7·VDD — 1.8 V drive is insufficient). Dual-supply translator, VCCA=+1V8/VCCB=+5V, TXB0102/TXS0102-class — **part TBD-JP** (OD-9). Per-LED 0.1 µF; strip supply = +5V boost (hardware doc §7: full brightness for P1+).

### 4.4 Sensor cluster (Nicla replica — copy ABX00050 nets at capture)

- **BHI260AP** (44-pad LGA, 3.6×4.1×0.83 mm): HSCX pad 33 → P0.03 (SCK); HSDX pad 11 → P0.04 (MOSI); HSDO pad 32 → P0.05 (MISO); HCSB pad 34 → P0.31 (CS — "SPI mode"); HIRQ pad 10 → P0.14; **RESETN pad 9 → P0.13** (moved, C3; pad is "Input, Pull-Up, Reset input, active low"). VDD 1.71–3.6 V, **VDDIO 1.71–1.89 V** → both to +1V8 rail (this hard-pins the 1.8 V architecture — no 3.3 V sensor bus possible). Decoupling per Nicla bank: 1 µF + 100 nF ×3–4 (C5/C6/C7/C12/C13).
- **BMM150** (U4) + **BMP390L** (U3) + **BME688** (U6): sub-sensors on BHI260AP master port M1 (BMM150 SCK/SDI ← M1SCX/M1SDX; BMP390L via MCSB1; BME688 via MCSB2 per ABX00050 pinout). **Per-ball wiring = copy Nicla schematic verbatim at capture** — exact M1/M2/M3 pin assignment of the BHI cluster is a Nicla-internal net list; mark as "copy reference" in capture. BMP390L: 10-pin LGA (1 VDDIO, 2 SCK, 3 VSS, 4 SDI, 5 SDO, …, CSB; CSB→VDDIO selects I²C — here SPI to BHI).
- **BME688 populate-vs-DNP**: firmware never reads it → **OD-6** (footprint retained either way; Nicla parity = populate).
- **U2 "BHI Flash" MX25R1635FZUIH0** (Nicla U2, +1V8): BHI260AP QSPI (CLK/CS/D0–D3) — **⚠ missing from BOM v4.3** — BHY2 sensor firmware lives here (Arduino_BHY2 upload path). Must be added (OD-5).

|---|---|---|
| 1 | CS# | P0.26 (&spi2 hardware CS reg 0) |
| 2 | SO/SIO1 | P0.05 (MISO/CIPO) |

| 6 | SCLK | P0.03 |

| 8 | VCC | +1V8 + 100 nF |

RawRunStore 8 MB layout per hardware doc (pre-roll 0x0000–0x13FFF etc.) unchanged. U7 supply at +1V8 = Nicla parity (schematic shows U7 on +1V8).

- **LDC1612** (WSON-12): SCL 1 / SDA 2 / CLKIN 3 / ADDR 4 → GND (**0x2A**, "when ADDR=L, I2C address = 0x2A") / INTB 5 → BUTTON net P0.02 ("Push-pull output; does not require pull-up") / SD 6 → GND / VDD 7 (+100 nF) / GND 8 / IN0A 9, IN0B 10 (coil ch.0; 14 mm spiral, footprint retained) / IN1A 11, IN1B 12 → GND or 2nd coil pads. Sensor-bus (&i2c1) placement per docs.
- **RV-3028-C7 RTC @ 0x52** on &i2c1: 7-pin C7 footprint, /INT → TP (unconnected test point, no GPIO steal — per hardware doc §2 I²C map + TOOLS notes). Exact pad map per Micro Crystal datasheet at capture (DNP — not fetched this pass).

| USB-C pin(s) | Net |

| A4, A9, B4, B9 | VBUS → VBUS_USB: **10 µF bulk at connector** (sgc_usb_c_charging_spec §1) + ESD (OD-13: PESD5V0U2UT vs TPD4E05U06) → BQ IN (+1 µF at ball) |
| A1, A12, B1, B12 + SHELL | GND (shell stitched to GND; TH shell stakes soldered for pull-out strength) |

USB-IF note (BQ §9.3.13): inrush compliance assumes device input capacitance < 10 µF — our 10 µF bulk + 1 µF IN exceeds it → fine for our USB-A→C/legacy sourcing, note in quote package (OD-14).

### 4.8 Connectors & test points

- **Battery JST-3** (VBAT / GND / NTC): part **TBD-JP** — BOM v4.1 flags the connector provisional, varies with final cell pack. Pinout per ABX00050 pinout PDF (battery connector = VBAT/NTC/GND).
- **SWD**: SWDCLK (pin 41), SWDIO (pin 42), SWO (pin 16, optional), RESET_N (pin 12), VCC(+1V8) sense, GND. Style OD-2: Tag-Connect TC2050 footprint vs 2×5 1.27 mm Cortex Debug (EVK uses a 6-pin J-link needle adapter — either is defensible).
- **UART console TP**: TX P0.20 (module pin 10), RX P0.09 (module pin 22) — Nicla LPIO1/LPIO2 parity (ABX00050 pinout: "2/LPIO1/TX P0_20, 1/LPIO2/RX P0_09").
- **TP set** (OD-3): +1V8, +5V, VBAT, V_PMID, GND, BQ INT, SWD row, UART row, ALRT, LED-data.

### 4.9 Mechanical / antenna keepout (internal chip antenna; SIM UBX-21000517-R08 quotes)

- SIM Table 4 (p.13), internal antenna: pin 5 ANT_INT "Connect to pin 6 – ANT"; corner placement → pin 1 ANT_PCB = "GND pattern", ANT_GND1/2 NC; middle-of-side → pins 2+3 ANT_GND1/2 = "GND pattern", ANT_PCB NC. **Recommendation: module in a PCB corner** ("a corner location offers slightly better antenna performance", SIM §2.2.1).
- Keepout rule (SIM Appendix B, p.70, verbatim): "It is important not to route any traces in any layer in the antenna strip clearance area." — antenna strip = module edge + counterpoise region per SIM Figures 33–36; **no traces/vias in any layer** under/around the strip; counterpoise trace per the reference design.
- Certification caution (SIM App. B): "PCB layout must be identical to that provided by u-blox… The designer must use the stack-up provided by u-blox. RF traces on the carrier PCB are part of the certified design." → our 0.8 mm 4-layer stackup must be checked against the SIM reference stackup; if it differs, follow SIM App. B exactly or contact u-blox (flag in §8).
- Board outline: 22 × 55 mm, 4-layer, 0.8 mm, ENIG (hardware doc §9). BHI260AP antenna-adjacent and BMM150 keepouts (>10 mm from coil/RFID footprints) per hardware doc §9 table. SK6812 strip along top edge; button/LED face outward (§8).
- datasheet note: "The IC should be placed far away from the mobile antenna in order to prevent the EMI" (IS31FL3194 datasheet) — keep U8 clear of the module antenna strip.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

**Yes — solved, flashed, and verified live.** The banner confirms `v0.25.1` (commit `9e37d536`) running: sensors configured, your 38 runs + the three test runs you recorded this evening all intact, and the BQ reports clean on USB.

**The fix in one paragraph:** the VIN oracle (`bq_on_vin`) was only updated on the *success* path of the battery read. On battery, the BQ's FAULTS register reports VIN-undervoltage (bit 0x20 — your full pack with USB out *proved* it's VIN_UV, not "no battery" as the old comment claimed), the read returned `-1` early, the oracle froze at its boot default `true` — and the device believed "on USB" forever, re-arming the off-timer every hour. Your 5-hour blue blink was that loop running five times. Now: the oracle updates from the faults read alone before any early return, plus a fail-safe (3 dead I²C reads → assume battery), plus every deferral branch prints *why* (`off deferred: connected/busy/VIN`) — today's hour of source-diving becomes tomorrow's 5-second log read.

**The acceptance test is yours, same as before, now with the fix aboard:**
1. USB out, app closed
2. Wait the hour — the blue blink should **stop** (~System OFF)
3. One button press → cold boot (boot LED pattern, device re-advertises, app finds it fresh)

One caveat I owe you honestly: with USB out there's no serial, so on battery we won't see the `off deferred` markers — the LED stopping is the proof. But if it *still* blinks past 75 minutes, plug USB back in, tell me, and I'll read the deferral markers from the last boot cycle — the observability is there for exactly that case.

And a nice detail from the log: your three evening presses recorded as runs (144 B, 5.1 KB, 21.9 KB) — the piezo arming is earning its keep.

High_Level_Requirements/sgc_requirements.md:131:| **H01** | Operating temperature range | −20°C to +40°C |

High_Level_Requirements/system_design/sgc_system_design.md:209:Barometric temperature is NOT stored per-frame. It is sampled once at run start and written to the run file header (queryable via BLE GATT). Temperature changes slowly — per-frame storage would waste ~12 KB per 2-min run for negligible value.
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_bom.md:85:- nRF52832 (ANNA-B112 module), BHI260AP, BMP390, BMM150, BME688 — already on Nicla. **Custom-board radio module: ANNA-B402** (nRF52833, decided 2026-09-10 — supersedes B112/B412 evaluations); add to the module line-item at the next BOM revision
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:34:P1 **standalone custom PCB** (first non-Nicla hardware spin), based on the **u-blox ANNA-B402** open-CPU module (nRF52833) per **AD-019** — no companion-carrier phase. The board is a **strict replica of the proven Nicla Sense ME sensor set** (BHI260AP + BMM150 + BMP390L + BME688 + dual MX25R flash + IS31FL3194 RGB + BQ25120A power) with the SGC deltas:
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:69:           ──► BHI260AP VDD/VDDIO + BMP390L + BME688 + BMM150 (Nicla cluster)
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:89:**Bus-map derivation (strict, per docs):** Zephyr `&i2c0` = P0.15/P0.16 = power-management bus ("Wire1" in Arduino naming) — gauge 0x36 (AD-029), LED 0x53, charger 0x6A. Zephyr `&i2c1` = P0.22/P0.23 = sensor bus ("Wire") — LDC1612 0x2A (ADDR=GND, DNP) + RV-3028 0x52 (DNP). BHI260AP is **SPI**, not I²C (app.overlay: `&spi2`, CS P0.31, 16 MHz, INT P0.14); BMP390/BMM150/BME688 are BHI260AP **sub-sensors on the BHI's M1 master port** (Nicla schematic — the task brief's "BMP390 I²C addr" does not apply; per the ABX00050 pinout, BMP390L rides BHI M1 with MCSB). Address map has no conflicts (AD-029 address table confirmed).
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:227:- **BMM150** (U4) + **BMP390L** (U3) + **BME688** (U6): sub-sensors on BHI260AP master port M1 (BMM150 SCK/SDI ← M1SCX/M1SDX; BMP390L via MCSB1; BME688 via MCSB2 per ABX00050 pinout). **Per-ball wiring = copy Nicla schematic verbatim at capture** — exact M1/M2/M3 pin assignment of the BHI cluster is a Nicla-internal net list; mark as "copy reference" in capture. BMP390L: 10-pin LGA (1 VDDIO, 2 SCK, 3 VSS, 4 SDI, 5 SDO, …, CSB; CSB→VDDIO selects I²C — here SPI to BHI).
High_Level_Requirements/system_design/architecture_modules/sgc_schematic_spec.md:228:- **BME688 populate-vs-DNP**: firmware never reads it → **OD-6** (footprint retained either way; Nicla parity = populate).

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

### 4.4 Sensor cluster (Nicla replica — copy ABX00050 nets at capture)

- **BHI260AP** (44-pad LGA, 3.6×4.1×0.83 mm): HSCX pad 33 → P0.03 (SCK); HSDX pad 11 → P0.04 (MOSI); HSDO pad 32 → P0.05 (MISO); HCSB pad 34 → P0.31 (CS — "SPI mode"); HIRQ pad 10 → P0.14; **RESETN pad 9 → P0.13** (moved, C3; pad is "Input, Pull-Up, Reset input, active low"). VDD 1.71–3.6 V, **VDDIO 1.71–1.89 V** → both to +1V8 rail (this hard-pins the 1.8 V architecture — no 3.3 V sensor bus possible). Decoupling per Nicla bank: 1 µF + 100 nF ×3–4 (C5/C6/C7/C12/C13).
- **BMM150** (U4) + **BMP390L** (U3) + **BME688** (U6): sub-sensors on BHI260AP master port M1 (BMM150 SCK/SDI ← M1SCX/M1SDX; BMP390L via MCSB1; BME688 via MCSB2 per ABX00050 pinout). **Per-ball wiring = copy Nicla schematic verbatim at capture** — exact M1/M2/M3 pin assignment of the BHI cluster is a Nicla-internal net list; mark as "copy reference" in capture. BMP390L: 10-pin LGA (1 VDDIO, 2 SCK, 3 VSS, 4 SDI, 5 SDO, …, CSB; CSB→VDDIO selects I²C — here SPI to BHI).
- **BME688 populate-vs-DNP**: firmware never reads it → **OD-6** (footprint retained either way; Nicla parity = populate).
- **U2 "BHI Flash" MX25R1635FZUIH0** (Nicla U2, +1V8): BHI260AP QSPI (CLK/CS/D0–D3) — **⚠ missing from BOM v4.3** — BHY2 sensor firmware lives here (Arduino_BHY2 upload path). Must be added (OD-5).

| Pin | Name | Net |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CS# | P0.26 (&spi2 hardware CS reg 0) |
| 2 | SO/SIO1 | P0.05 (MISO/CIPO) |
| 3 | WP#/SIO2 | NC (datasheet Note 1: "will remain internal pull up function while this pin is not physically connected") |
| 4 | GND | GND |
| 5 | SI/SIO0 | P0.04 (MOSI/COPI) |
| 6 | SCLK | P0.03 |
| 7 | RESET#/SIO3 or HOLD#/SIO3 | NC (same internal-pull-up note) |
| 8 | VCC | +1V8 + 100 nF |

RawRunStore 8 MB layout per hardware doc (pre-roll 0x0000–0x13FFF etc.) unchanged. U7 supply at +1V8 = Nicla parity (schematic shows U7 on +1V8).

### 4.6 DNP footprints (v2)

- **LDC1612** (WSON-12): SCL 1 / SDA 2 / CLKIN 3 / ADDR 4 → GND (**0x2A**, "when ADDR=L, I2C address = 0x2A") / INTB 5 → BUTTON net P0.02 ("Push-pull output; does not require pull-up") / SD 6 → GND / VDD 7 (+100 nF) / GND 8 / IN0A 9, IN0B 10 (coil ch.0; 14 mm spiral, footprint retained) / IN1A 11, IN1B 12 → GND or 2nd coil pads. Sensor-bus (&i2c1) placement per docs.
- **RV-3028-C7 RTC @ 0x52** on &i2c1: 7-pin C7 footprint, /INT → TP (unconnected test point, no GPIO steal — per hardware doc §2 I²C map + TOOLS notes). Exact pad map per Micro Crystal datasheet at capture (DNP — not fetched this pass).
- Beeper BZ1 (DNP): P0.09 via 100 Ω/NPN footprint retained.

USB-IF note (BQ §9.3.13): inrush compliance assumes device input capacitance < 10 µF — our 10 µF bulk + 1 µF IN exceeds it → fine for our USB-A→C/legacy sourcing, note in quote package (OD-14).

- **Battery JST-3** (VBAT / GND / NTC): part **TBD-JP** — BOM v4.1 flags the connector provisional, varies with final cell pack. Pinout per ABX00050 pinout PDF (battery connector = VBAT/NTC/GND).

- **UART console TP**: TX P0.20 (module pin 10), RX P0.09 (module pin 22) — Nicla LPIO1/LPIO2 parity (ABX00050 pinout: "2/LPIO1/TX P0_20, 1/LPIO2/RX P0_09").

### 4.9 Mechanical / antenna keepout (internal chip antenna; SIM UBX-21000517-R08 quotes)

- SIM Table 4 (p.13), internal antenna: pin 5 ANT_INT "Connect to pin 6 – ANT"; corner placement → pin 1 ANT_PCB = "GND pattern", ANT_GND1/2 NC; middle-of-side → pins 2+3 ANT_GND1/2 = "GND pattern", ANT_PCB NC. **Recommendation: module in a PCB corner** ("a corner location offers slightly better antenna performance", SIM §2.2.1).
- Keepout rule (SIM Appendix B, p.70, verbatim): "It is important not to route any traces in any layer in the antenna strip clearance area." — antenna strip = module edge + counterpoise region per SIM Figures 33–36; **no traces/vias in any layer** under/around the strip; counterpoise trace per the reference design.
- Certification caution (SIM App. B): "PCB layout must be identical to that provided by u-blox… The designer must use the stack-up provided by u-blox. RF traces on the carrier PCB are part of the certified design." → our 0.8 mm 4-layer stackup must be checked against the SIM reference stackup; if it differs, follow SIM App. B exactly or contact u-blox (flag in §8).
- Board outline: 22 × 55 mm, 4-layer, 0.8 mm, ENIG (hardware doc §9). BHI260AP antenna-adjacent and BMM150 keepouts (>10 mm from coil/RFID footprints) per hardware doc §9 table. SK6812 strip along top edge; button/LED face outward (§8).

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

Both reviews are in, cross-checked, and the disagreements resolved. Here's the synthesized verdict:

## The two reviews agree on 2 defects — and I arbitrated the third

**DS pass verdict (independent parser, 351 pins, own transform): 301 OK + 45 NC OK, and it found the two detach clusters with better forensics than my gate:**

1. **`U3.B1` (VBAT) floating** — the smoking gun: a stranded `VBAT` global label sits exactly 5.08 mm away at the position where *every other* BQ pin has its stub. The **wire is missing** — redraw one 5 mm stub from pin to the stranded label.
2. **`BUTTON_RAW` label lost** — but crucially, DS found the **wires are intact**: J5.1, R41.1, D6.2, D7.2 are still correctly wired together as one node. Only the *name* vanished (zero occurrences in all 7 sheets). Fix = **one global label** on that node. Much cheaper than my gate suggested.

**Where they disagreed, my gate was right:** DS reported "0 wrong-nets, 0 shorts" in the ANNA zone — but I re-checked the raw file: at (199.39, 120.65) a label genuinely sits **on a foreign net's wire**, and KiCad *does* connect mid-wire labels — that's a real +1V8↔UART_TX_TP↔GND short chain on `U1.9`/`U1.10`. Practical advice for that zone: it's tangled — delete the wires/labels in that small area and redraw the two stubs clean rather than nudging.

**Plus my fourth finding stands:** `C17.2` (GND) endpoint lands mid-span inside a `SWO` wire — move that endpoint off.

DS went ball-for-ball: **BHI260AP M-ports, BME688, BMP390, BMM150, Y1, ANNA — exact parity** on every pad that matters. And the two flags it raised both resolve in our favor:
- **HOSTBOOT direction**: I checked the ABX extraction — Nicla's R23 also pulls **down to GND**. Our R13 is exact parity, no change needed.

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

| D3 | RESET | NC (BQ's MR-reset output unused on P1 — Nicla's "P0.18→MR" net dropped, see C3) |

| Pin | Name | Connection |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CTG | GND ("Connect to Ground") |

| 3 | VDD | **VBAT** ("MAX17048: Voltage sense input. Connect to positive battery terminal") + **0.1 µF** ("Bypass with 0.1 µF to GND") |

| 7 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) — "I2C Clock Input" (fixed addr **0x36**, per ADI datasheet/AD-029) |
| 8 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| EP | — | GND |

| B1 SDA / C1 SCL | &i2c0 (P0.15/P0.16) — fixed 7-bit address **"101 0011" = 0x53**, no strap pins |
| B2/C2/D2 OUT1–OUT3 | SMLP34RGB2W3 R/G/B anodes (current-sink outputs; no resistors) |
| D1 GND | GND |

   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │

### 3.3 Conflicts, risks, firmware impact

| ID | Finding | Resolution in this spec | FW impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | **P0.24 absent** — hardware doc §10 assigns Boost EN = P0.24 (v1) / RFID_EN = P0.24 (v2) | Boost EN → **P0.17** (module pin 49). v2 RFID_EN → P0.17 likewise (or P0.06/P0.12) | `boost_en` pin change in config/overlay |
| C2 | **P0.25 absent** — hardware doc §2 assigns BQ CD = P0.25 | CD → **P0.08** (module pin 50) + 100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID so the board always boots active (CD low + battery-only = BQ Hi-Z ship mode = dead board). See OD-8 | `bq_cd` pin change |
| C3 | **Module RESET_N = P0.18** (fixed) vs Nicla's BHI260AP RESET on P0.18 (app.overlay pulses it low at bring-up; hardware doc §2 "P0.18 → BQ25120 MR reset network") | BHI RESETN → **P0.13** (module pin 52), pull-up retained. Do **not** wire anything external to pin 12 except SWD/TP. (The Nicla's "P0.18 → BQ MR" net is dropped — MR unused on P1, see §4.1) | overlay: BHI reset-gpios 18 → 13 |
| R1 | P0.03 (SPI SCK) carries Table 4 remark "standard drive, low-frequency I/O only… avoid using these pins for high-speed digital interfaces… Digital noise on these pins can reduce radio sensitivity" — vs app.overlay's 16 MHz BHI SPI | Keep Nicla-parity routing (function locked to the proven design); mitigation documented: if RF sensitivity regressions appear in bench S03/S04, drop SPI clock (BHI works at 8/4 MHz) and re-test. Decision point at EMC/range bench — JP informed | optional `spi-max-frequency` reduction |
| R2 | P0.19 (SK6812 data, 800 kHz NZR) carries the same "low frequency I/O only" remark | Same treatment as R1; the strip is 3 mm from the antenna zone — also see §4.9 keepout. Fallback alternative: move strip to a full-drive GPIO (P0.06/P0.12) with zero Nicla-parity loss (SK6812 is an SGC peripheral, not a Nicla part) — JP call (OD-9b) | overlay pin change if moved |
| C4 | Nicla's VDDIO_EXT header rail (BQ LS/LDO, programmable 1.8–3.3 V per ABX00050 pinout) has **no consumer on P1** (no external header, no level translators) | LS/LDO unused: LSCTRL → GND (disabled), LS/LDO pin → 1 µF to GND (stability, §7 pin table), VINLS → SYS (per SLUSD08A §9.3: "If the output of the LDO is less than the programmed V(SYS) voltage, connect VINLS to SYS") | none |

---

## 4. Per-subsystem net lists

### 4.1 Charger subsystem — BQ25120A (YFP 25-ball DSBGA; ball map verbatim from SLUSD08A §7)

| Ball | Name | Net / connection |
|---|---|---|
| A2 | IN | VBUS_USB (USB-C VBUS) + **C_IN 1 µF** ("Bypass IN to GND with at least 1 µF") |
| A3, B3 | PMID | V_PMID + **C_PMID ≥3 µF** ("at least 3 µF… as close as possible"; Nicla uses 4.7 µF C10) → IS31FL3194 VCC, CD pull-up rail |
| A1, D5 | GND | GND |
| A5 | PGND | GND (buck hot loop; output cap to this ground per §7) |
| A4 | SW | L1 **2.2 µH** (Nicla: MLZ1608A2R2WT000) → PGND side; SYS sense |
| B5 | SYS | **+1V8 rail** + **C_SYS ≥4.7 µF** (Nicla: C15 10 µF) — buck default **1.8 V** (SYS_VOUT "1.8 V through 3.3 V selection", default per §7 table "BQ25120A Enabled 1.8 V Load Switch") |
| B1, B2 | BAT | VBAT (cell +) + **C_BAT ≥1 µF** |
| C3 | TS | NTC net: **R_HI from VBUS/driver to TS**, **R_LO TS→GND**, pack NTC (TS→GND) per Fig. 18 + Eq. 1–2. R_HI/R_LO values **TBD-JP** (need Renata NTC R25/B constants; JEITA thresholds V(COLD/COOL/WARM/HOT) per datasheet) |
| C1 | ISET | **R_ISET = 1.82 kΩ 1%** → ICHG = K(ISET)/R(ISET) = 200/1820 ≈ **110 mA** (Table 5, KISET typ 200 AΩ; task-given 110 mA) |
| C2 | ILIM | **R_ILIM = 1.0 kΩ 1%** → 200 mA (Table 4 row "0.19/0.2/0.21 A — 1000 Ω") |
| D1 | IPRETERM | **4.99 kΩ** → termination/pre-charge = 10 % of ISET ≈ 11 mA (Table 3 row 10 % → 4990 Ω) |
| D2 | INT | open-drain status → 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **NC on MCU** (charging bit read from FAULTS reg over I²C, per AD-029 firmware note); TP |
| D3 | RESET | NC (BQ's MR-reset output unused on P1 — Nicla's "P0.18→MR" net dropped, see C3) |
| D4 | /PG | TP only (optional 100 kΩ pull-up to +1V8) |
| E1 | /MR | NC (internal logic handles; ship mode via I²C/CD per OD-8 decision) |
| E2 | /CD | **P0.08** (module pin 50) + **100 kΩ pull-up to V_PMID** — pull-up guarantees active mode at cold boot (CD has internal 900 kΩ pull-down; CD low + battery-only = Hi-Z). OD-8 |
| E3 | LSCTRL | GND (LS/LDO disabled — no consumer, C4) |
| E4 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| E5 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) |
| C4, B4 | VINLS | → SYS (rule §9.3 quoted in C4) + 1 µF |
| C5 | LS/LDO | 1 µF to GND, otherwise NC |

VBATREG note: default register = **4.2 V** (§7 table "4.2 V" battery-regulation default; VBREG equation "VBATREG = 3.6 V + VBREGCODE × 10 mV", charge range 3.6–4.65 V) — correct for the cell; no divider/resistor needed.

### 4.2 Fuel gauge — MAX17048G+T10 (TDFN-8; pin functions verbatim from ADI datasheet Pin Description table)

| Pin | Name | Connection |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CTG | GND ("Connect to Ground") |
| 2 | CELL | GND ("MAX17048: Not internally connected") |
| 3 | VDD | **VBAT** ("MAX17048: Voltage sense input. Connect to positive battery terminal") + **0.1 µF** ("Bypass with 0.1 µF to GND") |
| 4 | GND | GND ("negative battery terminal") |
| 5 | ALRT | "Open-Drain, Active-Low Alert Output" → 10 kΩ pull-up to +1V8 → **P0.21** (module pin 26). Wired for firmware freedom; use v2-optional per AD-029 |
| 6 | QSTRT | GND ("Connect to GND if not used") |
| 7 | SCL | &i2c0 SCL (P0.16) — "I2C Clock Input" (fixed addr **0x36**, per ADI datasheet/AD-029) |
| 8 | SDA | &i2c0 SDA (P0.15) |
| EP | — | GND |

**Note (OD-12):** verify MAX17048 VIH accepts 1.8 V pull-ups with VDD=VBAT (datasheet fetch was bot-blocked; pin table above is from the ADI datasheet text). BQ25120A VIH = 0.825 V and IS31FL3194 VIH ≤ 1.4 V are already 1.8 V-safe.

### 4.3 RGB LED (Nicla stock) + SK6812 strip (SGC)

**IS31FL3194-CLS2-TR (WLCSP-8)** + ROHM **SMLP34RGB2W3** LED (exact Nicla BOM, ABX00050 schematic U8/DL1):

| IS31 pin (datasheet Pin Description) | Connection |
|---|---|
| A1 SDB | "Shutdown the chip when pulled to low" → **V_PMID** (always-enabled; control via I²C) — Nicla SDB net **TBD-JP** (confirm on ABX00050 schematic at capture; do not guess) |
| A2 VCC | **V_PMID** (Nicla parity: U8 powered from PMID; IS31 VCC range 2.7–5.5 V covers 3.0–5.0 V battery/input) + 0.1 µF (value **TBD-JP** — typical-app figure is graphical; confirm vs Lumissil EVB/Nicla) |
| B1 SDA / C1 SCL | &i2c0 (P0.15/P0.16) — fixed 7-bit address **"101 0011" = 0x53**, no strap pins |
| B2/C2/D2 OUT1–OUT3 | SMLP34RGB2W3 R/G/B anodes (current-sink outputs; no resistors) |
| D1 GND | GND |

**SK6812-mini ×5** (SGC strip, P0.19): DIN ← P0.19 **through a 5 V-logic level translator** (boost rail is 5 V; SK6812 VIH ≈ 0.7·VDD — 1.8 V drive is insufficient). Dual-supply translator, VCCA=+1V8/VCCB=+5V, TXB0102/TXS0102-class — **part TBD-JP** (OD-9). Per-LED 0.1 µF; strip supply = +5V boost (hardware doc §7: full brightness for P1+).

### 4.4 Sensor cluster (Nicla replica — copy ABX00050 nets at capture)

## 5. Power tree with currents

```
USB-C 5 V ──IN── BQ25120A ──BAT── Renata 600 mAh (3.7 V, NTC 3-wire, JST-3)
   │               │  │ILIM 200 mA      │
   │               │  └ ICHG 110 mA     ├─► MAX17048 VDD (3 µA hibernate typ — AD-029)
   │               │                    └─► (nothing else on VBAT)
   │               ├─PMID──► IS31FL3194 VCC (≤ 3×10 mA LED band, I2C-set)
   │               └─SYS = +1V8 (300 mA buck max) ──► B402 VCC (module DC/DC int.)
   │                                            ──► BHI cluster + U2 + U7 (≤ ~15 mA active)
   │                                            ──► I²C pull-ups, Y1 osc
   └─(via boost, battery-side) MT3608 ── +5V ──► SK6812 ×5 (anim ~8–15 mA; 60 mA worst)
```

- System peaks: BLE TX peak handled by B402's internal DC/DC (datasheet §2.1.1: integrated step-down; battery must handle module peak per SIM §3.4.1); BQ buck 300 mA ceiling ≫ our ~25 mA ARMED/LOGGING budget (hardware doc §7 power table).
- Charge + system simultaneously: 110 mA (ICHG) + ~25 mA (system) + LEDs ~15 mA @5V→~23 mA battery-side ≈ 158 mA < ILIM 200 mA ✓ (with USB present the buck loads are served from VIN via power path, per BQ §9.3 DPPM description).
- Session budget unchanged from hardware doc §7 (~48 mAh/session → ~12.5 sessions @ 20 °C; gauge adds ~3 µA — AD-029).
- Battery capacity: docs say **Renata ICP622540PMT, 600 mAh** (sgc_system_design §746, hardware doc §7) — the task brief's "550 mAh" figure appears nowhere in the repo; **confirm OD-4**.

Fix: flip D7 (A=GND, K=BUTTON_RAW). Values answer: both clamps are **BAT42WS** SOD-323 (30 V/0.35 A Schottky) — fine for −40…85 °C; R41 100 k + dual-rail clamp is adequate ESD/ring protection once flipped (note: 100 k vs ~13 k internal pull-up attenuates ~8:1 — detectable, but keep firmware thresholds generous).

**2. R14 BHI_HIRQ 10 k→+1V8 — CORRECT (harmless, keep).**
